### cpwd_admin monitor_list

##### Description

Prints the status of actively monitored processes on the screen.

See the explanation about the active monitoring in "cpwd_admin" on page 202.

##### Syntax

cpwd_admin monitor_list

##### Example

[Expert@HostName:0]# cpwd_admin monitor_list cpwd_admin: APP FILE_NAME NO_MSG_TIMES LAST_MSG_TIME CPD CPD_5420_4714.mntr 0/10 [19:00:33] 31/5/2019 [Expert@HostName:0]#


### cpwd_admin start

##### Description

Starts a process as monitored by the WatchDog.

##### Syntax on a Management Server

cpwd_admin start -name < _Application Name_ > -path "< _Full Path to Executable_ >" -command "< _Command Syntax_ >" [-env {inherit | < _Env_ Var_ >=< _Value_ >] [-slp_timeout < _Timeout_ >] [-retry_limit {< _Limit_ > | u}]

##### Syntax on a Security Gateway

cpwd_admin start -name < _Application Name_ > [-ctx < _VSID_ >] -path "< _Full Path to Executable_ >" -command "< _Command Syntax_ >" [-env {inherit | < _Env_Var_ >=< _Value_ >] [-slp_timeout < _Timeout_ >] [-retry_ limit {< _Limit_ > | u}]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-name<br><_Application_|Name, under which thecpwd_admin listcommand shows<br>the monitored process in the leftmost columnAPP.|
|_Name_>|Examples:|
||n FWM|
||n FWD|
||n CPD|
||n CPM|
|-ctx <_VSID_>|On a VSX Gateway, specifies the context of the applicable<br>Virtual System.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-path "<_Full Path_<br>_to Executable_>"|The full path (with or without Check Point environment variables)<br>to the executable including the executable name.<br>Must enclose in double quotes.<br>Examples:<br>n For FWM: "$FWDIR/bin/fwm"<br>n For FWD: "/opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/bin/fw"<br>n For CPD: "$CPDIR/bin/cpd"<br>n For CPM: "/opt/CPsuite-<br>R81/fw1/scripts/cpm.sh"<br>n For SICTUNNEL: "/opt/CPshrd-R81/bin/cptnl"|
|-command<br>"<_Command_<br>_Syntax_>"|The command and its arguments to run.<br>Must enclose in double quotes.<br>Examples:<br>n For FWM: "fwm"<br>n For FWM on Multi-Domain Server: "fwm mds"<br>n For FWD: "fwd"<br>n For CPD: "cpd"<br>n For CPM: "/opt/CPsuite-<br>R81/fw1/scripts/cpm.sh -s"<br>n For SICTUNNEL: "/opt/CPshrd-R81/bin/cptnl -c<br>"/opt/CPuepm-R81/engine/conf/cptnl_<br>srv.conf""|
|-env {inherit |<br><_Env__<br>_Var_>=<_Value_>}|Configures whether to inherit the environment variables from the<br>shell.<br>n inherit- Inherits all the environment variables<br>(WatchDog supports up to 80 environment variables)<br>n <_Env_Var_>=<_Value_>- Assigns the specified value to the<br>specified environment variable|
|-slp_timeout<br><_Timeout_>|Configures the specified value of the "sleep_timeout"<br>configuration parameter.<br>See"cpwd_admin config" on page 205.|
|-retry_limit<br>{<_Limit_> | u}|Configures the value of the "retry_limit" configuration<br>parameter.<br>See"cpwd_admin config" on page 205.<br>n <_Limit_>- Tries to restart the process the specified<br>number of times<br>n u- Tries to restart the process unlimited number of times|


##### Example

For the list of process and the applicable syntax, see <u>sk97638.</u>


### cpwd_admin start_monitor

##### Description

Starts the active WatchDog monitoring. WatchDog monitors the predefined processes actively.

See the explanation for the "cpwd_admin" on page 202 command.

##### Syntax

cpwd_admin start_monitor

##### Example

[Expert@HostName:0]# cpwd_admin start_monitor cpwd_admin:

CPWD has started to perform active monitoring on Check Point services/processes [Expert@HostName:0]#


### cpwd_admin stop

##### Description

Stops a WatchDog monitored process.


Important - This change does not survive reboot.

##### Syntax on a Management Server

cpwd_admin stop -name < _Application Name_ > [-path "< _Full Path to Executable_ >" -command "< _Command Syntax_ >" [-env {inherit | < _Env_ Var_ >=< _Value_ >]

##### Syntax on a Security Gateway

cpwd_admin stop -name < _Application Name_ > [-ctx < _VSID_ >] [-path "< _Full Path to Executable_ >" -command "< _Command Syntax_ >" [-env {inherit | < _Env_Var_ >=< _Value_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-name <_Application_<br>_Name_>|Name under which thecpwd_admin listcommand shows<br>the monitored process in the leftmost columnAPP.<br>Examples:<br>n FWM<br>n FWD<br>n CPD<br>n CPM|
|-ctx <_VSID_>|On a VSX Gateway, specifies the context of the applicable<br>Virtual System.|
|-path "<_Full Path_<br>_to Executable_>"|The full path (with or without Check Point environment<br>variables) to the executable including the executable name.<br>Must enclose in double quotes.<br>Examples:|
||n For FWM: "$FWDIR/bin/fwm"<br>n For FWD: "/opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/bin/fw"<br>n For CPD: "$CPDIR/bin/cpd_admin"|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-command "<_Command_<br>_Syntax_>"|The command and its arguments to run.<br>Must enclose in double quotes.<br>Examples:|
||n For FWM: "fw kill fwm"<br>n For FWD: "fw kill fwd"<br>n For CPD: "cpd_admin stop"|
|-env {inherit |<br><_Env_Var_>=<_Value_>}|Configures whether to inherit the environment variables from<br>the shell.|
||n inherit- Inherits all the environment variables<br>(WatchDog supports up to 80 environment variables)<br>n <_Env_Var_>=<_Value_>- Assigns the specified value to<br>the specified environment variable|


##### Example

For the list of process and the applicable syntax, see <u>sk97638.</u>


### cpwd_admin stop_monitor

##### Description

Stops the active WatchDog monitoring. WatchDog monitors all processes only passively. See the explanation for the "cpwd_admin" on page 202 command.

##### Syntax

cpwd_admin stop_monitor

##### Example

[Expert@HostName:0]# cpwd_admin stop_monitor cpwd_admin:

CPWD has stopped performing active monitoring on Check Point services/processes [Expert@HostName:0]#


## dbedit

##### Description

Edits the management database - the $FWDIR/conf/objects_5_0.C file - on the Security Management Server or Domain Management Server. See <u>skI3301.</u>


Important - Do NOT run this command, unless explicitly instructed by Check Point Support or R&D to do so. Otherwise, you can corrupt settings in the management database.

##### Syntax

dbedit -help dbedit [-globallock] [{-local | -s < _Management_Server_ >}] [{-u < _Username_ > | -c < _Certificate_ >}] [-p < _Password_ >] [-f < _File_Name_ > [ignore_script_failure] [-continue_updating]] [-r "< _Open_Reason_ Text_ >"] [-d < _Database_Name_ >] [-listen] [-readonly] [-session] Note: On a Multi-Domain Server, you must run this command in the context of the applicable Domain Management Server: mdsenv < _IP Address or Name of Domain Management Server_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-help|Prints the general help.|
|-globallock|When you work with the dbedit utility, it partially locks the management<br>database. If a user configures objects in SmartConsole at the same<br>time, it causes problems in the management database.<br>This option does not let SmartConsole, or a dbedit user to make<br>changes in the management database.<br>When you specify this option, the dbedit commands run on a copy of<br>the management database. After you make the changes with the<br>dbeditcommands and run thesavedbcommand, the dbedit utility<br>saves and commits your changes to the actual management database.|
|-local|Connects to the localhost (127.0.0.1) without using<br>username/password.<br>If you do not specify this parameter, the dbedit utility asks how to<br>connect.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-s<br><_Management__<br>_Server_>|Specifies the Security Management Server - by IP address or<br>HostName.<br>If you do not specify this parameter, the dbedit utility asks how to<br>connect.|
|-u<br><_Username_>|Specifies the username, with which the dbedit utility connects to the<br>Security Management Server.<br>Mandatory parameter when you specify the "-s <_Management__<br>_Server_>" parameter.|
|-c<br><<br>_Certificate_>|Specifies the user's certificate file, with which the dbedit utility connects<br>to the Security Management Server.<br>Mandatory parameter when you specify the "-s <_Management__<br>_Server_>" parameter.|
|-p<br><_Password_>|Specifies the user's password, with which the dbedit utility connects to<br>the Security Management Server.<br>Mandatory parameter when you specify the "-s <_Management__<br>_Server_>" and "-u <_Username_>" parameters.|
|-f <_File__<br>_Name_>|Specifies the file that contains the applicable dbedit internal commands<br>(see the section "dbedit Internal Commands" below):<br>n create <_object_type_> <_object_name_><br>n modify <_table_name_> <_object_name_> <_field_name_><br><_value_><br>n update <_table_name_> <_object_name_><br>n delete <_table_name_> <_object_name_><br>n print <_table_name_> <_object_name_><br>n quit<br>Note- Each command is limited to 4096 characters.|
|ignore_<br>script_<br>failure|Continues to execute the dbedit internal commands in the file and<br>ignores errors.<br>You can use it when you specify the "-f <_File_Name_>" parameter.|
|-continue_<br>updating|Continues to update the modified objects, even if the operation fails for<br>some of the objects (ignores the errors and runs theupdate_all<br>command at the end of the script).<br>You can use it when you specify the "-f <_File_Name_>" parameter.|
|-r "<_Open__<br>_Reason__<br>_Text_>"|Specifies the reason for opening the database in read-write mode<br>(default mode).|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d<br><_Database__<br>_Name_>|Specifies the name of the database, to which the dbedit utility should<br>connect (for example,mdsdb).|
|-listen|The dbedit utility "listens" for changes (use this mode for advanced<br>troubleshooting with the assistance of Check Point Support).<br>The dbedit utility prints its internal messages when a change occurs in<br>the management database.|
|-readonly|Specifies to open the management database in read-only mode.|
|-session|Session Connectivity.|


##### **dbedit** Internal Commands


Note - To see the available tables, class names (object types), attributes and values, connect to Management Server with Database Tool (GuiDBEdit Tool) (see <u>sk13009).</u>

|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|-h|Description:<br>Prints the general help.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> -h|
|-q<br>quit|Description:<br>Quits from dbedit.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> -q|
||dbedit> quit [-update_all | -noupdate]|
||Examples:|
||n Exit the utility and commit the remaining modified objects<br>(interactive mode):|
||dbedit> quit|
||n Exit the utility and update all the remaining modified objects:|
||dbedit> quit -update_all|
||n Exit the utility and discard all modifications:|
||dbedit> quit -no_update|


|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|update|Description:<br>Saves the specified object in the specified table (for example,<br>"network_objects", "services", "users").<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> update <_table_name_> <_object_name_>|
||Example:<br>Save the object My_Service in the table services:|
||dbedit> update services My_Service|
|update_all|Description:<br>Saves all the modified objects.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> update_all|
|_print_set|Description:<br>Prints the specified object from the specified table (for example,<br>"network_objects", "services", "users") as it appears in the<br>$FWDIR/conf/objects_5_0.Cfile (sets of attributes).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> _print_set <_table_name_> <_object_name_>|
||Example:<br>Print the object My_Obj from the table network_objects:|
||dbedit> print network_objects My_Obj|
|print|Description:<br>Prints the list of attributes of the specified object from the specified<br>table (for example, "network_objects", "properties",<br>"services", "users").<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> print <_table_name_> <_object_name_>|
||Examples:|
||n Print the object My_Obj from the table network_objects (in<br>"Network Objects"):|
||dbedit> print network_objects my_obj|
||n Print the object firewall_properties from the table properties (in<br>"Global Properties"):|
||dbedit> print properties firewall_properties|


##### Command

##### Description, Syntax, Examples

##### printxml

printxml Description: Prints in XML format the list of attributes of the specified object from the specified table (for example, "network_objects", "properties", "services", "users"). You can export the settings from a Management Server to an XML file that you can use later with external automation systems. Syntax: dbedit> printxml < _table_name_ > [< _object_name_ >] Examples: n Print the object My_Obj from the table network_objects: dbedit> printxml network_objects my_obj n Print the object firewall_properties from the table properties (in "Global Properties"): dbedit> printxml properties firewall_ properties printbyuid Description: Prints the attributes of the object specified by its UID (appears in the $FWDIR/conf/objects_5_0.C file at the beginning of the object as "chkpf_uid ({...})"). Syntax: dbedit> printbyuid { _object_id_ } Example: Print the attributes of the object with the specified UID: dbedit> printbyuid {D3833F1D-0A58-AA42-865F39BFE3C126F1}


Command Description, Syntax, Examples query Description: Prints all the objects in the specified table. Optionally, you can query for objects with specific attribute and value - query is separated by a comma after "query <table_name>" (spaces are not allowed between the < _attribute_ > and '< _value_ >'). Syntax: dbedit> query < _table_name_ > [ , < _attribute_ >='< _value_ >' ] Examples: n Print all objects in the table users: dbedit> query users n Print all objects in the table network_objects that are defined as Management Servers: dbedit> query network_objects, management='true' n Print all objects in the table services with the name ssh: _command_sdbedit> query services, name='ssh'_ n Print all objects in the table services with the port 22: dbedit> query services, port='22' n Print all objects with the IP address 10.10.10.10: dbedit> query network_objects, ipaddr='10.10.10.10' whereused Description: Checks where the specified object used in the database. Prints the number of places, where this object is used and relevant information about each such place. Syntax: dbedit> whereused < _table_name_ > < _object_name_ > Example: Check where the object My_Obj is used: dbedit> whereused network_objects My_Obj


|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|create|Description:<br>Creates an object of specified type (with its default values) in the<br>database.<br>Restrictions apply to the object's name:<br>n Object names can have a maximum of 100 characters.<br>n Objects names can contain only ASCII letters, numbers, and<br>dashes.<br>n Reserved words will be blocked by the Management Server (refer<br>to sk40179).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> create <_object_type_> <_object_name_>|
||Example:<br>Create the service object My_Service of the type tcp_service (with its<br>default values):|
||dbedit> create tcp_service my_service|
|delete|Description:<br>Deletes an object from the specified table.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> delete <_table_name_> <_object_name_>|
||Example:<br>Delete the service object My_Service from the table services:|
||dbedit> delete services my_service|


##### Command

##### modify

##### Description, Syntax, Examples

##### Description:

Modifies the value of specified attribute in the specified object in the specified table (for example, "network_objects", "services", "users") in the management database.

Syntax:

dbedit> modify < _table_name_ > < _object_name_ > < _field_ name_ > < _value_ >

##### Examples:

- Modify the color to red in the object My_Service in the table services:

dbedit> modify services My_Service color red

- Add a comment to the object MyObj:

   - dbedit> modify network_objects MyObj comments "Created by fwadmin with dbedit"

- Set the value of the global property ike_use_largest_possible_ subnets in the table properties to false:

   - dbedit> modify properties firewall_properties ike_use_largest_possible_subnets false

- Create a new interface on the Security Gateway My_FW and modify its attributes - set the IP address / Mask and enable AntiSpoofing on interface with "Element Index"=3 (check the attributes of the object My_FW in Database Tool (GuiDBEdit Tool) (see <u>sk13009)):</u>


##### Command


|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|
|dbedit> addelement network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces interface<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:officialname NAME_OF_INTERFACE<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:ipaddr IP_ADDRESS<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:netmask NETWORK_MASK<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:security:netaccess:access<br>specific<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:security:netaccess:allowed<br>network_objects:group_name<br>dbedit> modify network_objects My_FW<br>interfaces:3:security:netaccess:perform_anti_<br>spoofing true<br>dbedit> modify network_objects MyObj FieldA<br>LINKSYS|
|n In the Owned Object MyObj change the value of FieldB to<br>NewVal:|
|dbedit> modify network_objects MyObj<br>FieldA:FieldB NewVal|
|n In the Linked Object MyObj change the value of FieldA from B to<br>C:|
|dbedit> modify network_objects MyObj FieldA<br>B:C|


##### Command

##### lock

##### Description, Syntax, Examples

##### Description:

Locks the specified object (by administrator) in the specified table (for example, "network_objects", "services", "users") from being modified by other users.

For example, if you connect from a remote computer to this Management Server with admin1 and lock an object, you are be able to connect with admin2, but are not able to modify the locked object, until admin1 releases the lock.

Syntax:

dbedit> lock < _table_name_ > < _object_name_ >

##### Example:

Lock the object My_Service_Obj in the table services in the database: dbedit> lock services My_Service_Obj

##### addelement

##### Description:

Adds a specified multiple field / container (with specified value) to a specified object in specified table. Syntax:

dbedit> addelement < _table_name_ > < _object_name_ > < _field_name_ > < _value_ >

##### Examples:

- Add the element BranchObjectClass with the value Organization to a multiple field Read in the object My_Obj in the table ldap:

dbedit> addelement ldap My_Obj Read:BranchObjectClass Organization

##### n Add the service MyService to the group of services MyServicesGroup in the table services:

dbedit> addelement services MyServicesGroup '' services:MyService

- Add the network MyNetwork to the group of networks MyNetworksGroup in the table network_objects:

dbedit> addelement network_objects MyNetworksGroup '' network_objects:MyNetwork


|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|rmelement|Description:<br>Removes a specified multiple field / container (with specified value)<br>from a specified object in specified table.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> rmelement <_table_name_> <_object_name_><br><_field_name_> <_value_>|
||Examples:<br>n Remove the service MyService from the group of services<br>MyServicesGroup from the table services:|
||dbedit> rmelement services MyServicesGroup ''<br>services:MyService|
||n Remove the network MyNetwork from the group of networks<br>MyNetworksGroup from the table network_objects:|
||dbedit> rmelement network_objects<br>MyNetworksGroup '' network_objects:MyNetwork|
||n Remove the element BranchObjectClass with the value<br>Organization from the multiple field Read in the object My_Obj in<br>the table ldap:|
||dbedit> rmelement ldap my_obj<br>Read:BranchObjectClass Organization|
|rename|Description:<br>Renames the specified object in specified table.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> rename <_table_name_> <_object_name_> <_new__<br>_object_name_>|
||Example:<br>Rename the network object london to chicago in the table network_<br>objects:|
||dbedit> rename network_objects london chicago|


|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|rmbyindex|Description:<br>Removes an element from a container by element's index.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> rmbyindex <_table_name_> <_object_name_><br><_field_name_> <_index_number_>|
||Example:<br>Remove the element backup_log_servers from the container log_<br>servers by element index 1 in the table network_objects:|
||dbedit> rmbyindex network_objects g log_<br>servers:backup_log_servers 1|
|add_owned_<br>remove_name|Description:<br>Adds an owned object (and removes its name) to a specified owned<br>object field (or container).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> add_owned_remove_name <_table_name_><br><_object_name_> <_field_name_> <_value_>|
||Example:<br>Add the owned object My_Gateway (and remove its name) to the<br>owned object field (or container) my_external_products:|
||dbedit> add_owned_remove_name network_objects My_<br>Gateway additional_products owned:my_external_<br>products|
|is_delete_<br>allowed|Description:<br>Checks if the specified object can be deleted from the specified table<br>(object cannot be deleted if it is used by other objects).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> is_delete_allowed <_table_name_> <_object__<br>_name_>|
||Example:|
||dbedit> is_delete_allowed network_objects MyObj|
||Check if the object MyObj can be deleted from the table network_<br>objects:|


|Command|Description, Syntax, Examples|
|---|---|
|set_pass|Description:<br>Sets specified password for specified user.<br>Notes:|
||n The password must contain at least 4 characters and no more<br>than 50 characters.<br>n This command cannot change the administrator's password.<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> set_pass <_Username_> <_Password_>|
||Example:<br>Set the password 1234 for the user abcd:|
||dbedit> set_pass abcd 1234|
|savedb|Description:<br>Saves the database. You can run this command only when the<br>database is locked globally (when you start the dbedit utility with the<br>"dbedit -globallock" command).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> savedb|
|savesession|Description:<br>Saves the session. You can run this command only when you start the<br>dbedit utility in session mode (with the "dbedit -session"<br>command).<br>Syntax:|
||dbedit> savesession|


## fw

##### Description

- Performs various operations on Security or Audit log files.

- Kills the specified Check Point processes.

- Manages the Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM) rules.

- Manages the Suspicious Activity Policy editor.

##### Syntax

fw [-d] fetchlogs < _options_ > hastat < _options_ > kill < _options_ > log < _options_ > logswitch < _options_ > lslogs < _options_ > mergefiles < _options_ > repairlog < _options_ > sam < _options_ > sam_policy < _options_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output to<br>a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|fetchlogs<br><_options_>|Fetches the specified Check Point log files - Security<br>($FWDIR/log/*.log*) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog*), from the<br>specified Check Point computer.<br>See"fw fetchlogs" on page 244.|
|hastat<br><_options_>|Shows information about Check Point computers in High Availability<br>configuration and their states.<br>See"fw hastat" on page 246.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|kill<br><_options_>|Kills the specified Check Point process.<br>See"fw kill" on page 247.|
|log<br><_options_>|Shows the content of Check Point log files - Security<br>($FWDIR/log/*.log) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog).<br>See"fw log" on page 248.|
|logswitch<br><_options_>|Switches the current active Check Point log file - Security<br>($FWDIR/log/fw.log) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog).<br>See"fw logswitch" on page 258.|
|lslogs<br><_options_>|Shows a list of Check Point log files - Security ($FWDIR/log/*.log*)<br>or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog*), located on the local computer or a<br>remote computer.<br>See"fw lslogs" on page 262.|
|mergefiles<br><_options_>|Merges several Check Point log files - Security ($FWDIR/log/*.log)<br>or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog), into a single log file.<br>See"fw mergefiles" on page 265.|
|repairlog<br><_options_>|Rebuilds pointer files for Check Point log files - Security<br>($FWDIR/log/*.log) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog).<br>See"fw repairlog" on page 268.|
|sam<br><_options_>|Manages the Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM) rules.<br>See"fw sam" on page 269.|
|sam_policy<br><_options_>|Manages the Suspicious Activity Policy editor that works with these type<br>of rules:|
|or<br>samp<br><_options_>|n Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM) rules.<br>n Rate Limiting rules.|
||See"fw sam_policy" on page 277.|


### fw fetchlogs

##### Description

Fetches the specified Security log files ($FWDIR/log/*.log*) or Audit log files ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog*) from the specified Check Point computer.

##### Syntax

fw [-d] fetchlogs [-f < _Name of Log File 1_ >] [-f < _Name of Log File 2_ >]... [-f < _Name of Log File N_ >] < _Target_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output to a<br>file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|-f <_Name_<br>_of Log_<br>_File N_>|Specifies the name of the log file to fetch. Need to specify name only.<br>Notes:<br>n If you do not specify the log file name explicitly, the command<br>transfers all Security log files ($FWDIR/log/*.log*) and all Audit<br>log files ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog*).<br>n The specified log file name can include wildcards * and ? (for<br>example,2017-0?-*.log).<br>If you enter a wildcard, you must enclose it in double quotes or single<br>quotes.<br>n You can specify multiple log files in one command.<br>You must use the-fparameter for each log file name pattern.<br>n This command also transfers the applicable log pointer files.|
|<_Target_>|Specifies the remote Check Point computer, with which this local Check<br>Point computer has established SIC trust.<br>n If you run this command on a Security Management Server or Domain<br>Management Server, then<_Target_>is the applicable object's name<br>or main IP address of the Check Point Computer as configured in<br>SmartConsole.<br>n If you run this command on a Security Gateway or Cluster Member,<br>then<_Target_>is the main IP address of the applicable object as<br>configured in SmartConsole.|


##### Notes:

- This command moves the specified log files from the $FWDIR/log/ directory on the specified Check Point computer. Meaning, it deletes the specified log files on the specified Check Point computer after it copies them successfully.

- This command moves the specified log files to the $FWDIR/log/ directory on the local Check Point computer, on which you run this command.

- This command cannot fetch the active log files $FWDIR/log/fw.log or $FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog.

To fetch these active log files:

1. Perform log switch on the applicable Check Point computer:

fw logswitch [-audit] [-h < _IP Address or Hostname_ >]

2. Fetch the rotated log file from the applicable Check Point computer:

fw fetchlogs -f < _Log File Name_ > < _IP Address or Hostname_ >

- This command renames the log files it fetched from the specified Check Point computer. The new log file name is the concatenation of the Check Point computer's name (as configured in SmartConsole), two underscore (_) characters, and the original log file name (for example: MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.log).

##### Example - Fetching log files from a Management Server

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs MyGW Size Log file name 23KB 2019-05-16_000000.log 9KB 2019-05-17_000000.log 11KB 2019-05-18_000000.log 5796KB 2019-06-01_000000.log 4610KB fw.log [Expert@HostName:0]#

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw fetchlogs -f 2019-06-01_000000 MyGW File fetching in process. It may take some time... File MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.log was fetched successfully [Expert@HostName:0]# [Expert@HostName:0]# ls $FWDIR/log/MyGW* /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.log /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.logaccount_ptr /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.loginitial_ptr /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/MyGW__2019-06-01_000000.logptr [Expert@HostName:0]# [Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs MyGW Size Log file name 23KB 2019-05-16_000000.log 9KB 2019-05-17_000000.log 11KB 2019-05-18_000000.log 4610KB fw.log [Expert@HostName:0]#


### fw hastat

##### Description

Shows information about Check Point computers in High Availability configuration and their states.


Note - This command is outdated. On cluster members, run the Gaia Clish command "show cluster state", or the Expert mode command "cphaprob state". Note - This command is outdated. On Management Servers, run the "cpstat" on page 190 command.

##### Syntax

fw hastat [< _Target1_ >] [< _Target2_ >] ... [< _TargetN_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<Target1>|Specifies the Check Point computers to query.|
|<Target2> ...|If you run this command on the Management Server, you can enter the|
|<TargetN>|applicable IP address, or the resolvable HostName of the managed<br>Security Gateway or Cluster Member.<br>If you do not specify the target, the command queries the local computer.|


##### Example - Querying the cluster members from the Management Server

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fw hastat 192.168.3.52 HOST NUMBER HIGH AVAILABILITY STATE MACHINE STATUS 192.168.3.52 1 active OK [Expert@MGMT:0]# [Expert@MGMT:0]# fw hastat 192.168.3.53 HOST NUMBER HIGH AVAILABILITY STATE MACHINE STATUS 192.168.3.53 2 stand-by OK [Expert@MGMT:0]# [Expert@MGMT:0]# fw hastat 192.168.3.52 192.168.3.53 HOST NUMBER HIGH AVAILABILITY STATE MACHINE STATUS 192.168.3.52 1 active OK 192.168.3.53 2 stand-by OK [Expert@MGMT:0]#

##### Example - Querying the local Cluster Member

[Expert@Member1:0]# fw hastat HOST NUMBER HIGH AVAILABILITY STATE MACHINE STATUS 192.168.3.52 1 active OK [Expert@Member1:0]#


### fw kill

##### Description

Kills the specified Check Point processes.


Important - Make sure the killed process is restarted, or restart it manually. See <u>sk97638.</u>

Syntax

fw [-d] kill [-t < _Signal Number_ >] < _Name of Process_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the<br>output to a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire<br>CLI session.|
|-t <_Signal_<br>_Number_>|Specifies which signal to send to the Check Point process.<br>For the list of available signals and their numbers, run thekill -l<br>command.<br>For information about the signals, see the manual pages for the<br>kill<br>and signal<br>.|
||If you do not specify the signal explicitly, the command sends Signal<br>15 (SIGTERM).<br>Note- Processes can ignore some signals.|
|<_Name of_|Specifies the name of the Check Point process to kill.|
|_Process_>|To see the names of the processes, run theps auxwfcommand.|


##### Example

fw kill fwd


### fw log

##### Description

Shows the content of Check Point log files - Security ($FWDIR/log/*.log) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog).

##### Syntax

fw log {-h | -help} fw [-d] log [-a] [-b "< _Start Timestamp_ >" "< _End Timestamp_ >"] [-c < _Action_ >] [{-f | -t}] [-g] [-H] [-h < _Origin_ >] [-i] [-k {< _Alert Name>_ | all}] [-l] [-m {initial | semi | raw}] [-n] [-o] [-p] [-q] [-S] [-s "< _Start Timestamp_ >"] [-e "< _End Timestamp_ >"] [-u < _Unification Scheme File_ >] [-w] [-x < _Start Entry Number_ >] [-y < _End Entry Number_ >] [-z] [-#] [< _Log File_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|{-h | -help}|Shows the built-in usage.<br>Note- The built-in usage does not show some of the parameters<br>described in this table.|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output<br>to a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI<br>session.|
|-a|Shows only Account log entries.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-b "<_Start_<br>_Timestamp_>"<br>"<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged between the specified start and<br>end times.<br>n The<_Start Timestamp_>and<_End Timestamp_>may be a<br>date, a time, or both.<br>n If date is omitted, then the command assumes the current date.<br>n Enclose the "<_Start Timestamp_>"and"<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>in single or double quotes (-b 'XX' 'YY", or-b<br>"XX" "YY).<br>n You cannot use the "-b" parameter together with the "-s" or "-<br>e" parameters.<br>n See the date and time format below.|
|-c <_Action_>|Shows only events with the specified action. One of these:<br>n accept<br>n drop<br>n reject<br>n encrypt<br>n decrypt<br>n vpnroute<br>n keyinst<br>n authorize<br>n deauthorize<br>n authcrypt<br>n ctl|
||Notes:|
||n Thefw logcommand always shows theControl(ctl) actions.<br>n For login action, use theauthcrypt.|
|-e "<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged before the specified time.<br>Notes:|
||n The<_End Timestamp_>may be a date, a time, or both.<br>n Enclose the<_End Timestamp_>in single or double quotes (-e<br>'...', or-e "...").<br>n You cannot use the "-e" parameter together with the "-b"<br>parameter.<br>n See the date and time format below.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-f|This parameter:<br>1. Shows the saved entries that match the specified conditions.<br>2. After the command reaches the end of the currently opened log<br>file, it continues to monitor the log file indefinitely and shows the<br>new entries that match the specified conditions.<br>Note- Applies only to the active log file$FWDIR/log/fw.logor<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog|
|-g|Does not show delimiters.<br>The default behavior is:|
||n Show a colon (:) after a field name<br>n Show a semi-colon (;) after a field value|
|-H|Shows the High Level Log key.|
|-h <_Origin_>|Shows only logs that were generated by the Security Gateway with<br>the specified IP address or object name (as configured in<br>SmartConsole).|
|-i|Shows log UID.|
|-k {<_Alert_<br>_Name_> | all}|Shows entries that match a specific alert type:<br>n <_Alert Name_>- Show only entries that match a specific alert<br>type:<br>l alert<br>l mail<br>l snmp_trap<br>l spoof<br>l user_alert<br>l user_auth<br>n all- Show entries that match all alert types (this is the default).|
|-l|Shows both the date and the time for each log entry.<br>The default is to show the date only once above the relevant entries,<br>and then specify the time for each log entry.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-m|Specifies the log unification mode:<br>n initial- Complete unification of log entries. The command<br>shows one unified log entry for each ID. This is the default.<br>If you also specify the-fparameter, then the output does not<br>show any updates, but shows only entries that relate to the start<br>of new connections. To shows updates, use thesemi<br>parameter.<br>n semi- Step-by-step unification of log entries. For each log<br>entry, the output shows an entry that unifies this entry with all<br>previously encountered entries with the same ID.<br>n raw- No log unification. The output shows all log entries.|
|-n|Does not perform DNS resolution of the IP addresses in the log file<br>(this is the default behavior).<br>This significantly speeds up the log processing.|
|-o|Shows detailed log chains - shows all the log segments in the log<br>entry.|
|-p|Does not perform resolution of the port numbers in the log file (this is<br>the default behavior).<br>This significantly speeds up the log processing.|
|-q|Shows the names of log header fields.|
|-S|Shows the Sequence Number.|
|-s "<_Start_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged after the specified time.<br>Notes:|
||n The<_Start Timestamp_>may be a date, a time, or both.<br>n If the date is omitted, then the command assumed the current<br>date.<br>n Enclose the<_Start Timestamp_>in single or double quotes<br>(-s '...', or-s "...").<br>n You cannot use the "-s" parameter together with the "-b"<br>parameter.<br>n See the date and time format below.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-t|This parameter:<br>1. Does not show the saved entries that match the specified<br>conditions.<br>2. After the command reaches the end of the currently opened log<br>file, it continues to monitor the log file indefinitely and shows the<br>new entries that match the specified conditions.<br>Note- Applies only to the active log file$FWDIR/log/fw.logor<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog|
|-u<br><_Unification_|Specifies the path and name of the log unification scheme file.<br>The default log unification scheme file is:|
|_Scheme File_>|<br>$FWDIR/conf/log_unification_scheme.C|
|-w|Shows the flags of each log entry (different bits used to specify the<br>"nature" of the log - for example, control, audit, accounting,<br>complementary, and so on).|
|-x <_Start_<br>_Entry Number_>|Shows only entries from the specified log entry number and below,<br>counting from the beginning of the log file.|
|-y <_End Entry_<br>_Number_>|Shows only entries until the specified log entry number, counting from<br>the beginning of the log file.|
|-z|In case of an error (for example, wrong field value), continues to show<br>log entries.<br>The default behavior is to stop.|
|-#|Show confidential logs in clear text.|
|<_Log File_>|Specifies the log file to read.<br>If you do not specify the log file explicitly, the command opens the<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.loglog file.<br>You can specify a switched log file.|


##### Date and Time format

|Part of timestamp|Format|Example|
|---|---|---|
|Date only|MMM DD, YYYY|June 11, 2018|
|Time only|HH:MM:SS|14:20:00|
|Note - In this case, the command assumes<br>the current date.|||
|Date and Time|MMM DD, YYYY<br>HH:MM:SS|June 11, 2018<br>14:20:00|


##### Output

Each output line consists of a single log entry, whose fields appear in this format:

Note - The fields that show depends on the connection type.

HeaderDateHour ContentVersion HighLevelLogKey Uuid SequenceNum Flags Action Origin IfDir InterfaceName LogId ...

##### This table describes some of the fields.

|Field Header|Description|Example|
|---|---|---|
|HeaderDateHour|Date and Time|12Jun2018 12:56:42|
|ContentVersion|Version|5|
|HighLevelLogKey|High Level Log<br>Key|<max_null>, or empty|
|Uuid|Log UUID|(0x5b1f99cb,0x0,0x3403a8c0,0xc00000<br>00)|
|SequenceNum|Log Sequence<br>Number|1|


|Field Header|Description|Example|
|---|---|---|
|Flags|Internal flags<br>that specify the<br>"nature" of the<br>log - for<br>example,<br>control, audit,<br>accounting,<br>complementary,<br>and so on|428292|
|Action|Action<br>performed on<br>this connection|n accept<br>n dropreject<br>n encrypt<br>n decrypt<br>n vpnroute<br>n keyinst<br>n authorize<br>n deauthorize<br>n authcrypt<br>n ctl|
|Origin|Object name of<br>the Security<br>Gateway that<br>generated this<br>log|MyGW|
|IfDir|Traffic direction|n <|
||through<br>interface:|n >|
||n <-<br>Outbound<br>(sent by a<br>Security<br>Gateway)<br>n >-<br>Inbound<br>(received<br>by a<br>Security<br>Gateway)||


|Field Header|Description|Example|
|---|---|---|
|InterfaceName|Name of the<br>Security<br>Gateway<br>interface, on<br>which this traffic<br>was logged<br>If a Security<br>Gateway<br>performed some<br>internal action<br>(for example,<br>log switch), then<br>the log entry<br>showsdaemon|n eth0<br>n daemon<br>n N/A|
|LogId|Log ID|0|
|Alert|Alert Type|n alert<br>n mail<br>n snmp_trap<br>n spoof<br>n user_alert<br>n user_auth|
|OriginSicName|SIC name of the<br>Security<br>Gateway that<br>generated this<br>log|CN=MyGW,O=MyDomain_<br>Server.checkpoint.com.s6t98x|
|inzone|Inbound<br>Security Zone|Local|
|outzone|Outbound<br>Security Zone|External|
|service_id|Name of the<br>service used to<br>inspect this<br>connection|ftp|


|Field Header|Description|Example|
|---|---|---|
|src|Object name or<br>IP address of<br>the connection's<br>source<br>computer|MyHost|
|dst|Object name or<br>IP address of<br>the connection's<br>destination<br>computer|MyFTPServer|
|proto|Name of the<br>connection's<br>protocol|tcp|
|sport_svc|Source port of<br>the connection|64933|
|ProductName|Name of the<br>Check Point<br>product that<br>generated this<br>log|n VPN-1 & FireWall-1<br>n Application Control<br>n FloodGate-1|
|ProductFamily|Name of the<br>Check Point<br>product family<br>that generated<br>this log|Network|


##### Examples

###### Example 1 - Show all log entries with both the date and the time for each log entry

fw log -l


###### Example 2 - Show all log entries that start after the specified timestamp

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw log -l -s "June 12, 2018 12:33:00" 12Jun2018 12:33:00 5 N/A 1 accept MyGW > N/A LogId: <max_null>; ContextNum: <max_null>; OriginSicName: CN=MyGW,O=MyDomain_ Server.checkpoint.com.s6t98x; fg-1_client_in_rule_name: Default; fg-1_client_out_rule_name: Default; fg-1_server_in_rule_name: Host Redirect; fg-1_server_out_rule_name: ; ProductName: FG; ProductFamily: Network;

[Expert@MyGW:0]#

Check DNS and Proxy configuration on the gateway.; Severity: 2; status: Failed; version: 1.0; failure_impact: Contracts may be out-of-date; update_service: 1; ProductName: Security Gateway/Management; ProductFamily: Network; [Expert@MyGW:0]#
