### fw log

##### Description

Shows the content of Check Point log files - Security ($FWDIR/log/*.log) or Audit ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog).

##### Syntax

fw log {-h | -help} fw [-d] log [-a] [-b "< _Start Timestamp_ >" "< _End Timestamp_ >"] [-c < _Action_ >] [{-f | -t}] [-g] [-H] [-h < _Origin_ >] [-i] [-k {< _Alert Name>_ | all}] [-l] [-m {initial | semi | raw}] [-n] [-o] [-p] [-q] [-S] [-s "< _Start Timestamp_ >"] [-e "< _End Timestamp_ >"] [-u < _Unification Scheme File_ >] [-w] [-x < _Start Entry Number_ >] [-y < _End Entry Number_ >] [-z] [-#] [< _Log File_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|{-h | -help}|Shows the built-in usage.<br>Note- The built-in usage does not show some of the parameters<br>described in this table.|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output<br>to a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI<br>session.|
|-a|Shows only Account log entries.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-b "<_Start_<br>_Timestamp_>"<br>"<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged between the specified start and<br>end times.<br>n The<_Start Timestamp_>and<_End Timestamp_>may be a<br>date, a time, or both.<br>n If date is omitted, then the command assumes the current date.<br>n Enclose the "<_Start Timestamp_>"and"<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>in single or double quotes (-b 'XX' 'YY", or-b<br>"XX" "YY).<br>n You cannot use the "-b" parameter together with the "-s" or "-<br>e" parameters.<br>n See the date and time format below.|
|-c <_Action_>|Shows only events with the specified action. One of these:<br>n accept<br>n drop<br>n reject<br>n encrypt<br>n decrypt<br>n vpnroute<br>n keyinst<br>n authorize<br>n deauthorize<br>n authcrypt<br>n ctl|
||Notes:|
||n Thefw logcommand always shows theControl(ctl) actions.<br>n For login action, use theauthcrypt.|
|-e "<_End_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged before the specified time.<br>Notes:|
||n The<_End Timestamp_>may be a date, a time, or both.<br>n Enclose the<_End Timestamp_>in single or double quotes (-e<br>'...', or-e "...").<br>n You cannot use the "-e" parameter together with the "-b"<br>parameter.<br>n See the date and time format below.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-f|This parameter:<br>1. Shows the saved entries that match the specified conditions.<br>2. After the command reaches the end of the currently opened log<br>file, it continues to monitor the log file indefinitely and shows the<br>new entries that match the specified conditions.<br>Note- Applies only to the active log file$FWDIR/log/fw.logor<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog|
|-g|Does not show delimiters.<br>The default behavior is:|
||n Show a colon (:) after a field name<br>n Show a semi-colon (;) after a field value|
|-H|Shows the High Level Log key.|
|-h <_Origin_>|Shows only logs that were generated by the Security Gateway with<br>the specified IP address or object name (as configured in<br>SmartConsole).|
|-i|Shows log UID.|
|-k {<_Alert_<br>_Name_> | all}|Shows entries that match a specific alert type:<br>n <_Alert Name_>- Show only entries that match a specific alert<br>type:<br>l alert<br>l mail<br>l snmp_trap<br>l spoof<br>l user_alert<br>l user_auth<br>n all- Show entries that match all alert types (this is the default).|
|-l|Shows both the date and the time for each log entry.<br>The default is to show the date only once above the relevant entries,<br>and then specify the time for each log entry.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-m|Specifies the log unification mode:<br>n initial- Complete unification of log entries. The command<br>shows one unified log entry for each ID. This is the default.<br>If you also specify the-fparameter, then the output does not<br>show any updates, but shows only entries that relate to the start<br>of new connections. To shows updates, use thesemi<br>parameter.<br>n semi- Step-by-step unification of log entries. For each log<br>entry, the output shows an entry that unifies this entry with all<br>previously encountered entries with the same ID.<br>n raw- No log unification. The output shows all log entries.|
|-n|Does not perform DNS resolution of the IP addresses in the log file<br>(this is the default behavior).<br>This significantly speeds up the log processing.|
|-o|Shows detailed log chains - shows all the log segments in the log<br>entry.|
|-p|Does not perform resolution of the port numbers in the log file (this is<br>the default behavior).<br>This significantly speeds up the log processing.|
|-q|Shows the names of log header fields.|
|-S|Shows the Sequence Number.|
|-s "<_Start_<br>_Timestamp_>"|Shows only entries that were logged after the specified time.<br>Notes:|
||n The<_Start Timestamp_>may be a date, a time, or both.<br>n If the date is omitted, then the command assumed the current<br>date.<br>n Enclose the<_Start Timestamp_>in single or double quotes<br>(-s '...', or-s "...").<br>n You cannot use the "-s" parameter together with the "-b"<br>parameter.<br>n See the date and time format below.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-t|This parameter:<br>1. Does not show the saved entries that match the specified<br>conditions.<br>2. After the command reaches the end of the currently opened log<br>file, it continues to monitor the log file indefinitely and shows the<br>new entries that match the specified conditions.<br>Note- Applies only to the active log file$FWDIR/log/fw.logor<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog|
|-u<br><_Unification_|Specifies the path and name of the log unification scheme file.<br>The default log unification scheme file is:|
|_Scheme File_>|<br>$FWDIR/conf/log_unification_scheme.C|
|-w|Shows the flags of each log entry (different bits used to specify the<br>"nature" of the log - for example, control, audit, accounting,<br>complementary, and so on).|
|-x <_Start_<br>_Entry Number_>|Shows only entries from the specified log entry number and below,<br>counting from the beginning of the log file.|
|-y <_End Entry_<br>_Number_>|Shows only entries until the specified log entry number, counting from<br>the beginning of the log file.|
|-z|In case of an error (for example, wrong field value), continues to show<br>log entries.<br>The default behavior is to stop.|
|-#|Show confidential logs in clear text.|
|<_Log File_>|Specifies the log file to read.<br>If you do not specify the log file explicitly, the command opens the<br>$FWDIR/log/fw.loglog file.<br>You can specify a switched log file.|


##### Date and Time format

|Part of timestamp|Format|Example|
|---|---|---|
|Date only|MMM DD, YYYY|June 11, 2018|
|Time only|HH:MM:SS|14:20:00|
|Note - In this case, the command assumes<br>the current date.|||
|Date and Time|MMM DD, YYYY<br>HH:MM:SS|June 11, 2018<br>14:20:00|


##### Output

Each output line consists of a single log entry, whose fields appear in this format:

Note - The fields that show depends on the connection type.

HeaderDateHour ContentVersion HighLevelLogKey Uuid SequenceNum Flags Action Origin IfDir InterfaceName LogId ...

##### This table describes some of the fields.

|Field Header|Description|Example|
|---|---|---|
|HeaderDateHour|Date and Time|12Jun2018 12:56:42|
|ContentVersion|Version|5|
|HighLevelLogKey|High Level Log<br>Key|<max_null>, or empty|

||through<br>interface:|n >|
||n <-<br>Outbound<br>(sent by a<br>Security<br>Gateway)<br>n >-<br>Inbound<br>(received<br>by a<br>Security<br>Gateway)||


|Field Header|Description|Example|

### fw logswitch

##### Description

Switches the current active log file:

1. Closes the current active log file

2. Renames the current active log file

3. Creates a new active log file with the default name


##### Notes:

- By default, this command switches the active Security log file -

   - $FWDIR/log/fw.log

> - You can specify to switch the active Audit log file - $FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog

##### Syntax

fw [-d] logswitch

- [-audit] [< _Name of Switched Log_ >]

-h < _Target_ > [[+ | -]< _Name of Switched Log_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output to a<br>file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|-audit|Specifies to switch the active Audit log file ($FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog).<br>You can use this parameter only on a Management Server.|
|-h<br><_Target_>|Specifies the remote computer, on which to switch the log.<br>Notes:|
||n The local and the remote computers must have established SIC trust.<br>n The remote computer can be a Security Gateway, a Log Server, or a<br>Security Management Server in High Availability deployment.<br>n You can specify the remote managed computer by its main IP<br>address or Object Name as configured in SmartConsole.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_Name of_<br>_Switched_<br>_Log_>|Specifies the name of the switched log file.<br>Notes:<br>n If you do not specify this parameter, then a default name is:<br><YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>.log<br><YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>.adtlog<br>For example, 2018-03-26_174455.log<br>n If you specify the name of the switched log file, then the name of the<br>switch log file is:<br><Specified_Log_Name>.log<br><Specified_Log_Name>.adtlog<br>n The log switch operation fails if the specified name for the switched<br>log matches the name of an existing log file.<br>n The maximal length of the specified name of the switched log file is<br>230 characters.|
|+|Specifies to copy the active log from the remote computer to the local<br>computer.<br>Notes:<br>n If you specify the name of the switched log file, you must write it<br>immediately after this + (plus) parameter.<br>n The command copies the active log from the remote computer and<br>saves it in the$FWDIR/log/directory on the local computer.<br>n The default name of the saved log file is:<br><Gateway_Object_Name>__<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>.log<br>For example, MyGW__2018-03-26_174455.log<br>n If you specify the name of the switched log file, then the name of the<br>saved log file is:<br><Gateway_Object_Name>__<Specified_Log_Name>.log<br>n When this command copies the log file from the remote computer, it<br>compresses the file.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-|Specifies to transfer the active log from the remote computer to the local<br>computer.<br>Notes:<br>n The command saves the copied active log file in the$FWDIR/log/<br>directory on the local computer and then deletes the switched log file<br>on the remote computer.<br>n If you specify the name of the switched log file, you must write it<br>immediately after this - (minus) parameter.<br>n The default name of the saved log file is:<br><Gateway_Object_Name>__<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS>.log<br>For example, MyGW__2018-03-26_174455.log<br>n If you specify the name of the switched log file, then the name of the<br>saved log file is:<br><Gateway_Object_Name>__<Specified_Log_Name>.log<br>n When this command transfers the log file from the remote computer, it<br>compresses the file.<br>n As an alternative, you can use the"fw fetchlogs" on page 244<br>command.|


##### Compression

When this command transfers the log files from the remote computer, it compresses the file with the gzip command (see RFC 1950 to RFC 1952 for details). The algorithm is a variation of LZ77 method. The compression ratio varies with the content of the log file and is difficult to predict. Binary data are not compressed. Text data, such as user names and URLs, are compressed.

###### Example - Switching the active Security log on a Security Management Server or Security Gateway

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fw logswitch Log file has been switched to: 2018-06-13_182359.log [Expert@MGMT:0]#

###### Example - Switching the active Audit log on a Security Management Server

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fw logswitch -audit Log file has been switched to: 2018-06-13_185711.adtlog [Expert@MGMT:0]#


###### Example - Switching the active Security log on a managed Security Gateway and copying the switched log

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fw logswitch -h MyGW + Log file has been switched to: 2018-06-13_185451.log [Expert@MGMT:0]# [Expert@MGMT:0]# ls $FWDIR/log/*.log /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/fw.log /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/MyGW__2018-06-13_185451.log [Expert@MGMT:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# ls $FWDIR/log/*.log /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/fw.log /opt/CPsuite-R81/fw1/log/2018-06-13_185451.log [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### fw lslogs

##### Description

Shows a list of Security log files ($FWDIR/log/*.log) and Audit log files ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog) residing on the local computer or a remote computer.

##### Syntax

fw [-d] lslogs [-f < _Name of Log File 1_ >] [-f < _Name of Log File 2_ >] ... [-f < _Name of Log File N_ >] [-e] [-r] [-s {name | size | stime | etime}] [< _Target_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect the output to a<br>file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|-f <_Name_<br>_of Log_<br>_File_>|Specifies the name of the log file to show. Need to specify name only.<br>Notes:<br>n If the log file name is not specified explicitly, the command shows all<br>Security log files ($FWDIR/log/*.log).<br>n File names may include*and?as wildcards (for example,2019-<br>0?-*). If you enter a wildcard, you must enclose it in double quotes or<br>single quotes.<br>n You can specify multiple log files in one command. You must use the<br>"-f" parameter for each log file name pattern:<br>-f <_Name of Log File 1_> -f <_Name of Log File 2_><br>... -f <_Name of Log File N_>|
|-e|Shows an extended file list. It includes the following information for each log<br>file:|
||n Size- The total size of the log file and its related pointer files<br>n Creation Time- The time the log file was created<br>n Closing Time- The time the log file was closed<br>n Log File Name- The file name|
|-r|Reverses the sort order (descending order).|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-s {name |<br>size |<br>stime |<br>etime}|Specifies the sort order of the log files using one of the following sort<br>options:<br>n name- The file name<br>n size- The file size<br>n stime- The time the log file was created (this is the default option)<br>n etime- The time the log file was closed|
|<_Target_>|Specifies the remote Check Point computer, with which this local Check<br>Point computer has established SIC trust.|
||n If you run this command on a Security Management Server or<br>Domain Management Server, then<_Target_>is the applicable<br>object's name or main IP address of the Check Point Computer as<br>configured in SmartConsole.<br>n If you run this command on a Security Gateway or Cluster Member,<br>then<_Target_>is the main IP address of the applicable object as<br>configured in SmartConsole.|


##### Example 1 - Default output

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs Size Log file name 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.log 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.log 9KB 2019-06-16_000000.log 10KB 2019-06-17_000000.log 9KB fw.log [Expert@HostName:0]#

##### Example 2 - Showing all log files

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs -f "*" Size Log file name 9KB fw.adtlog 9KB fw.log 9KB 2019-05-29_000000.adtlog 9KB 2019-05-29_000000.log 9KB 2019-05-20_000000.adtlog 9KB 2019-05-20_000000.log [Expert@HostName:0]#

##### Example 3 - Showing only log files specified by the patterns

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs -f "2019-06-14*" -f '2019-06-15*' Size Log file name 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.adtlog 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.log 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.adtlog 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.log [Expert@HostName:0]#


##### Example 4 - Showing only log files specified by the patterns and their extended information

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs -f "2019-06-14*" -f '2019-06-15*' Size Log file name 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.adtlog 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.log 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.adtlog 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.log [Expert@HostName:0]#

Example 5 - Showing only log files specified by the patterns, sorting by name in reverse order

[Expert@HostName:0]# fw lslogs -f "2019-06-14*" -f '2019-06-15*' -e -s name -r Size Creation Time Closing Time Log file name 11KB 14Jun2018 0:00:00 15Jun2018 0:00:00 2019-06-15_000000.log 11KB 14Jun2018 0:00:00 15Jun2018 0:00:00 2019-06-15_000000.adtlog 9KB 13Jun2018 18:23:59 14Jun2018 0:00:00 2019-06-14_000000.log 9KB 13Jun2018 0:00:00 14Jun2018 0:00:00 2019-06-14_000000.adtlog [Expert@HostName:0]#

##### Example 6 - Showing only log files specified by the patterns, from a managed Security Gateway with main IP address 192.168.3.53

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fw lslogs -f "2019-06-14*" -f '2019-06-15*' 192.168.3.53 Size Log file name 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.adtlog 11KB 2019-06-15_000000.log 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.log 9KB 2019-06-14_000000.adtlog [Expert@MGMT:0]#


### fw mergefiles

##### Description

Merges several Security log files ($FWDIR/log/*.log) into a single log file.

Merges several Audit log files ($FWDIR/log/*.adtlog) into a single log file.


##### Important:

- Do not merge the active Security file $FWDIR/log/fw.log with other Security switched log files.

   - Switch the active Security file $FWDIR/log/fw.log (with the "fw logswitch" on page 1067 command) and only then merge it with other Security switched log files.

- Do not merge the active Audit file $FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog with other Audit switched log files.

   - Switch the active Audit file $FWDIR/log/fw.adtlog (with the "fw logswitch" on page 1067 command) and only then merge it with other Audit switched log files.

- This command unifies logs entries with the same Unique-ID (UID). If you rotate the current active log file before all the segments of a specific log arrive, this command merges the records with the same Unique ID from two different files, into one fully detailed record.

- If the size of the final merged log file exceeds 2GB, this command creates a list of merged files, where the size of each merged file size is not more than 2GB. The user receives this warning:

Warning: The size of the files you have chosen to merge is greater than 2GB. The merge will produce two or more files.

The names of merged files are:

  - < _Name of Merged Log File_ >.log

>   - < _Name of Merged Log File_ >_1.log

>   - < _Name of Merged Log File_ >_2.log

>   - ... ...

  - < _Name of Merged Log File_ >_N.log

##### Syntax

fw [-d] mergefiles {-h | -help}

fw [-d] mergefiles [-r] [-s] [-t < _Time Conversion File_ >] < _Name of Log File 1_ > < _Name of Log File 2_ > ... < _Name of Log File N_ > < _Name of Merged Log File_ >


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then<br>redirect the output to a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|{-h | -help}|Shows the built-in usage.|
|-r|Removes duplicate entries.|
|-s|Sorts the merged file by theTimefield in log records.|
|-t <_Time Conversion_<br>_File_>|Specifies a full path and name of a file that instructs this<br>command how to adjust the times during the merge.<br>This is required if you merge log files from Log Servers<br>configured with different time zones.<br>The file format is:|
||<_IP Address of Log Server #1_> <_Signed_<br>_Date Time #1 in Seconds_><br><_IP Address of Log Server #2_> <_Signed_<br>_Date Time #2 in Seconds_><br>... ...|
||Notes<br>n You must specify the absolute path and the file<br>name.<br>n The name of the time conversion file cannot<br>exceed 230 characters.|
|<_Name of Log File 1_><br>... <_Name of Log File_<br>_N_>|Specifies the log files to merge.<br>Notes:<br>n You must specify the absolute path and the<br>name of the input log files.<br>n The name of the input log file cannot exceed<br>230 characters.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_Name of Merged Log_<br>_File_>|Specifies the output merged log file.<br>Notes:|
||n The name of the merged log file cannot<br>exceed 230 characters.<br>n If a file with the specified name already exists,<br>the command stops and asks you to remove<br>the existing file, or to specify another name.<br>n The size of the merged log file cannot exceed<br>2 GB. In such scenario, the command creates<br>several merged log files, each not exceeding<br>the size limit.|


##### Example - Merging Security log files

[Expert@HostName:0]# ls -l $FWDIR/*.log -rw-rw-r-- 1 admin root 189497 Sep 7 00:00 2019-09-07_000000.log -rw-rw-r-- 1 admin root 14490 Sep 9 09:52 2019-09-09_000000.log -rw-rw-r-- 1 admin root 30796 Sep 10 10:56 2019-09-10_000000.log -rw-rw-r-- 1 admin root 24503 Sep 10 13:08 fw.log [Expert@HostName:0]# [Expert@HostName:0]# fw mergefiles -s $FWDIR/2019-09-07_000000.log $FWDIR/2019-09-09_000000.log $FWDIR/2019-09-10_000000.log /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.log [Expert@HostName:0]# [Expert@HostName:0]# ls -l /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.log* -rw-rw---- 1 admin root 213688 Sep 10 13:18 /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.log -rw-rw---- 1 admin root 8192 Sep 10 13:18 /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.logLuuidDB -rw-rw---- 1 admin root 80 Sep 10 13:18 /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.logaccount_ptr -rw-rw---- 1 admin root 2264 Sep 10 13:18 /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.loginitial_ptr -rw-rw---- 1 admin root 4448 Sep 10 13:18 /var/log/2019-Sep-Merged.logptr [Expert@HostName:0]#


### fw monitor

##### Description

Firewall Monitor is the Check Point traffic capture tool.

In a Security Gateway, traffic passes through different inspection points - Chain Modules in the Inbound direction and then in the Outbound direction (see "fw ctl chain" on page 1017).

The FW Monitor tool captures the traffic at each Chain Module in both directions.

You can later analyze the captured traffic with the same FW Monitor tool, or with special tools like Wireshark.


##### Notes:

- Only one instance of "fw monitor" can run at a time.

- You can stop the "fw monitor" instance in one of these ways:

     - In the shell, in which the "fw monitor" instance runs, press CTRL + C keys

     - In another shell, run this command: fw monitor -U

- Each time you run the FW Monitor, it compiles its temporary policy files ($FWDIR/tmp/monitorfilter.*).

- From R80.20, the FW Monitor is able to show the traffic accelerated with SecureXL.

- For more information, see <u>sk30583</u> and <u>How to use FW Monitor.</u>

##### Syntax for IPv4

fw monitor {-h | -help}

fw monitor [-d] [-D] [-ci < _Number of Inbound Packets_ >] [-co < _Number of Outbound Packets_ >] [-e < _INSPECT Expression_ > | -f {< _INSPECT Filter File_ > | -}] [-F "< _Source IP_ >,< _Source Port_ >,< _Dest IP_ >,< _Dest Port_ >,< _Protocol Number_ >"] [-i] [-l < _Length_ >] [-m {i,I,o,O,e,E}] [-o < _Output File_ > [-w]] [[-pi < _Position_ >] [-pI < _Position_ >] [-po < _Position_ >] [-pO < _Position_ >] | -p all [-a]] [-T] [-u | -s] [-U] [-v < _VSID_ >] [-x < _Offset_ >[,< _Length_ >] [-w]]


##### Syntax for IPv6

fw6 monitor {-h | -help}

fw6 monitor [-d] [-D] [-ci < _Number of Inbound Packets_ >] [-co < _Number of Outbound Packets_ >] [-e < _INSPECT Expression_ > | -f {< _INSPECT Filter File_ > | -}] [-F "< _Source IP_ >,< _Source Port_ >,< _Dest IP_ >,< _Dest Port_ >,< _Protocol Number_ >"] [-i] [-l < _Length_ >] [-m {i,I,o,O,e,E}] [-o < _Output File_ > [-w]] [[-pi < _Position_ >] [-pI < _Position_ >] [-po < _Position_ >] [-pO < _Position_ >] | -p all [-a]] [-T] [-u | -s] [-U] [-v < _VSID_ >] [-x < _Offset_ >[,< _Length_ >] [-w]]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|{-h | -help}|Shows the built-in usage.|
|-d<br>-D|Runs the command in debug mode and shows some information<br>about how the FW Monitor starts and compiles the specified<br>INSPECT filter:<br>n -d<br>Simple debug output.<br>n -D<br>Verbose output.<br>Note- You can specify both parameters to show more<br>information.|
|-ci <_Number of_<br>_Inbound Packets_><br>-co <_Number of_<br>_Outbound_<br>_Packets_>|Specifies how many packets to capture.<br>The FW Monitor stops the traffic capture if it counted the specified<br>number of packets.<br>n -ci<br>Specifies the number of inbound packets to count.<br>n -co<br>Specifies the number of inbound packets to count<br>Best Practice- You can use the "-ci" and the "-co"<br>parameters together. This is especially useful during large<br>volumes of traffic. In such scenarios, FW Monitor may bind so<br>many resources (for writing to the console, or to a file) that<br>recognizing the break sequence (CTRL+C) might take a very<br>long time.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-e <_INSPECT_<br>_Expression_><br>or<br>-f {<_INSPECT_<br>_Filter File_> |<br>-}|Captures only specific packets of non-accelerated traffic:<br>n "-e <_INSPECT Expression_>"<br>Defines the INSPECT filter expression on the command line.<br>n "-f <_INSPECT Filter File_>"<br>Reads the INSPECT filter expression from the specified file.<br>You must enter the full path and name of the plain-text file<br>that contains the INSPECT filter expression.<br>n "-f -"<br>Reads the INSPECT filter expression from the standard<br>input. After you enter the INSPECT filter expression, you<br>must enter the^D(CTRL+D) as the EOF (End Of File)<br>character.|
||Warning- These INSPECT filters donotapply to the<br>accelerated traffic.<br>Important- Make sure to enclose the INSPECT filter<br>expression correctly in single quotes (ASCII value 39) or<br>double quotes (ASCII value 34).<br>Notes:<br>n Refer to the$FWDIR/lib/fwmonitor.deffile for<br>useful macro definitions.<br>n See syntax examples below ("Examples for the "-e"<br>parameter" on page 1094).|
|-F "<_Source_<br>_IP_>,<_Source_<br>_Port_>,<_Dest_<br>_IP_>,<_Dest_<br>_Port_>,<_Protocol_<br>_Number_>"|Specifies the capture filter (for both accelerated and non-<br>accelerated traffic):<br>n <_Source IP_>- Specifies the source IP address<br>n <_Source Port_>- Specifies the source Port Number (see<br>IANA<br>Service<br>Name<br>and<br>Port<br>Number<br>Registry<br>)<br>n <_Dest IP_>- Specifies the destination IP address<br>n <_Dest Port_>- Specifies the destination Port Number (see<br>IANA<br>Service<br>Name<br>and<br>Port<br>Number<br>Registry<br>)<br>n <_Protocol Number_>- Specifies the Protocol Number (see<br>IANA<br>Protocol<br>Numbers<br>)|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
||Notes:<br>n See syntax examples below ("Examples for the "-F"<br>parameter" on page 1108).<br>n The "-F" parameter uses these Kernel Debug Filters.<br>For more information, see the R81<br>Quantum<br>Security<br>Gateway<br>Guide<br>- Chapter Kernel Debug on Security<br>Gateway - Section Kernel Debug Filters.<br>l For the Source IP address:|
||simple_debug_filter_saddr_<_N_> "<_IP_<br>_Address_>"|
||l For the Source Ports:|
||simple_debug_filter_sport_<_N_> <1-<br>65535>|
||l For the Destination IP address:|
||simple_debug_filter_daddr_<_N_> "<_IP_<br>_Address_>"|
||l For the Destination Ports:|
||simple_debug_filter_dport_<_N_> <1-<br>65535>|
||l For the Protocol Number:|
||simple_debug_filter_proto_<_N_> <0-<br>254>|
||n Value 0 means "any".<br>n This parameter supports up to 5 capture filters (up to 5<br>instances of the "-F" parameter in the syntax).<br>The FW Monitor performs the logical "OR" between all<br>specified simple capture filters.|
|-H|Creates an IP address filter.<br>For more information, see the R81<br>Quantum<br>Security<br>Gateway<br>Guide<br>- Chapter Kernel Debug on Security Gateway - Section<br>Kernel Debug Filters.<br>This parameter supports up to 3 capture filters (up to 3 instances of<br>the "-H" parameter in the syntax).<br>Example - Capture only HTTP traffic to and from the Host 1.1.1.1:<br>fw ctl debug –H "1.1.1.1"|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-i|Flushes the standard output.<br>Note- This parameter is valid only with the "-v <_VSID_>"<br>parameter.<br>Best Practice- Use this parameter to make sure FW Monitor<br>immediately writes the captured data for each packet to the<br>standard output. This is especially useful if you want to kill a<br>running FW Monitor process, and want to be sure that FW<br>Monitor writes all the data to the specified file.|
|-l <_Length_>|Specifies the maximal length of the captured packets. FW Monitor<br>reads only the specified number of bytes from each packet.<br>Notes:<br>n This parameter is optional.<br>n With this parameter you can capture only the headers<br>from each packet (for example, IP and TCP) and omit<br>the payload. This decreases the size of the output file.<br>This also helps the internal FW Monitor buffer not to fill<br>too fast.<br>n Make sure to capture the minimal required number of<br>bytes, to capture the Layer 3 IP header and Layer 4<br>Transport header.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-m {i, I, o, O,<br>e, E}|Specifies the capture mask (inspection point) in relation to Chain<br>Modules, in which the FW Monitor captures the traffic.<br>These are the inspection points, through which each packet<br>passes on a Security Gateway.<br>n -m i<br>Pre-Inbound only (before the packet enters a Chain Module<br>in the inbound direction)<br>n -m I<br>Post-Inbound only (after the packet passes a Chain Module<br>in the inbound direction)<br>n -m o<br>Pre-Outbound only (before the packet enters a Chain Module<br>in the outbound direction)<br>n -m O<br>Post-Outbound only (after the packet passes through a<br>Chain Module in the outbound direction)<br>n -m e<br>Pre-Outbound VPN only (before the packet enters a VPN<br>Chain Module in the outbound direction)<br>n -m E<br>Post-Outbound VPN only (after the packet passes through a<br>VPN Chain Module in the outbound direction)|


- Parameter Description Notes: n You can specify several capture masks (for example, to see NAT on the egress packets, enter "... -m o O ...").

- You can use this capture mask parameter "-m {i, I, o, O, e, E}" together with the chain module position parameter "-p{i | I | o | O}".

- In the inbound direction: l All chain positions before the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Pre-Inbound (the "fw ctl chain" on page 1017 command shows this module as "fw VM inbound").

  - All chain modules after the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Post-Inbound.

- In the outbound direction: l All chain position before the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Pre-Outbound.

  - All chain modules after the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Post-Outbound.

- By default, the FW Monitor captures the traffic only in the FireWall Virtual Machine module.

- The packet direction relates to each specific packet, and not to the connection's direction.

- The letters "q" and "Q" after the inspection point mean that the QoS policy is applied to the interface.

- Example packet flows: n From a Client to a Server through the FireWall Virtual Machine module: [Client] --> ("i") {FW VM attached to eth1} ("I") [Security Gateway] ("o") {FW VM attached to eth2} ("O") --> [Server]

- From a Server to a Client through the FireWall Virtual Machine module: [Client] <-- ("O") {FW VM attached to eth1} ("o") [Security Gateway] ("I") {FW VM attached to eth2} ("i") <-- [Server]


|Para|meter|Description|
|---|---|---|
|-o|<_Output File_>|Specifies the output file, to which FW Monitor writes the captured<br>raw data.<br>Important- If you do not specify the path explicitly, FW<br>Monitor creates this output file in the current working directory.<br>Because this output file can grow very fast to very large size,<br>we always recommend to specify the full path to the largest<br>partition/var/log/.<br>The format of this output file is the same format used by tools like<br>snoop(refer to RFC<br>1761<br>).<br>You can later analyze the captured traffic with the same FW<br>Monitor tool, or with special tools like Wireshark.|
|-pi <br>-pI <br>-po <br>-pO <br>or<br>-p|<_Position_><br> <_Position_><br> <_Position_><br> <_Position_><br>all [-a]|Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module at the specified position<br>between the kernel Chain Modules (see the"fw ctl chain" on<br>page 1017).<br>If the FW Monitor writes the captured data to the specified output<br>file (with the parameter "-o <_Output File_>"), it also writes the<br>position of the FW Monitor chain module as one of the fields.<br>You can insert the FW Monitor Chain Module in these positions<br>only:|
|||n -pi <_Position_><br>Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module in the specified Pre-<br>Inbound position.<br>n -pI <_Position_><br>Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module in the specified Post-<br>Inbound position.<br>n -po <_Position_><br>Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module in the specified Pre-<br>Outbound position.<br>n -pO <_Position_><br>Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module in the specified Post-<br>Outbound position<br>n -p all [-a]<br>Inserts the FW Monitor Chain Module at all positions (both<br>Inbound and Outbound).<br>Warning- This parameter causes very high load on the<br>CPU, but provides the most complete traffic capture.<br>The "-a" parameter specifies to use absolute chain<br>positions. This parameter changes the chain ID from a<br>relative value (which only makes sense with the matching<br>output from the"fw ctl chain" on page 1017command) to an<br>absolute value.|


Parameter Description Notes: n < _Position_ > can be one of these: l A relative position number In the output of the "fw ctl chain" on page 1017 command, refer to the numbers in the leftmost column (for example, 0, 5, 14). l A relative position alias In the output of the "fw ctl chain" on page 1017 command, refer to the internal chain module names in the rightmost column in the parentheses (for example, sxl_in, fw, cpas). l An absolute position In the output of the "fw ctl chain" on page 1017 command, refer to the numbers in the second column from the left (for example, -7fffffff, -1fffff8, 7f730000). In the syntax, you must write these numbers in the hexadecimal format (for example, -0x7fffffff, -0x1fffff8, 0x7f730000). n You can use this chain module position parameter "-p{i | I| o | O} ..." together with the capture mask parameter "-m {i, I, o, O, e, E}". n In the inbound direction: l All chain positions before the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Pre-Inbound (the "fw ctl chain" on page 1017 command shows this module as "fw VM inbound"). l All chain modules after the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Post-Inbound. n In the outbound direction: l All chain position before the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Pre-Outbound. l All chain modules after the FireWall Virtual Machine module are Post-Outbound. n By default, the FW Monitor captures the traffic only in the FireWall Virtual Machine module. n The chain module position parameters "-p{i | I| o | O} ..." parameters do not apply to the accelerated traffic, which is still monitored at the default inbound and outbound positions.

> - For more information about the inspection points, see the applicable table below.


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-T|Shows the timestamp for each packet:<br>DDMMMYYYY HH:MM:SS.mmmmmm<br>Best Practice- Use this parameter if you do not save the<br>output to a file, but print it on the screen.|
|-u<br>or<br>-s|Shows UUID for each packet (it is only possible to print either the<br>UUID, or the SUUID - not both):<br>n -u<br>Prints connection's Universal-Unique-ID (UUID) for each<br>packet<br>n -s<br>Prints connection's Session UUID (SUUID) for each packet|
|-U|Removes the simple capture filters specified with this parameter:|
||-F "<_Source IP_>,<_Source Port_>,<_Dest IP_>,<_Dest_<br>_Port_>,<_Protocol Number_>"|
|-v <_VSID_>|On a VSX Gateway or VSX Cluster Member, captures the packets<br>on the specified Virtual System or Virtual Router.<br>By default, FW Monitor captures the packets on all Virtual Systems<br>and Virtual Routers.<br>Example:|
||fw monitor -v 4 -e "accept;" -o /var/log/fw_<br>mon.cap|
|-w|Captures the entire packet, instead of only the header.<br>Must be used together with one of these parameters:<br>n -o <_Output File_><br>n -x <_Offset_>[,<_Length_>]|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-x <_Offset_><br>[,<_Length_>]|Specifies the position in each packet, where the FW Monitor starts<br>to capture the data from each packet.<br>Optionally, it is also possible to limit the amount of data the FW<br>Monitor captures.<br>n <_Offset_><br>Specifies how many bytes to skip from the beginning of each<br>packet. FW Monitor starts to capture the data from each<br>packet only after the specified number of bytes.<br>n <_Length_><br>Specifies the maximal length of the captured packets. FW<br>Monitor reads only the specified number of bytes from each<br>packet.|
||For example, to skip over the IP header and TCP header, enter "-x<br>52,96"|


Inspection points in Security Gateway and in the FW Monitor output

Note - The Inbound and Outbound traffic direction relates to each specific packet, and not to the connection.


##### n Inbound

|Name of inspection<br>point|Relation to the FireWall<br>Virtual Machine|Notion of inspection<br>point<br>in the FW Monitor output|
|---|---|---|
|Pre-Inbound|Before the inbound FireWall<br>VM|i (for example,eth4:i)|
|Post-Inbound|After the inbound FireWall VM|I (for example,eth4:I)|
|Pre-Inbound VPN|Inbound before decrypt|id (for example,<br>eth4:id)|
|Post-Inbound VPN|Inbound after decrypt|ID (for example,<br>eth4:ID)|
|Pre-Inbound QoS|Inbound before QoS|iq (for example,<br>eth4:iq)|
|Post-Inbound QoS|Inbound after QoS|IQ (for example,<br>eth4:IQ)|


##### n Outbound

|Name of inspection<br>point|Relation to the FireWall<br>Virtual Machine|Notion of inspection<br>point<br>in the FW Monitor output|
|---|---|---|
|Pre-Outbound|Before the outbound FireWall<br>VM|o (for example,eth4:o)|
|Post-Outbound|After the outbound FireWall<br>VM|O (for example,eth4:O)|
|Pre-Outbound VPN|Outbound before encrypt|e (for example,eth4:e)|
|Post-Outbound VPN|Outbound after encrypt|E (for example,eth4:E)|
|Pre-Outbound QoS|Outbound before QoS|oq (for example,<br>eth4:oq)|
|Post-Outbound QoS|Outbound after QoS|OQ (for example,<br>eth4:OQ)|

##### Examples for the "-e" parameter

###### Example 1 - Capture everything

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "accept;" -o /var/log/fw_ mon.cap

###### Example 2 - Capture traffic to / from specific hosts

To specify a host, you can use one of these expressions:

- Use "host(< _IP_Address_in_Doted_Decimal_format_ >)", which applies to both Source IP address and Destination IP address

- Use a specific Source IP address "src=< _IP_Address_in_Doted_Decimal_ format_ >" and a specific Destination IP address "dst=< _IP_Address_in_Doted_ Decimal_format_ >"

##### Example filters:


- Capture everything between host X and host Y:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "host(x.x.x.x) and host (y.y.y.y), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap [Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "((src=x.x.x.x , dst=y.y.y.y) or (src=y.y.y.y , dst=x.x.x.x)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

> - Capture everything between hosts X,Z and hosts Y,Z in all Firewall kernel chains:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -p all -e "((src=x.x.x.x or dst=z.z.z.z) and (src=y.y.y.y or dst=z.z.z.z)), accept ;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

- Capture everything to/from host X or to/from host Y or to/from host Z:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "host(x.x.x.x) or host (y.y.y.y) or host(z.z.z.z), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "((src=x.x.x.x or dst=x.x.x.x) or (src=y.y.y.y or dst=y.y.y.y) or (src=z.z.z.z or dst=z.z.z.z)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

###### Example 3 - Capture traffic to / from specific ports


Note - You must specify port numbers in Decimal format. Refer to the /etc/services file on the Security Gateway, or to <u>IANAService Name andPort Number Registry.</u>

To specify a port, you can use one of these expressions:

- Use "port(< _IANA_Port_Number_ >)", which applies to both Source Port and Destination Port

- Use a specific Source Port "sport=< _IANA_Port_Number_ >" and a specific Destination Port "dport=< _IANA_Port_Number_ >"

- In addition:

     - For specific TCP port, you can use "tcpport(< _IANA_Port_Number_ >)", which applies to both Source TCP Port and Destination TCP Port

     - For specific UDP port, you can use "udpport(< _IANA_Port_Number_ >)", which applies to both Source UDP Port and Destination UDP Port

Example filters:


##### n Capture everything to/from port X:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "port(x), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "(sport=x or dport=x), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

##### n Capture everything except port X:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "((sport=!x) or (dport=!x)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "not (sport=x or dport=x), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

##### n Capture everything except SSH:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "((sport!=22) or (dport!=22)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "not (sport=22 or dport=22), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "not tcpport(22), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

##### n Capture everything to/from host X except SSH:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "(host(x.x.x.x) and (sport!=22 or dport!=22)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "((src=x.x.x.x or dst=x.x.x.x) and (not (sport=22 or dport=22))), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "(host(x.x.x.x) and not tcpport(22)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

##### n Capture everything except NTP:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "not udpport(123), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

###### Example 4 - Capture traffic over specific protocol


Note - You must specify protocol numbers in Decimal format. Refer to the /etc/protocols file on the Security Gateway, or to <u>IANAProtocolNumbers.</u>

To specify a protocol, you can use one of these expressions:


- Use "ip_p=< _IANA_Protocol_Number_ >"

   - Examples:

        - To specify TCP protocol with byte offset, use "ip_p=6"

        - To specify UDP protocol with byte offset, use "ip_p=11"

        - To specify ICMP protocol with byte offset, use "ip_p=1"

- Use "accept [9:1]=< _IANA_Protocol_Number_ >"

   - Examples:

        - To specify TCP protocol with byte offset, use "accept [9:1]=6"

        - To specify UDP protocol with byte offset, use "accept [9:1]=11"

        - To specify ICMP protocol with byte offset, use "accept [9:1]=1"

- In addition, you can explicitly use these expressions to specify protocols:

   - Summary Table

|Which protocol to<br>specify|On which port(s) traffic is<br>captured|Expression|
|---|---|---|
|TCP|N / A|"tcp, accept;"|
|UDP|N / A|"udp, accept;"|
|ICMPv4|N / A|"icmp, accept;"<br>or<br>"icmp4, accept;"|
|ICMPv6|N / A|"icmp6, accept;"|
|HTTP|TCP 80|"http, accept;"|
|HTTPS|TCP 443|"https, accept;"|
|PROXY|TCP 8080|"proxy, accept;"|
|DNS|UDP 53|"dns, accept;"|
|IKE|UDP 500|"ike, accept;"|
|NAT-T|UDP 4500|"natt, accept;"|
|ESP and IKE|IP proto 50 and UDP 500|"vpn, accept;"|


|Whic<br>spec|h protocol to<br>ify|On which port(s) traffic is<br>captured|Expression|
|---|---|---|---|
|All VPN<br>|-related data:<br>|a. IP proto 50|"vpnall,<br>|
|a. <br>|ESP<br>|b. UDP 2746|accept;"|
|b.|IPsec over UDP|c. UDP 500||
|c. <br>|IKE<br>|d. UDP 4500||
|d.|NAT-T|e. TCP 18264||
|e. <br>f. <br>g. <br>h. <br>i. <br>j. <br>k. <br>l.|CRL<br> RDP<br> Tunnel Test<br> Topology<br> L2TP<br> SCV<br> Multi-Portal<br> and so on|f. UDP 259<br>g. UDP 18234<br>h. TCP 264<br>i. TCP 1701<br>j. UDP 18233<br>k. TCP 443 + TCP 444<br>l. and so on||
|Multi-P|ortal connections|TCP 443 and TCP 444|"multi, accept;"|
|SSH||TCP 22|"ssh, accept;"|
|FTP||TCP 20 and TCP 21|"ftp, accept;"|
|Telnet||TCP 23|"telnet,<br>accept;"|
|SMTP||TCP 25|"smtp, accept;"|
|POP3||TCP 110|"pop3, accept;"|


Example filters:


> - Filter to capture everything on protocol X:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "ip_p=X, accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

> - Filter to capture rverything on protocol X and port Z on protocol Y:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "(ip_p=X) or (ip_p=Y, port (Z)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

> - Filter to capture capture everything TCP between host X and host Y:

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "ip_p=6, host(x.x.x.x) or host(y.y.y.y), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap

[Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "tcp, host(x.x.x.x) or host (y.y.y.y), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap [Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "accept [9:1]=6 , ((src=x.x.x.x , dst=y.y.y.y) or (src=y.y.y.y , dst=x.x.x.x));" [Expert@HostName]# fw monitor -e "ip_p=6, ((src=x.x.x.x , dst=y.y.y.y) or (src=y.y.y.y , dst=x.x.x.x)), accept;" -o /var/log/fw_mon.cap
