## fw ctl affinity

The fw ctl affinity command shows and configures the CoreXL affinity settings for:

- Interfaces

- User-space processes

- CoreXL Firewall instances


### Running the 'fw ctl affinity -l' command in Gateway Mode

##### Description

The fw ctl affinity -l command shows the current CoreXL affinity settings on a Security Gateway for:

##### n Interfaces

- User-space processes

> - CoreXL Firewall instances

##### Syntax

##### n To see the built-in help:

fw ctl affinity

> - To show all the existing affinities:

fw ctl affinity -l [-a] [-v] [-r] [-q]

##### n To show the affinity for a specified interface:

fw ctl affinity -l -i < _Interface Name_ >

##### n To show the affinity for a specified CoreXL Firewall instance:

fw ctl affinity -l -k < _CoreXL Firewall instance ID_ >

##### n To show the affinity for a specified user-space process by its PID:

fw ctl affinity -l -p < _Process ID_ >

##### n To show the affinity for a specified user-space process by its name:

fw ctl affinity -l -n < _Process Name_ >

##### n To show the number of system CPU cores allowed by the installed CoreXL license:

fw -d ctl affinity -corelicnum


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-i <_Interface_<br>_Name_>|Shows the affinity for the specified interface.|
|-k <_CoreXL_<br>_Firewall instance_<br>_ID_>|Shows the affinity for the specified CoreXL Firewall instance.|
|-p <_Process ID_>|Shows the affinity for the Check Point user-space process (for<br>example: fwd, vpnd) specified by its PID.|
|-n <_Process Name_>|Shows the affinity for the Check Point user-space process (for<br>example: fwd, vpnd) specified by its name.|
|all|Shows the affinity for all CPU cores (numbers start from zero).|
|<_CPU ID0_> ... <_CPU_<br>_IDn_>|Shows the affinity for the specified CPU cores (numbers start<br>from zero).|
|-a|Shows all current CoreXL affinities.|
|-v|Shows verbose output with IRQ numbers of interfaces.|
|-r|Shows the CoreXL affinities in reverse order.|
|-q|Suppresses the errors in the output.|


##### Example 1

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l eth0: CPU 0 eth1: CPU 0 eth2: CPU 0 eth3: CPU 0 fw_0: CPU 7 fw_1: CPU 6 fw_2: CPU 5 fw_3: CPU 4 fw_4: CPU 3 fw_5: CPU 2 fwd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 fgd50: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 status_proxy: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 rad: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpstat_monitor: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 mpdaemon: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpsead: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cserver: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 rtmd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 fwm: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpsemd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpca: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cprid: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l -a -v Interface eth0 (irq 67): CPU 0 Interface eth1 (irq 75): CPU 0 Interface eth2 (irq 83): CPU 0 Interface eth3 (irq 59): CPU 0 fw_0: CPU 7 fw_1: CPU 6 fw_2: CPU 5 fw_3: CPU 4 fw_4: CPU 3 fw_5: CPU 2 fwd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 fgd50: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 status_proxy: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 rad: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpstat_monitor: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 mpdaemon: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpsead: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cserver: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 rtmd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 fwm: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpsemd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpca: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cprid: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 cpd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 [Expert@MyGW:0]#


##### Example 3

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l -a -v -r CPU 0: eth0 (irq 67) eth1 (irq 75) eth2 (irq 83) eth3 (irq 59) CPU 1: CPU 2: fw_5 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd CPU 3: fw_4 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd CPU 4: fw_3 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd CPU 5: fw_2 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd CPU 6: fw_1 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd CPU 7: fw_0 fwd fgd50 status_proxy rad cpstat_monitor mpdaemon cpsead cserver rtmd fwm cpsemd cpca cprid cpd All: [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 4

##### Example 5

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ps -ef | grep -v grep | egrep "PID|fwd" UID PID PPID C STIME TTY TIME CMD admin 26641 26452 0 Mar27 ? 00:06:56 fwd [Expert@MyGW:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l -p 26641 Process 26641: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 [Expert@MyGW:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l -n fwd fwd: CPU 2 3 4 5 6 7 [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 6

### Running the 'fw ctl affinity -l' command in VSX Mode

##### Description

The fw ctl affinity -l command shows the CoreXL affinity settings on a VSX Gateway for:

##### n Interfaces

- User-space processes

- CoreXL Firewall instances


Note - Before running the fw ctl affinity -l -x commands, you must go to the context of the applicable Virtual System or Virtual Router with the Gaia Clish command set virtual-system < _VSID_ >.

##### Syntax

##### n To show the affinities in VSX mode (you can combine the optional parameters):

- fw ctl affinity -l -x [-vsid < _VSID ranges_ >] [-cpu < _CPU ID ranges_ >]

   - [-flags {e | k | t | n | h | o}]

##### n To show the number of system CPU cores allowed by the installed CoreXL license:

fw -d ctl affinity -corelicnum


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-vsid <_VSID ranges_>|Shows the affinity for:<br>n The specified single Virtual System (for example,-<br>vsid 7)<br>n The specified several Virtual Systems (for<br>example,-vsid 0-2 4)<br>Important- If you omit the-vsidparameter, the<br>command runs in the current virtual context.|
|<_CPU ID ranges_>|Shows the affinity for:<br>n The specified single CPU (for example,-cpu 7)<br>n The specified several CPU cores (for example,-<br>cpu 0-2 4)|
|-flags {e | k | t | n <br>h | o}||<br>The-flagsparameter requires at least one of these<br>arguments:<br>n e- Do not print the exception processes<br>n k- Do not print the kernel threads<br>n t- Print all process threads<br>n n- Print the process name instead of the<br>/proc/<PID>/cmdline<br>n h- Print the CPU mask in Hex format<br>n o- Print the output into the file called<br>/tmp/affinity_list_output<br>Important- You must specify multiple arguments<br>together. For example:-flags tn|


##### Example 1

|[Expert@VSX_GW:0]# fw ctl affinity -l -x -cpu 0<br>---------------------------------------------------------------------<br><br><br><br>|
|---|
||PID<br>|VSID |<br>CPU<br>|SRC|V|KT |EXC| NAME|
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
||<br>2 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>3 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>4 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>14 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>99 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>278 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>382 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>674 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>2195 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>6348 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>||
||<br>6378 |<br>0 |<br>0 |<br>| | K |<br>|<br>---------------------------------------------------------------------|
|PID<br>- represents the pid of the process|
|VSID<br>- represents the virtual device id|
|CPU<br>- represents the CPUs assigned to the specific process|
|SRC<br>- represents the source configuration file of the process - (V)SID / (I)nstance /|
|(P)rocess|
|V<br>- represents validity,star means that the actual affinity is different than the configured|
|affinity|
|KT<br>- represents whether the process is a kernel thread|
|EXC<br>- represents whether the process belongs to the process exception list (vsaffinity_<br>exception.conf)|
|[Expert@VSX_GW:0]#|

### Running the 'fw ctl affinity -s' command in Gateway Mode

##### Description

The fw ctl affinity -s command configures the CoreXL affinity settings on a Security Gateway for:

##### n Interfaces

> - User-space processes

> - CoreXL Firewall instances


Note - The Security Gateway saves these changes in the $FWDIR/conf/fwaffinity.conf configuration file.

##### Syntax

> - To see the built-in help:

fw ctl affinity

##### n To configure the affinity for a specified interface by its name:

fw ctl affinity -s -i < _Interface Name_ > all < _CPU ID0_ > [ < _CPU ID1_ > ... < _CPU IDn_ > ]

##### n To configure the affinity for a specified CoreXL Firewall instance:

fw ctl affinity -s -k < _CoreXL Firewall instance ID_ > all

< _CPU ID0_ > [ < _CPU ID1_ > ... < _CPU IDn_ > ]

##### n To configure the affinity for a specified user-space process by its PID:

fw ctl affinity -s -p < _Process ID_ > all < _CPU ID0_ > [ < _CPU ID1_ > ... < _CPU IDn_ > ]

##### n To configure the affinity for a specified user-space process by its name:

fw ctl affinity -s -n < _Process Name>_ all < _CPU ID0_ > [ < _CPU ID1_ > ... < _CPU IDn_ > ]


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-i <_Interface_<br>_Name_>|Configures the affinity for the specified interface.|
|-k <_CoreXL_<br>_Firewall instance_<br>_ID_>|Configures the affinity for the specified CoreXL Firewall<br>instance.|
|-p <_Process ID_>|Configures the affinity for the Check Point user-space process<br>(for example: fwd, vpnd) specified by its PID.|
|-n <_Process Name_>|Configures the affinity for the Check Point user-space process<br>(for example: fwd, vpnd) specified by its name.<br>Important- The process name is case-sensitive.|
|all|Configures the affinity for all CPU cores (numbers start from<br>zero).|
|<_CPU ID0_> ... <_CPU_<br>_IDn_>|Configures the affinity for the specified CPU cores (numbers<br>start from zero).|


##### Example 1 - Affine the interface eth1 to the CPU core #1

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -i eth1 1 eth1: CPU 1 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 2 - Affine the CoreXL Firewall instance #1 to the CPU core #2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -k 1 2 fw_1: CPU 2 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 3 - Affine the process CPD by its PID to the CPU core #2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# cpwd_admin list | egrep "PID|cpd" APP PID STAT #START START_TIME MON COMMAND CPD 6080 E 1 [13:46:27] 17/9/2018 Y cpd [Expert@MyGW:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -p 6080 2 Process 6080: CPU 2 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#


##### Example 4 - Affine the process CPD by its name to the CPU core #2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -n cpd 2 cpd: CPU 2 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### Running the 'fw ctl affinity -s' command in VSX Mode

##### Description

The fw ctl affinity -s command configures the CoreXL affinity settings on a VSX Gateway for:

##### n Interfaces

> - User-space processes

> - CoreXL Firewall instances

##### Syntax

##### n To see the built-in help:

fw ctl affinity

##### n To configure the affinities of Virtual Systems:

fw ctl affinity -s -d [-vsid < _VSID ranges_ > ] -cpu < _CPU ID ranges_ >

##### n To configure the affinities of a specified user-space process:

fw ctl affinity -s -d -pname < _Process Name_ > [-vsid < _VSID ranges_ >] -cpu all -cpu < _CPU ID ranges_ >

##### n To configure the affinities of specified FWK daemon instances (user-space Firewall):

fw ctl affinity -s -d -inst < _Instances Ranges_ > -cpu < _CPU ID ranges_ >

##### n To configure the affinities of all FWK instances (user-space Firewalls):

fw ctl affinity -s -d -fwkall < _Number of CPUs_ >

##### n To reset the affinities to defaults:

fw ctl affinity -vsx_factory_defaults -vsx_factory_defaults_no_prompt


##### Important

- The VSX Gateway saves these changes in the $FWDIR/conf/fwaffinity.conf configuration file.

- When you configure affinity of an interface, it automatically configures the affinities of all other interfaces that share the same IRQ to the same CPU core.

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-vsid <_VSID_<br>_ranges_>|Configures the affinity for:<br>n One specified Virtual System.<br>For example:-vsid 7<br>n Several specified Virtual Systems.<br>For example:-vsid 0-2 4<br>Note- If you omit the-vsidparameter, the command uses<br>the current virtual context.|
|<_CPU ID ranges_>|Configures the affinity to:<br>n One specified CPU core.<br>For example:-cpu 7<br>n Several specified CPU cores.<br>For example:-cpu 0-2 4<br>Important- Numbers of CPU cores start from zero.|
|-pname <_Process_<br>_Name_>|Configures the affinity for the Check Point daemon specified by its<br>name (for example: fwd, vpnd).<br>Important- The process name is case-sensitive.|
|-inst <_Instances_<br>_Ranges_>|Configures the affinity for:<br>n One specified FWK daemon instance.<br>For example:-inst 7<br>n Several specified FWK daemon instances.<br>For example:-inst 0 2 4|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-fwkall <_Number_<br>_of CPUs_>|Configures the affinity for all running FWK daemon instances to<br>the specified number of CPU cores.<br>If it is necessary to affine all running FWK daemon instances to all<br>CPU cores, enter the number of all available CPU cores.|
|-vsx_factory_<br>defaults|Deletes all existing affinity settings and creates the default affinity<br>settings during the next reboot.<br>Important- Before this operation, the command prompts the<br>user whether to proceed. You must reboot to complete the<br>operation.|
|-vsx_factory_<br>defaults_no_<br>prompt|Deletes all current affinity settings and creates the default affinity<br>settings during the next reboot.<br>Important- Before this operation, the command doesnot<br>prompt the user whether to proceed. You must reboot to<br>complete the operation.|


##### Example 1 - Affine the Virtual Devices #0,1,2,4,7,8 to the CPU cores #0,1,2,4

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -d -vsid 0-2 4 6-8 -cpu 0-2 4 VDevice 0-2 4 6-8 : CPU 0 1 2 4 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 2 - Affine the process CPD by its name for Virtual Devices #0-12 to the CPU core #7

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -d -pname cpd -vsid 0-12 -cpu 7 VDevice 0-12 : CPU 7 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. Warning: some of the VSIDs did not exist [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 3 - Affine the FWK daemon instances #0,2,4 to the CPU core #5

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -d -inst 0 2 4 -cpu 5 VDevice 0 2 4: CPU 5 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 4 - Affine all FWK daemon instances to the last two CPU cores

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -d -fwkall 2 VDevice 0-2 : CPU 2 3 - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#


##### Example 5 - Affine all FWK daemon instances to all CPU cores

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl affinity -s -d -fwkall 4 There are configured processes/FWK instances

(y) will override all currently configured affinity and erase the configuration files (n) will set affinity only for unconfigured processes/threads Do you want to override existing configurations (y/n) ? y VDevice 0-2 : CPU all - set successfully Multi-queue affinity was not changed. For More info, see sk113834. [Expert@MyGW:0]#


## fw -i

##### Description

By default, the "fw" on page 1002 commands apply to the entire Security Gateway. The fw commands show aggregated information for all CoreXL Firewall instances. The fw -i commands apply to the specified CoreXL Firewall instance.

##### Syntax

fw -i < _ID of CoreXL Firewall instance_ > < _Command_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_ID of CoreXL_<br>_Firewall_<br>_instance_>|Specifies the ID of the CoreXL Firewall instance.<br>To see the available IDs, run the"fw ctl multik stat" on page 1513<br>command.|
|<_Command_>|Only these commands support thefw -isyntax:|
||n fw -i <_ID_> conntab ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> ctl get ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> ctl leak ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> ctl pstat ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> ctl set ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> monitor ...|
||n fw -i <_ID_> tab ...|
||For details and additional parameters for any of these<br>commands, refer to the corresponding entry for each command.|


##### Example 1 - Show the Connections table for CoreXL Firewall instance #1

fw -i 1 tab -t connections

##### Example 2 - Show various internal statistics for CoreXL Firewall instance #1

fw -i 1 ctl pstat


## fwboot bootconf

##### Description

Configures boot security options.


Notes:

- You must run this command from the Expert mode.

- The settings are saved in the $FWDIR/boot/boot.conf file.


Warning - To avoid issues, do not edit the $FWDIR/boot/boot.conf file manually. Edit the file only with this command.

- Refer to these related commands: l "fwboot corexl" on page 1173 l "control_bootsec" on page 915

##### Syntax to show the current boot security options

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot bootconf get_corexl get_core_override get_def get_ipf get_ipv6 get_kernnum get_kern6num

##### Syntax to configure the boot security options

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot bootconf set_corexl {0 | 1} set_core_override < _number_ > set_def [< _/path/filename_ >] set_ipf {0 | 1} set_ipv6 {0 | 1} set_kernnum < _number_ > set_kern6num < _number_ >


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in help with available parameters.|
|get_corexl|Shows if the CoreXL is enabled or disabled:<br>n 0 - disabled<br>n 1 - enabled<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theCOREXL_INSTALLED.|
|get_core_<br>override|Shows the number of overriding CPU cores.<br>The SMT (HyperThreading) feature (sk93000<br>)uses this<br>configuration to set the number of CPU cores after reboot.<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theCORE_OVERRIDE.|
|get_def|Shows the configured path and the name of the Default Filter policy<br>file (default is$FWDIR/boot/default.bin).<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theDEFAULT_FILTER_PATH.|
|get_ipf|Shows if the IP Forwarding during boot is enabled or disabled:<br>n 0 - disabled (Security Gateway does not forward traffic<br>between its interfaces during boot)<br>n 1 - enabled<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theCTL_IPFORWARDING.|
|get_ipv6|Shows if the IPv6 support is enabled or disabled:<br>n 0 - disabled<br>n 1 - enabled<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theIPV6_INSTALLED.|
|get_kernnum|Shows the configured number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theKERN_INSTANCE_NUM.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|get_kern6num|Shows the configured number of IPv6 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theKERN6_INSTANCE_NUM.|
|set_corexl {0 |<br>1}|Enables or disables CoreXL:<br>n 0 - disables<br>n 1 - enables<br>Notes:<br>n In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the value<br>of theCOREXL_INSTALLED.<br>n To configure CoreXL, use the"cpconfig" on page 934<br>menu.|
|set_core_<br>override<br><_number_>|Configures the number of overriding CPU cores.<br>The SMT (HyperThreading) feature (sk93000<br>)uses this<br>configuration to set the number of CPU cores after reboot.<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theCORE_OVERRIDE.|
|set_def<br>[<<br>_/path/filename_<br>>]|Configures the path and the name of the Default Filter policy file<br>(default is$FWDIR/boot/default.bin).<br>Notes:<br>n In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the value<br>of theDEFAULT_FILTER_PATH.<br>n If you do not specify the path and the name explicitly,<br>then the value of theDEFAULT_FILTER_PATHis set to<br>0.<br>As a result, Security Gateway does not load a Default<br>Filter during boot.<br>Best Practice- The best location for this file is the<br>$FWDIR/boot/directory.|
|set_ipf {0 | 1}|Configures the IP forwarding during boot:<br>n 0 - disables (forbids the Security Gateway to forward traffic<br>between its interfaces during boot)<br>n 1 - enables<br>Note- In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the<br>value of theCTL_IPFORWARDING.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|set_ipv6 {0 |<br>1}|Enables or disables the IPv6 Support:<br>n 0 - disables<br>n 1 - enables<br>Notes:<br>n In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the value<br>of theIPV6_INSTALLED.<br>n Configure the IPv6 Support in Gaia Portal, or Gaia Clish.<br>See the R81<br>Gaia<br>Administration<br>Guide<br>.|
|set_kernnum<br><number>|Configures the number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>Notes:<br>n In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the value<br>of theKERN_INSTANCE_NUM.<br>n To configure CoreXL, use the"cpconfig" on page 934<br>menu.|
|set_kern6num<br><_number_>|Configures the number of IPv6 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>Notes:<br>n In the$FWDIR/boot/boot.conffile, refer to the value<br>of theKERN6_INSTANCE_NUM.<br>n To configure CoreXL, use the"cpconfig" on page 934<br>menu.|


## fwboot corexl

##### Description

Configures and monitors the CoreXL.


Note - The settings are saved in the $FWDIR/boot/boot.conf file.


Warning - To avoid issues, do not edit the $FWDIR/boot/boot.conf file manually. Edit the file only with this command.

##### Syntax to show CoreXL configuration

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl core_count curr_instance4_count curr_instance6_count def_instance4_count def_instance6_count eligible installed max_instance4_count max_instances4_32bit max_instances4_64bit max_instance6_count max_instances_count max_instances_32bit max_instances_64bit min_instance_count unsupported_features


##### Syntax to configure CoreXL


##### Important:

- The configuration commands are for Check Point use only. To configure CoreXL, use the Check Point CoreXL option in the "cpconfig" on page 934 menu.

- After all changes in CoreXL configuration on the Security Gateway, you must reboot it.

- In a Cluster, you must configure all the Cluster Members in the same way.

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl def_by_allowed [n] default [-v] disable [-v] enable [n] [-6 k] vmalloc_recalculate

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No<br>Parameters|Shows the built-in help with available parameters.|
|core_count|Returns the number of CPU cores on this computer.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl core_<br>count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>4<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep processor<br>processor : 0<br>processor : 1<br>processor : 2<br>processor : 3<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


|Parameter|Description||
|---|---|---|
|curr_<br>instance4_<br>count|Returns the current configured number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewa<br>Example|ll instances.|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl <br>instance4_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>3<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl multik stat<br>ID | Active<br>| CPU<br>| Connections | Peak<br>------------------------------------------|curr_<br>----|
||0 | Yes<br>| 3<br>|<br>11 ||18|
||1 | Yes<br>| 2<br>|<br>12 ||18|
||2 | Yes<br>| 1<br>|<br>13 ||18|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]#||
|curr_<br>instance6_<br>count|Returns the current configured number of IPv6 CoreXL Firewa<br>Example|ll instances.|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl <br>instance6_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>2<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw6 ctl multik stat<br>ID | Active<br>| CPU<br>| Connections | Peak<br>------------------------------------------|curr_<br>----|
||0 | Yes<br>| 3<br>|<br>11 ||18|
||1 | Yes<br>| 2<br>|<br>12 ||18|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]#||
|def_by_<br>allowed<br>[n]|Sets the default configuration for CoreXL according to the spec<br>allowed number of CPU cores.|ified|
|default|Sets the default configuration for CoreXL.||


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|def_<br>instance4_<br>count|Returns the default number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances for this<br>Security Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl def_<br>instance4_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>3<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|def_<br>instance6_<br>count|Returns the default number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances for this<br>Security Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl def_<br>instance6_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>2<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|[-v]<br>disable|Disables CoreXL.<br>n -v- Leaves the high memory (vmalloc) unchanged.<br>See the"cp_conf corexl" on page 924command.|
|eligible|Returns whether CoreXL can be enabled on this Security Gateway.<br>n 0 - CoreXL cannot be enabled<br>n 1 - CoreXL can be enabled<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl<br>eligible<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>1<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|[-v]<br>enable [n]<br>[-6 k]|Enables CoreXL with 'n' IPv4 Firewall instances and optionally 'k' IPv6<br>Firewall instances.<br>n -v- Leaves the high memory (vmalloc) unchanged.<br>n n- Denotes the number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>n k- Denotes the number of IPv6 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>See the"cp_conf corexl" on page 924command.|

||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl<br>installed<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>1<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|

|max_<br>instances<br>4_32bit|Returns the maximal allowed number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances<br>for a Security Gateway that runs Gaia with 32-bit kernel.<br>Example|

||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl max_<br>instances4_64bit<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>38<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|max_<br>instance6_<br>count|Returns the maximal allowed number of IPv6 CoreXL Firewall instances<br>for this Security Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl max_<br>instance6_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>3<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|max_<br>instances_<br>count|Returns the total maximal allowed number of CoreXL Firewall instances<br>(IPv4 and IPv6) for this Security Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl max_<br>instances_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>40<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|max_<br>instances_<br>32bit|Returns the total maximal allowed number of CoreXL Firewall instances<br>for a Security Gateway that runs Gaia with 32-bit kernel.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl max_<br>instances_32bit<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>16<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|max_<br>instances_<br>64bit|Returns the total maximal allowed number of CoreXL Firewall instances<br>for a Security Gateway that runs Gaia with 64-bit kernel.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl max_<br>instances_64bit<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>40<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|min_<br>instance_<br>count|Returns the minimal allowed number of IPv4 CoreXL Firewall instances.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl min_<br>instance_count<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>2<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|vmalloc_<br>recalculat<br>e|Updates the value of thevmallocparameter in the<br>/boot/grub/grub.conffile.|
|unsupporte<br>d_features|Returns 1 if at least one feature is configured, which CoreXL does not<br>support.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot corexl<br>unsupported_features<br>corexl unsupported feature: QoS is configured.<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>1<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


## fwboot cpuid

##### Description

Shows the number of available CPUs and CPU cores on this Security Gateway.

##### Syntax

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid {-h | -help | --help} -c --full ht_aware -n --possible

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No<br>Parameters|Shows the IDs of the available CPU cores on this Security Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid<br>3 2 1 0<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|-c|Counts the number of available CPU cores on this Security Gateway.<br>The command stores the returned number as its exit code.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid -c<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>4<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|--full|Shows a full map of the available CPUs and CPU cores on this Security<br>Gateway.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid --full<br>cpuid phys_id core_id thread_id<br>0 0 0 0<br>1 2 0 0<br>2 4 0 0<br>3 6 0 0<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|ht_aware|Shows the CPU cores in the order of their awareness of Hyper-Threading.<br>Example<br>|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid ht_aware<br>3 2 1 0<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|-n|Counts the number of available CPUs on this Security Gateway.<br>The command stores the returned number as its exit code.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid -n<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>4<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|
|--<br>possible|Counts the number of possible CPU cores.<br>The command stores the returned number as its exit code.<br>Example|
||[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot cpuid --<br>possible<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]# echo $?<br>4<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#|


## fwboot ht


Important - This command is obsolete and is not supported. To configure SMT (HyperThreading) feature, follow <u>sk93000.</u>


## fwboot multik_reg

##### Description

Shows the internal memory address of the registration function for the specified CoreXL Firewall instance.


Important - This command is for Check Point use only.


Note - You must run this command from the Expert mode.

##### Syntax

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot multik_reg < _Number of CoreXL Firewall instance_ > {ipv4 | ipv6} [-d]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in help with available<br>parameters.|
|<_Number of CoreXL Firewall_<br>_instance_>|Specifies the ID number of the CoreXL Firewall<br>instance.|
|ipv4|Specifies to work with IPv4 CoreXL Firewall<br>instances.|
|ipv6|Specifies to work with IPv6 CoreXL Firewall<br>instances.|
|-d|Shows the decimal 64-bit address of the hook<br>function.|


##### Example


<!-- Start of picture text -->
[Expert@MyGW:0]# fw ctl multik stat<br>ID | Active | CPU | Connections | Peak<br>----------------------------------------------<br>0 | Yes | 3 | 11 | 18<br>1 | Yes | 2 | 12 | 18<br>2 | Yes | 1 | 13 | 18<br>[Expert@MyGW:0]#<br><!-- End of picture text -->

[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot multik_reg 0 ipv4 0 [Expert@MyGW:0]#

[Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot multik_reg 1 ipv4 0xffffffff8a2a5690 [Expert@MyGW:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot multik_reg 2 ipv4 0xffffffff8a2a5690 [Expert@MyGW:0]#


## fwboot post_drv

##### Description

Loads the Firewall driver for CoreXL during boot.


##### Important:

- This command is for Check Point use only.

- If you run this command, Security Gateway can block all traffic. In such case, you must connect to the Security Gateway over a console and restart Check Point services with the "cpstop" on page 965 and "cpstart" on page 955 commands. Alternatively, you can reboot the Security Gateway.


- Note - You must run this command from the Expert mode.

##### Syntax

[Expert@HostName:0]# $FWDIR/boot/fwboot post_drv {ipv4 | ipv6}

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in help with available parameters.|
|ipv4|Loads the IPv4 Firewall driver for CoreXL.|
|ipv6|Loads the IPv6 Firewall driver for CoreXL.|


# Multi-Queue Commands

For more information about Multi-Queue, see the <u>R81Performance Tuning Administration Guide</u> - Chapter Multi-Queue.


## mq_mng

You configure Multi-Queue on the command line in one of these shells:

- In the Expert mode

- In Gaia Clish

### Multi-Queue Configuration in the Expert mode

##### Description

The mq_mng utility shows and configures the Multi-Queue on supported interfaces.

##### Syntax


##### Important:

- In a Cluster, you must configure all the Cluster Members in the same way.

- You must run these commands in the Expert mode.

- Change in the Multi-Queue mode can cause short packet loss.

##### n To see the built-in help

mq_mng {-h | --help}

##### n To show the existing Multi-Queue configuration:

mq_mng {-o | --show} [{-v | -vv}] [-a]

##### n To configure the Multi-Queue for the specified driver:

mq_mng {-s | --set-mode} auto manual {-i | --interface} < _Names of Interfaces_ > {-c | --core} < _IDs of CPU Cores_ > off [{-i | --interface} < _Names of Interfaces_ >]

##### n To apply the existing Multi-Queue policy:

mq_mng {-r | --reconf}


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-h | --<br>help|Shows built-in help.|
|-o | --<br>show|Shows the existing Multi-Queue configuration.|
|-v | -vv|Verbose output.|
|-a|Shows all interfaces in the output.|
|-s | --<br>set-mode|Configures the Multi-Queue mode:<br>n auto- Automatic mode (this is the default). Multi-Queue<br>automatically configures the affinity of all supported interfaces to CPU<br>cores that run CoreXL SND Instances.<br>n manual- Manual mode. Administrator configures the affinity of<br>interfaces to CPU cores that run CoreXL SND Instances. In this<br>mode, you can specify interfaces, CPU cores, or both.<br>n off- Disables the Multi-Queue on all or specified supported<br>interfaces.|
||Important- Change in the Multi-Queue mode can cause short packet<br>loss.|


##### Parameter Description


##### Notes:

- To specify interfaces:

     - Use this syntax:

      - {-i | --interface} < _Names of Interfaces_ >

     - If you do not specify interfaces, then the configuration applies to all supported interfaces.

     - To specify a specific interface, enter its name (for example: -i eth2).

     - To specify several interfaces, enter their names separates with spaces (for example: -i eth2 eth4).

- To specify CPU cores:

     - Use this syntax:

      - {-c | --core} < _IDs of CPU Cores that run CoreXL SND Instances_ >

     - To specify a specific CPU core, enter its ID number (for example: -c 1).

     - To specify several nonconsecutive CPU cores, enter their ID numbers separated with spaces (for example: -c 1 3) or commas (for example: -c 1,3).

     - To specify several consecutive CPU cores, enter their first and last ID numbers separated with a hyphen (for example: -c 3-6).

- To see the current CoreXL affinity configuration, run the "fw ctl affinity" on page 1518 command (with applicable parameters).

- To see the CoreXL Firewall Instances and which CPU cores they use, run the "fw ctl multik stat" on page 1513 command.

- To see all available CPU cores, run:

cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep processor -r | -- Applies the existing Multi-Queue policy. reconf

##### Examples

###### Show the current Multi-Queue configuration on all interfaces

[Expert@MyGW:0]# mq_mng --show

|Total 8 cores.|Multiqueue 2||||
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cores i/f<br>--------------|type<br>--------------|state<br>--------------|config<br>-----------------|cores<br>---------------|
|eth1|igb|Up|Auto|0,4|
|eth2|igb|Up|Auto|0,4|
|eth2-01|igb|Up|Auto|0,4|
|[Expert@MyGW:0|]#||||


###### Show the current Multi-Queue verbose configuration on all interfaces

[Expert@MyGW:0]# mq_mng --show -v

Total 8 cores. Multiqueue 2 cores: 0,4

|i/f<br>-----------|type<br>------------------|state<br>------------------|config<br>-------------|cores<br>--------------||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|eth1|igb|Up|Auto|0(58),4(78)||
|eth2|igb|Up|Auto|4(62),0(79)||
|eth2-01|igb|Up|Auto|0(42),4(86)||
|core<br>-----------|interfaces<br>------------------|queue<br>------------------|irq<br>-------------|rx packets<br>-----------------|tx packets<br>--------------|
|0|eth1|eth1-TxRx-0|58|2350|3012|
||eth2|eth2-TxRx-1|79|0|0|
||eth2-01|eth2-01-TxRx-0|42|0|45|
|4|eth1|eth1-TxRx-1|78|652|764|
||eth2|eth2-TxRx-0|62|0|0|
||eth2-01|eth2-01-TxRx-1|86|0|12|
|[Expert@MyG|W:0]#|||||


###### Show the current Multi-Queue verbose configuration on the interface eth2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# mq_mng --show -v -i eth2

|Total 8 cores. Multiqueue 2|cores: 0,4||||
|---|---|---|---|---|
|i/f<br>type<br>----------------------------|state<br>-------------------|config<br>------------|cores<br>--------------------|-------|
|eth2<br>igb<br>----------------------------<br>eth2 <igb> max 8 cur 2|Up<br>-------------------|Auto<br>------------|4(62),0(79)<br>--------------------|-------|
|06:00.2 Ethernet controller:|Intel Corporation|82580 Gigabi|t Network Connection|(rev 01)|
|core<br>interfaces<br>----------------------------|queue<br>-------------------|irq<br>------------|rx packets<br>--------------------|tx packets<br>------------|
|0<br>eth2|eth2-TxRx-1|79|4212|3965|
|4<br>eth2|eth2-TxRx-0|62|0|0|

###### Set automatic Multi-Queue mode on all interfaces

mq_mng --set-mode auto

###### Set manual Multi-Queue mode on the interfaces eth1 and eth2 to CPU cores 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6

mq_mng -s manual -i eth1 eth2 -c 0-2 4-6


### Multi-Queue Configuration in Gaia Clish

##### Syntax


Important:

   - In a Cluster, you must configure all the Cluster Members in the same way.

   - You must run these commands in Gaia Clish.

   - Change in the Multi-Queue mode can cause short packet loss.

- To show the existing Multi-Queue configuration for the specified interface:

show interface < _Name of Interface_ > multi-queue [verbose]

##### n To configure the Multi-Queue for the specified interface:

set interface < _Name of Interface_ > multi-queue auto manual core < _IDs of CPU Cores that run CoreXL SND Instances_ > off

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_Name of_|Specifies the interface.|
|_Interface_>||
|verbose|Verbose output that also includes:|
||n IRQ numbers for traffic queues<br>n Total number of RX and TX packets in traffic queues|
|auto|Configures the automatic Multi-Queue mode (this is the default).<br>Multi-Queue automatically configures the affinity of the specified<br>interface to CPU cores that run CoreXL SND Instances.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|manual core <_IDs_<br>_of CPU Cores_>|Configures the manual Multi-Queue mode.<br>Administrator configures the affinity of the specified interface to<br>CPU cores that run CoreXL SND Instances.<br>Notes:<br>n To specify a specific CPU core, enter its ID number (for<br>example:manual core 1).<br>n To specify several nonconsecutive CPU cores, enter<br>their ID numbers separated with commas and without<br>spaces (for example:manual core 1,3).<br>n To specify several consecutive CPU cores, enter their<br>first and last ID numbers separated with a hyphen (for<br>example:manual core 3-6).<br>n To see the current CoreXL affinity configuration, run the<br>"fw ctl affinity" on page 1518command (with applicable<br>parameters).<br>n To see the CoreXL Firewall Instances and which CPU<br>cores they use, run the"fw ctl multik stat" on page 1513<br>command.<br>n To see all available CPU cores, run:|
||cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep processor|
|off|Disables the Multi-Queue on the specified interface.|


##### Examples

###### Show Multi-Queue configuration on the interface eth2

MyGW> show interface eth2 multi-queue

Total 8 cores. Multiqueue 2 cores

i/f type state config cores -------------------------------------------------------------------------eth2 igb Up Auto 4,0 Note: The output does not include network interfaces that are currently in the down state. MyGW>


###### Show Multi-Queue verbose configuration on the interface eth2

MyGW> show interface eth2 multi-queue verbose

Total 8 cores. Multiqueue 2 cores: 0,4

|i/f|type|state|config|cores||
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|-----------|------------------|-----------------|--------------|--------------||
|eth2|igb|Up|Auto|4(62),0(79)||
|core<br>-----------|interfaces<br>------------------|queue<br>-----------------|irq<br>--------------|rx packets<br>-----------------|tx packets<br>--------------|
|0|eth2|eth2-TxRx-1|79|212|80|
|4|eth2|eth2-TxRx-0|62|16232|18901|
|MyGW>||||||


###### Set automatic Multi-Queue mode on the interface eth2

set interface eth2 multi-queue auto

###### Set manual Multi-Queue mode on the interface eth2 to CPU cores 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6

set interface eth2 multi-queue manual core 0-2,4-6


# Identity Awareness Commands

For more information about Identity Awareness, see the <u>R81Identity Awareness Administration Guide.</u>

These terms are used in the CLI commands:

|Term|Description|
|---|---|
|PDP|Identity AwarenessPolicy Decision Point.<br>This is an Identity AwarenessSecurity Gateway, which is responsible to collect<br>and share identities.|
|PEP|Identity AwarenessPolicy Enforcement Point.<br>This is an Identity AwarenessSecurity Gateway, which is responsible to<br>enforce network access restrictions.<br>It makes its decisions based on identity data it collected from thePDP.|
|ADLOG|The module responsible for the acquisition of identities of entities (users or<br>computers) from the Active Directory.<br>Theadlogruns on:|
||n An Identity AwarenessSecurity Gateway, for which you enabled the AD<br>Query.<br>The AD Query serves the Identity AwarenessSoftware Blade, which<br>enforces the policy and logs identities.<br>n A Log Server. Theadloglogs identities.<br>Theadlogis the command line process used to control and monitor the<br>ADLOG feature.<br>The command line tool helps control users' statuses, as well as troubleshoot<br>and monitor the system.|


The PEP and PDP processes are key components of the system. Through them, administrators control user access and network protection.


## adlog

##### Description

Provides commands to control and monitor the AD Query process.

##### Syntax

- When the adlog runs on a Security Gateway, the AD Query serves the Identity Awareness Software Blade, which enforces policy and logs identities.

In this case, the command syntax is:

adlog a < _parameter_ > [< _option_ >]

- When the adlog runs on a Log Server, it logs identities.

   - In this case, the command syntax is:

   - adlog l < _parameter_ > [< _option_ >]


Note - Parameters for the "adlog a" and "adlog l" commands are identical.

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Displays available options for this command and exits.|
|a|Sets the working mode:|
|or<br>l|n adlog a- If you use the AD Query for Identity<br>Awareness.<br>n adlog l- If you use a Log Server (Identity Logging).|
|control <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Sends control commands to the AD Query.<br>See"adlog control" on page 1563.|
|dc|Shows the status of a connection to the AD domain controller.<br>See"adlog dc" on page 1565.|
|debug <_parameter_>|Enables and disables theadlogdebug output.<br>See"adlog debug" on page 1566.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|query <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows the database of identities acquired by the AD Query,<br>according to the specified filter.<br>See"adlog query" on page 1567.|
|statistics|Shows statistics about NT Event logs received byadlog, for<br>each IP address and total.<br>Also shows the number of identified IP addresses.<br>See"adlog statistics" on page 1568.|


### adlog control

##### Description

Sends control commands to the AD Query.

Syntax

adlog {a | l} control muh < _options_ > reconf srv_accounts < _options_ > stop

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|muh<br><_options_>|Manages the list of Multi-User Hosts.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n Show all known Multi-User Hosts:|
||adlog {a | l} control muh show|
||n Add an IP address as a Multi-User Host:|
||adlog {a | l} control muh mark|
||n Removes an IP address from the list of Multi-User Hosts:|
||adlog {a | l} control muh unmark|
|reconf|Sends a reconfiguration command to the AD Query.<br>Resets the policy configuration to the one defined in SmartConsole.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|srv_<br>accounts<br><_options_>|Manages service accounts.<br>Service accounts are accounts that do not belong to actual users, rather<br>they belong to services that run on a computer. Service accounts are<br>suspected, if they are logged in more than a certain number of times.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Show all known service accounts:<br>|
||adlog {a | l} control srv_accounts show|
||n Clear all the accounts from the list of service accounts:|
||adlog {a | l} control srv_accounts clear|
||n Manually update the list of service accounts:|
||adlog {a | l} control srv_accounts find|
||n Remove an account name from the list of service accounts:|
||adlog {a | l} control srv_accounts unmark|
|stop|Stops the AD Query.<br>Security Gateway does not acquire new identities with the AD Query<br>anymore.|


### adlog dc

##### Description

Shows the status of a connection to the AD domain controller.

##### Syntax

adlog a dc adlog l dc


### adlog debug

##### Description

Enables and disables the adlog debug output.

|Feature|Output Debug File|
|---|---|
|Identity Awareness on a Security Gateway|$FWDIR/log/pdpd.elg|
|Identity Logging on a Log Server|$FWDIR/log/fwd.elg|


##### Syntax

adlog {a | l} debug extended mode off on

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|extended|Turns on the debug and adds extended debug topics.|
|mode|Shows the debug status ("on", or "off").|
|off|Turns off the debug.|
|on|Turns on the debug.|


### adlog query

##### Description

Shows the database of identities acquired by the AD Query, according to the specified filter.

##### Syntax

adlog {a | l} query all ip < _IP Address_ > machine < _Computer Name_ > string < _String_ > user < _Username_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|all|No filter. Shows the entire identity database.|
|ip <_IP Address_>|Filters identities that relate to the specified IP address.|
|machine <_Computer_|Filters identity mappings based on the specified computer|
|_Name_>|name.|
|string <_String_>|Filters identity mappings based on the specified text string.|
|user <_Username_>|Filters identity mappings based on the specified user.|


Example - Show the entry that contains the string " **jo** " in the user name

adlog a query user jo


### adlog statistics

##### Description

Shows statistics about NT Event logs received by adlog, for each IP address and total. Also shows the number of identified IP addresses.

##### Syntax

adlog a statistics adlog l statistics


## pdp

##### Description

These commands control and monitor the pdpd process.

##### Syntax

pdp < _command_ > [< _parameter_ > [< _option_ >]]

##### Commands

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows available options for this command and exits.|
|ad <_parameter_><br><_option_>|For the AD Query, adds (or removes) an identity to the Identity<br>Awareness database on the Security Gateway.<br>See"pdp ad" on page 1571.|
|auth <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows authentication or authorization options.<br>See"pdp auth" on page 1573.|
|broker <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Controls the PDP Identity Broker.<br>See"pdp broker" on page 1577.|
|conciliation<br><_parameter_><br><_option_>|Controls the session conciliation mechanism.<br>See"pdp conciliation" on page 1581.|
|connections<br><_parameter_>|Shows the PDP connections with the PEP gateways, Terminal<br>Servers, and Identity Collectors.<br>See"pdp connections" on page 1583.|
|control|Controls the PDP parameters.|
|<_parameter_><br><_option_>|See"pdp control" on page 1584.|
|debug <_parameter_>|Controls the PDP debug.|
|<_option_>|See"pdp debug" on page 1585.|
|idc <_parameter_>|Operations related to Identity Collector.|
|<_option_>|See"pdp idc" on page 1588.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|idp <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Operations related to SAML-based authentication.<br>See"pdp idp" on page 1592.|
|monitor<br><_parameter_><br><_option_>|Monitors the status of connected PDP sessions.<br>See"pdp monitor" on page 1593.|
|muh <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows Multi-User Hosts (MUHs).<br>See"pdp muh" on page 1595.|
|nested_groups<br><_parameter_>|Shows LDAP Nested groups configuration.<br>See"pdp nested_groups" on page 1596.|
|network<br><_parameter_>|Shows information about network related features.<br>See"pdp network" on page 1599.|
|radius <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows and configures the RADIUS accounting options.<br>See"pdp radius" on page 1600.|
|roles <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows the user role information.<br>See"pdp roles" on page 1603.|
|status <_parameter_>|Shows PDP status information, such as start time or<br>configuration time.<br>See"pdp status" on page 1606.|
|tasks_manager<br><_parameter_>|Shows the status of the PDP tasks.<br>See"pdp tasks_manager" on page 1607.|
|timers <_parameter_>|Shows PDP timers information for each session.<br>See"pdp timers" on page 1608.|
|topology_map|Shows topology of all PDP and PEP addresses.<br>See"pdp topology_map" on page 1609.|
|tracker<br><_parameter_>|Adds the TRACKER topic to the PDP logs.<br>See"pdp tracker" on page 1610.|
|update <_parameter_>|Recalculates users and computers group membership.<br>See"pdp update" on page 1611.|
|vpn <_parameter_>|Shows connected VPN gateways that send identity data from<br>VPN Remote Access Clients.<br>See"pdp vpn" on page 1612.|


### pdp ad

###### General Syntax

pdp ad associate < _options_ > disassociate < _options_ >

The 'pdp ad associate' command

##### Description

For the AD Query, adds an identity to the Identity Awareness database on the Security Gateway.

The group data must be in the AD.

##### Syntax

pdp ad associate ip < _IP Address_ > u < _Username_ > d < _Domain_ > [m < _Computer Name_ >] [t < _Timeout_ >] [s]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|ip <_IP_<br>_Address_>|Specifies the IP address for the identity.|
|u <_Username_>|Specifies the username for the identity.|
|d <_Domain_>|Specifies the Domain of the ID server.|
|m <_Computer_<br>_Name_>|Specifies the computer that is defined for the identity.|
|t <_Timeout_>|Specifies the timeout for the AD Query.<br>Default timeout is 5 hours.|
|s|Associates the "u <_Username_>" and the "m <_Computer_>"<br>parameters sequentially.<br>First, adds the "<_Computer_>" and then adds the "<_Username_>" to<br>the database.|


The 'pdp ad disassociate' command

##### Description

For the AD Query, removes the identity from the Identity Awareness database on the Security Gateway.

Identity Awareness does not authenticate a user that is removed.

##### Syntax

pdp ad disassociate ip < _IP Address_ > {u < _Username_ > | m < _Computer Name_ >} [r {override | probed | timeout}]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|ip <_IP Address_>|Specifies the IP address for the identity.|
|u <_Username_>|Specifies the username for the identity.|
|m <_Computer Name_>|Specifies the computer that is defined for the identity.|
|r {override | probed |<br>timeout}|Specifies the reason to show in SmartConsole on theLogs<br>& Monitor>Logstab.|


### pdp auth

##### Description

Configures authentication/authorization options for PDP.

##### Syntax

pdp auth allow_empty_result < _options_ > count_in_non_ldap_group < _options_ > fetch_by_sid < _options_ > force_domain < _options_ > kerberos_any_domain < _options_ > kerberos_encryption < _options_ > reauth_agents_after_policy < _options_ > recovery_interval < _options_ > username_password < _options_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|allow_empty_<br>result|Shows the current configuration of fetching of local groups from the<br>AD server based on SID.|
|<_options_>|Configures that the fetching of local groups from the AD server<br>based on SID should succeed, even if all SIDs are foreign.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n Disable the fetching of local groups:|
||pdp auth allow_empty_result disable|
||n Enable the fetching of local groups:|
||pdp auth allow_empty_result enable|
||n Show the current configuration:|
||pdp auth allow_empty_result status|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|count_in_non_<br>ldap_group<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the identification of membership to individual<br>users that are selected in the user picker and LDAP branch groups<br>in SmartConsole.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the identification of membership:|
||pdp auth count_in_non_ldap_group disable|
||n Enable the identification of membership:|
||pdp auth count_in_non_ldap_group enable|
||n Show the current configuration:|
||pdp auth count_in_non_ldap_group status|
|fetch_by_sid<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the fetching of local groups from the AD<br>server based on SID.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the fetching of local groups:|
||pdp auth fetch_by_sid disable|
||n Enable the fetching of local groups:|
||pdp auth fetch_by_sid enable|
||n Show the current configuration:|
||pdp auth fetch_by_sid status|
|force_domain<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the PDP to match the identity's source,<br>based on the reported domain and authorization domain.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the match the identity's source:|
||pdp auth force_domain disable|
||n Enable the match the identity's source:|
||pdp auth force_domain enable|
||n Show the current configuration:|
||pdp auth force_domain status|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|kerberos_any_<br>domain<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the use of all available Kerberos principles.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the use of all available Kerberos principles:|
||pdp auth kerberos_any_domain disable|
||n Enable the use of all available Kerberos principles:|

|kerberos_<br>encryption<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the Kerberos encryption type.<br>Note- In SmartConsole, go toObjectsmenu >Object Explorer<br>>Servers> open theLDAP Account Unitobject > go to<br>Generaltab > clickActive Directory SSO Configuration).<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Configure the Kerberos encryption type:|
||pdp auth kerberos_encryption set|

|reauth_agents_<br>after_policy<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the automatic reauthentication of Identity<br>Agents after policy installation.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the automatic reauthentication:|

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|recovery_<br>interval<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the frequency of attempts to connect back to<br>the higher-priority PDP gateway.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the reconnect attemtps:|
||pdp auth recovery_interval disable|
||n Enable the reconnect attemtps:|

||n Configure the frequency or reconnect attempts:|

||n Show the current configuration:|

|username_<br>password<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the username and password authentication.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Disable the username and password authentication:|

### pdp broker

##### Description

These commands control the PDP Identity Broker.

##### Syntax

pdp broker debug {set | unset} < _options_ > discard < _options_ > reconnect < _options_ > status [-e] sync < _options_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|debug set<br><_options_><br>debug unset<br><_options_>|Controls the debug of the PDP Identity Broker.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n Print the logs related to remote Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set pub <_IP Address of_<br>_Publisher PDP_>|
||n Disable the logs related to remote Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset pub <_IP Address of_<br>_Publisher PDP_>|
||n Print the extended logs related to remote Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set pub_ext <_IP Address_<br>_of Publisher PDP_>|
||n Disable the extended logs related to remote Publisher<br>PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset pub_ext <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_>|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
||n Print the logs related to communication with remote<br>Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set pub_transport <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_>|
||Enable this debug on the Subscriber PDP side to observe<br>the Publisher PDP's JSON requests in these cases:<br>l To monitor networking issues in case the message<br>was not received.<br>l To monitor the JSON requests from the Publisher<br>PDPs and related message-parsing issues.<br>l To monitor if the content of the JSON does not meet<br>the requirements (for example: Sharing ID).<br>n Disable the logs related to communication with remote<br>Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset pub_transport <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_>|
||n Print the logs related to remote Subscriber PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set sub <_IP Address of_<br>_Subscriber PDP_>|
||n Disable the logs related to remote Subscriber PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset sub <_IP Address of_<br>_Subscriber PDP_>|
||n Print the extended logs related to remote Subscriber PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set sub_ext <_IP Address_<br>_of Subscriber PDP_>|
||n Disable the extended logs related to remote Subscriber<br>PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset sub_ext <_IP_<br>_Address of Subscriber PDP_>|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
||n Print the logs related to communication with remote<br>Subscriber PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug set sub_transport <_IP_<br>_Address of Subscriber PDP_>|
||n Disable the logs related to communication with remote<br>Subscriber PDPs:|
||pdp broker debug unset sub_transport <_IP_<br>_Address of Subscriber PDP_>|
||Notes:<br>n For more information about the debug, see"pdp debug"<br>on page 1585.<br>n To see the HTTP related issues, run this command to<br>enable the debug on the Publisher PDP side:|
||pdp debug set HttpClient all|
||To see more information for some errors, run this<br>command:|
||pdp broker status [-e]|
|discard <_option_>|Controls the timeout for discarding sessions received from the<br>specified Publisher PDP during a disconnection.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Show the current timeout:|
||pdp broker discard show_timeout <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_>|
||n Configure the new timeout (in seconds):|
||pdp broker discard set_timeout <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_> <_Timeout_>|
|reconnect <_IP_<br>_Address of_<br>_Subscriber PDP_>|Forces the reconnection to the specified Subscriber<br>PDP immediately.<br>If you run this command, the PDP ignores the keep-alive intervals<br>and exponential backoff timeouts, and sends the handshake /<br>keep-alive immediately.<br>Best Practice- You can use this command when a long time<br>passed since the PDP disconnected, and it is necessary to<br>establish the connection again immediately.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|status [-e]|Shows the status of remote Publisher PDPs and Subscriber<br>PDPs.<br>The option "-e" flag adds more information (Subscriber PDP port<br>and the last error time and description).|
|sync <_option_>|Synchronizes identities with the specified Publisher PDPs or<br>Subscriber PDPs.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n Send the synchronization request (in the next broker<br>message) to the specified remote Publisher PDP:|
||pdp broker sync pub <_IP Address of_<br>_Publisher PDP_>|
||n Send the synchronization request (in the next broker<br>message) to all remote Publisher PDPs:|
||pdp broker sync pub all|
||Control the schedule for synchronization with remote Publisher<br>PDPs:|
||pdp broker sync schedule {add <_option_> |<br>remove <_option_>| show <_option_>}|
||n To add new synchronization time:|
||pdp broker sync schedule add <_IP Address_<br>_of Publisher PDP_> "<_HH:MM_>"|
||n To remove the current schedule:|
||pdp broker sync schedule remove <_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_> "<_HH:MM_>"|
||n To show the current schedule:|
||pdp broker sync schedule show [<_IP_<br>_Address of Publisher PDP_>]|
||n Initiate the synchronization with the specified remote<br>Subscriber PDP:|
||pdp broker sync sub <_IP Address of_<br>_Subscriber PDP_>|
||n Initiate the synchronization with all remote Subscriber<br>PDPs:|
||pdp broker sync sub all|

### pdp debug

##### Description

Controls the debug of the PDP.

Syntax

pdp debug async1 ccc {off | on} memory off on reset rotate set < _Topic Name_ > < _Severity_ > spaces [<0 - 5>] stat unset < _Topic Name_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|async1|Tests theasynccommand line with theechocommand for 30<br>seconds.|
|ccc {off | on}|Configures whether to write the CCC debug logs into the PDP log<br>file -$FWDIR/log/pdpd.elg<br>n on- Writes the CCC debug logs<br>n off- Does not write the CCC debug logs|
|memory|Shows the memory consumption by the pdpd daemon.|
|off|Disables the PDP debug.|
|on|Enables the PDP debug.<br>Important- After you run this command "pdp debug on",<br>you must run the command "pdp debug set ..." to<br>configure the required filter.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|reset|Resets the PDP debug options for Debug Topic and Severity.<br>Important- After you run this command "pdp debug<br>reset", you must run the command "pdp debug off" to<br>turn off the debug.|
|rotate|Rotates the PDP log files - increases the index of each log file:<br>1. $FWDIR/log/pdpd.elgbecomes<br>$FWDIR/log/pdpd.elg.0<br>2. $FWDIR/log/pdpd.elg.0becomes<br>$FWDIR/log/pdpd.elg.1<br>3. And so on.|
|set <_Topic Name_><br><_Severity_>|Filters which debug logs PDP writes to the log file based on the<br>specified Debug Topics and Severity:<br>The available Debug Topics are:<br>n all<br>n Check<br>Point<br>Support<br>provides more specific topics, based<br>on the reported issue<br>The available Severities are:<br>n all<br>n critical<br>n events<br>n important<br>n surprise<br>Best Practice- We recommend to enable all Topics and all<br>Severities. Run:|
||pdp debug set all all|
|spaces [<0 - 5>]|Shows and configures the number of indentation spaces in the<br>$FWDIR/log/pdpd.elgfile.<br>You can specify the number of spaces:<br>n 0 (this is the default)<br>n 1<br>n 2<br>n 3<br>n 4<br>n 5|
|stat|Shows the PDP current debug status.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|unset <_Topic_<br>_Name_>|Unsets the specified Debug Topic(s).|


Important - When you enable the debug, it affects the performance of the pdpd daemon. Make sure to disable the debug after you complete your troubleshooting.

|<_options_>|The available <options> are:|

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|groups_update<br><_options_>|Shows and configures the automatic update of Identity Collector's<br>LDAP Groups.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n Perform "update all" to get the current LDAP group status:|
||pdp idc groups_update on|
||n Disable the feature (default):|
||pdp idc groups_update off|
||n Show the current status of the feature:|
||pdp idc groups_update status|
|muh <_options_>|Shows and configures the Multi-User Host detection.<br>The available <options> are:|

||pdp idc muh show|
||n Unmark an IP address as a Multi-User Host:|

##### Parameter

##### Description

service_ Important - This parameter is available in <u>R81 Jumbo Hotfix</u> accounts <u>Accumulator</u> starting from Take 51. < _options_ > Shows and configures the suspected Service Accounts. Important - This feature is enabled by default. The available <options> are:

- Show service account statistics -the current mode, known Service Accounts, and excluded accounts: pdp idc service_accounts show

- Configure the number of simultaneous logins (default is 100), after which all usernames are detected as Service Accounts: pdp idc service_accounts set_threshold <21000>

- Enable (this is the default) or disable the Prevent Mode (AutoExclude Mode): pdp idc service_accounts set_auto_ prevention {enable | disable} Notes: l If you disable the Prevent Mode, then Identity Collector works in the Detect Mode.

  - When you change the work mode from Detect to Prevent, all sessions that are marked as a Service Account are revoked.

- Mark specific usernames as a Service Account (if prevention is enabled, the sessions for these users are revoked): pdp idc service_accounts mark < _username_ >

- Configure specific usernames not to be detected as Service Accounts (continue to enforce identity): pdp idc service_accounts add_exception < _username_1_ > < _username_2_ > ... < _username_N_ >

- Configure specific usernames to be detected as Service Accounts, if users log in the specified number of times: pdp idc service_accounts delete_exception < _username_1_ > < _username_2_ > ... < _username_N_ >

- Remove specific usernames from the list of Service Accounts: pdp idc service_accounts unmark_service_ accounts


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
||Note- You must put at least one space between account<br>names. Do not put punctuation between account names.<br>n Remove all usernames from the list of Service Accounts:|
||pdp idc service_accounts unmark_service_<br>accounts_all|
|status|Shows the status of configured identity sources (Identity<br>Collectors).|

Considers<br>groups received from configured User Directories only if the<br>Identity Provider sends no group. ### pdp monitor

##### Description

Monitors the status of connected PDP sessions.

You can run different queries with the commands below to get the output, in which you are interested.

##### Syntax

pdp monitor all client_type < _Client Type_ > cv_ge < _Version_ > cv_le < _Version_ > groups < _Group Name_ > ip < _IP address_ > machine < _Computer Name_ > machine_exact mad network s_port summary user < _Username_ > user_exact

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|all|Shows information for all connected sessions.|
|client_type<br><_Client Type_>|Shows all sessions that connect through the specified client type.<br>Possible client types are:|
||n "AD Query"- User was identified by the AD Query.<br>n "Identity Agent"- User or computer was identified by an<br>Identity Awareness Agent.<br>n portal- User was identified by the Captive Portal.<br>n unknown- User was identified by an unknown source.|
|cv_ge<br><_Version_>|Shows all sessions that are connected with a client version that is<br>higher than (or equal to) the specified version.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|cv_le<br><_Version_>|Shows all sessions that are connected through a client version that is<br>lower than (or equal to) the specified version.|
|groups <_Group_<br>_Name_>|Shows all sessions of users or computers that are members of the<br>specified group.|
|ip <_IP_<br>_address_>|Shows session information for the specified IP address.|
|machine<br><_Computer_<br>_Name_>|Shows session information for the specified computer name.|
|machine_exact|Shows sessions filtered by the exact computer name.|
|mad|Shows all sessions that relate to a managed asset.<br>For example, all sessions that successfully performed computer<br>authentication.|
|network|Shows sessions filtered by a network wildcard.<br>For example:192.168.72.*|
|s_port|Shows sessions filtered by the assigned source port (MUH sessions<br>only).|
|summary|Shows the summary monitoring data.|
|user<br><_Username_>|Shows session information for the specified user name.|
|user_exact|Shows sessions filtered by the exact user.|


Example - Show the connected user behind the IP address 192.0.2.1

pdp monitor ip 192.0.2.1


Note - The last field "Published" indicates whether the session information was already published to the Gateway PEPs, whose IP addresses are listed.

### pdp nested_groups

##### Description

Configures the Security Gateway queries LDAP Nested Groups. Shows the current configuration LDAP Nested Group queries.

##### Syntax

pdp nested_groups auto_tune {enable | disable} clear depth < _options_ > disable enable show status __set_state < _options_ >


Important:

- In a Cluster, you must configure all the Cluster Members in the same way.

- On Scalable Platforms (Maestro and Chassis), you must run the applicable commands in the Expert mode on the applicable Security Group.


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|auto_tune<br>{enable |<br>disable}|Note- This feature is available only in the R81<br>Jumbo<br>Hotfix<br>Accumulator<br>Take 42 and higher.<br>Enables and disables the auto-tune feature.<br>This feature calculates and automatically selects the state of Nested<br>Groups based on the LDAP configuration on the Security Gateway and the<br>Management Server.<br>Notes:|
||n When you enable this feature, the Security Gateway<br>automatically configures the best the state of Nested Groups it<br>calculated.<br>n When you disable this feature, the Security Gateway<br>automatically returns to the state of Nested Groups you<br>configured earlier with the "__set_state" parameter.<br>Best Practice- Enable this feature on the Policy Decision Point (PDP)<br>to increase the performance.|
|clear|Clears the list of users, for which the depth was not enough.|
|depth <1 -<br>40>|Configures the nested groups depth (between 1 and 40).|
|disable|Disables the nested groups.|
|enable|Enables the nested groups.|
|show|Shows a list of users, for which the depth was not enough.|
|status|Shows the configuration status of nested groups.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|__set_<br>state {1 |<br>2 | 3 | 4}|Configures the nested groups state:<br>n 1- Recursive (this is the default)<br>l The Security Gateway queries each user to find out its group<br>memberships, and then queries each group recursively until it<br>determines the nested groups.<br>l We recommend this method for environments that have few<br>nested groups or no nested groups configured on the LDAP<br>server.<br>n 2- Per-user<br>l The Security Gateway sends one LDAP query. The response<br>includes all groups for the specified user, including the nesting<br>levels. The response includes all groups for the given user,<br>including nesting levels. This query shows groups from any<br>branch in the Active Directory forest. This type of query are sent<br>to the Global Catalog ports (TCP 3268 or 3269).<br>l We recommend this method for environments that have a policy<br>that includes access roles with nested groups in them.<br>l Use this state if you work with multiple branches in the account<br>unit, or if you use group membership cross-domain trees. For<br>example, a user belongs to the domain treeexample1.com<br>and belongs to the different domain treeexample2.com. See<br>sk134292<br>.<br>n 3- Multi per-group<br>l The Security Gateway sends one LDAP query. This LDAP<br>query includes a user and a group. The response shows if the<br>user is included in this group.<br>l We recommend this method for environments that have all<br>types of users and groups and have a small number of access<br>roles with nested groups in them.<br>n 4- Per user, if there is a single branch in each Account Unit<br>l The Security Gateway sends one LDAP query. The response<br>includes all groups for the specified user, including the nesting<br>levels. This query shows groups from the branch specified in<br>the LDAP account unit. This type of query can work over all<br>LDAP ports (TCP 3268 or 3269, TCP 389 or 636).<br>l Use this state if you work with a single branch on each account<br>unit.|

### pdp roles

###### General Syntax

pdp roles extract fetch < _options_ >

###### The 'pdp roles extract' command

##### Description

Extracts and shows the roles from the file $FWDIR/tmp/roles_command_output.txt that was created with the "pdp roles fetch" command.

##### Syntax

pdp roles extract

###### The 'pdp roles fetch' command

##### Description

Fetches the roles that match the provided Access Role information and saves the output in the $FWDIR/tmp/roles_command_output.txt file.

##### Syntax

pdp roles fetch [-ip < _IP Address_ >] -u "< _Username_ >" -is "< _Identity Source_ >" -ug "< _User Group 1_ >","< _User Group 2_ >",... -mg "< _Machine Group 1_ >","< _Machine Group 2_ >",...


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-ip <_IP Address_>|Optional.<br>Specifies the IP address of identity, host, or session to<br>calculate and fetch Access Roles that also contain explicitly<br>selected objects in theNetworkspane.<br>Example for an Access Role object, in which a Host object with<br>the IPv4 address 5.5.5.5 was selected in theNetworkspane:|
||pdp roles fetch -i 5.5.5.5 -u "user_1" -is<br>"AD_Query"|
|-u "<_Username_>" -is<br>"<_Identity Source_>"|Specifies the username and the identity source.<br>The available identity sources are (case-sensitive):<br>n portal<br>n Identity_Agent<br>n Remote_Access<br>n AD_Query<br>n IFMAP<br>n Terminal_Server_Identity_Agent<br>n Radius_Accounting<br>Important- If in the Access Role object you explicitly<br>selected objects in theNetworksandUserspanes, you<br>must also use the parameter "-ip <_IP Address_>".<br>Examples:|
||pdp roles fetch -u "user_1" -is "AD_Query"|
||pdp roles fetch -i 5.5.5.5 -u "user_1" -is<br>"AD_Query"|
|-ug "<_User Group_<br>_1_>","<_User Group_<br>_2_>",...|Specifies the user group.<br>Enter the comma separated list of group names.<br>For Active Directory groups, you must enter the prefix "ad_<br>group_".<br>Example for an AD group called "LaptopUsers":|
||pdp roles fetch -ug "ad_group_LaptopUsers"|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-mg "<_Machine Group_|Specifies the machine group.|
|_1_>","<_Machine Group_|Enter the comma separated list of group names.|
|_2_>", ...|For Active Directory groups, you must enter the prefix "ad_<br>group_".<br>Example for an AD group called "Laptops":|
||pdp roles fetch -mg "ad_group_Laptops"|

## pep

##### Description

Provides commands to control and monitor the PEPD process (see below for options).

##### Syntax

pep < _command_ > [< _parameter_ > [< _option_ >]]

##### Commands

|Command|Description|
|---|---|
|control <_parameter_>|Controls the PEP parameters.|
|<_option_>|See"pep control" on page 1614.|
|debug <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Controls the PEP debug.<br>See"pep debug" on page 1615.|
|show <_parameter_><br><_option_>|Shows PEP information.<br>See"pep show" on page 1617.|
|tracker <_parameter_>|During the PEP debug, adds theTRACKERdebug topic to<br>the PEP logs.<br>See"pep tracker" on page 1620.|


### pep control

##### Description

Provides commands to control the PEP.

##### Syntax

pep control extended_info_storage < _options_ > portal_dual_stack < _options_ > tasks_manager status < _options_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|extended_info_storage<br><_options_>|Controls whether PEP stores the extended identities<br>information for debug.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n disable- PEP does not store the information.<br>n enable- PEP stores the information.|
|portal_dual_stack<br><_options_>|Controls the support for portal dual stack (IPv4 and IPv6).<br>The available <options> are:|
||n disable- Disables the support.<br>n enable- Enables the support.|
|tasks_manager<br><_options_>|Shows the status of the PEP tasks (current running,<br>previous, and pending tasks).<br>The available <options> are:<br>n status- Shows the status.|


### pep debug

##### Description

Controls the debug of the PEP.

##### Syntax

pep debug memory off on reset rotate set < _options_ > spaces [< _options_ >] stat unset < _options_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|memory|Displays the memory consumption by the pepd daemon.|
|off|Disables the PEP debug.|
|on|Enables the PEP debug.<br>Important- After you run this command "pep debug on",<br>you must run the command "pep debug set ..." to<br>determine the required filter.|
|reset|Resets the PEP debug options for Debug Topics and Severities.<br>Important- After you run this command "pep debug<br>reset ...", you must run the command "pep debug<br>off" to turn off the debug.|
|rotate|Rotates the PEP log files - increases the index of each log file:<br>n $FWDIR/log/pepd.elgbecomes<br>$FWDIR/log/pepd.elg.0,<br>n $FWDIR/log/pepd.elg.0becomes<br>$FWDIR/log/pepd.elg.1<br>n And so on.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|set <_Topic Name_><br><_Severity_>|Filters which debug logs PEP writes to the log file based on the<br>specified Debug Topics and Severity.<br>Available Debug Topics are:<br>n all<br>n Check Point Support provides more specific topics, based<br>on the reported issue<br>Available Severities are:<br>n all<br>n critical<br>n events<br>n important<br>n surprise<br>Best Practice- We recommend to enable all Topics and all<br>Severities. Run:|
||pep debug set all all|
|spaces<br>[0 | 1 | 2 |<br>3 | 4 | 5]|Displays and sets the number of indentation spaces in the<br>$FWDIR/log/pepd.elgfile.<br>The default is 0 spaces.|
|stat|Shows the PEP current debug status.|
|unset <_Topic Name_>|Unsets the specified Debug Topic(s).|


Important - When you enable the debug, it affects the performance of the pepd daemon. Make sure to turn off the debug after you complete your troubleshooting.


### pep show

##### Description

Shows information about PEP.

##### Syntax

pep show conciliation_clashes all clear ip < _Session IP Address_ > network pdp registration pdp all id < _ID of PDP_ > stat topology_map user all query cid < _IP_ [, _ID_ ]> cmp < _Compliance_ > mchn < _Computer Name_ > mgrp < _Group_ > pdp < _IP_ [, _ID_ ]> role < _Identity Role_ > ugrp < _Group_ > uid < _UID String_ > usr < _Username_ >


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|conciliation_<br>clashes <_options_>|Shows session conciliation clashes.<br>The available <options> are:<br>n all- Show all conciliation clashes.<br>n clear- Clears all session clashes.<br>n ip <_Session IP Address_>- Show all conciliation<br>clashes filtered by the specified session IP address.|
|network <_options_>|Shows network related information.<br>The available <options> are:|
||n pdp- Shows the Network-to-PDP mapping table.<br>n registration- Shows the networks registration table.|
|pdp <_options_>|Shows the communication channel between the PEP and the<br>PDP.<br>Available <options> are:|
||n all- Shows all connected PDPs.<br>n id- Shows the information for the specified PDP.|
|stat|Shows the last time the pepd daemon was started and the last<br>time a policy was received.<br>Important- Each time the pepd daemon starts, it loads the<br>policy and the two timers. The times between the pepd<br>daemon start and when it fetched the policy are very close.|
|topology_map|Shows topology of all PDP and PEP addresses.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|user <_options_>|Shows the status of sessions that PEP knows.<br>You can perform various queries to get the applicable output<br>(see below).<br>The available <options> are:<br>n all- Shows the list of all clients.<br>n query- Queries the list of users based on the specified<br>filters:<br>l cid <_IP_[,_ID_]>- Matches entries of clients with<br>the specified Client ID.<br>l cmp <Compliance>- Matches entries with the<br>specified compliance.<br>l mchn <_Computer Name_>- Matches entries with<br>the specified computer name.<br>l mgrp <_Group_>- Matches entries with the specified<br>machine group.<br>l pdp <_IP_[,_ID_]>- Matches entries, which the<br>specified PDP updated.<br>l role <_Identity Role_>- Matches entries with<br>the specified identity role.<br>l ugrp <_Group_>- Matches entries with the specified<br>user group.<br>l uid <_UID String_>- Matches entries with the<br>specified full or partial UID.<br>l usr <_Username_>- Matches entries with the<br>specified username.<br>Note- You can use multiple query filters at the same<br>time to create a logical AND correlation between<br>them.<br>For example, to show all users that have a sub-string<br>of "jo" AND are part of the user group "Employees"<br>you can use this query syntax:|
||# pep show user query usr jo ugrp<br>Employees|
