|vd <_Name_<br>_of Virtual_<br>_Device_<br>_Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual Device object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first command in a<br>transaction.|
|name <_Name_<br>_of_<br>_Interface_>|Interface name|Specifies the name of the physical or VLAN interface.<br>Note- You must use the "name" or "leads_to"<br>parameter, but not both.|
|leads_to<br><_Name of_|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual Switch or Virtual<br>Router object, to which this interface connects.|
|_VSW or VR_||This parameter is applicable only for a Virtual System.|
|_Object_>||Note- You must use the "name" or "leads_to"<br>parameter, but not both.|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|ip <_IPv4_<br>_Address_><br>{/<_IPv4_<br>_Prefix_> |<br>netmask<br><_IPv4_<br>_Netmask_> |<br>prefix<br><_IPv4_<br>_Prefix_>}|IPv4<br>configuration|Specifies the IPv4 settings:<br>n <_IPv4 Address_>- IPv4 address<br>n <_IPv4 Prefix_>- Integer between 1 and 32<br>n <_IPv4 Netmask_>- Number in a format<br>X.X.X.X<br>This parameter is applicable only for a:<br>n Virtual System<br>n Virtual Router<br>For interfaces on a Virtual System that connect to a<br>Virtual Router, you must use the possible maximum<br>for the IPv4 address family:<br>n Netmask 255.255.255.255<br>n Prefix 32|
|ip6 <_IPv6_<br>_Address_><br>{/<_IPv6_<br>_Prefix_> |<br>netmask6<br><_IPv6_<br>_Netmask_> |<br>prefix6<br><_IPv6_<br>_Prefix_>}|IPv6<br>configuration|Specifies the IPv6 settings:<br>n <_IPv6 Address_> - IPv6 address<br>n <_IPv6 Prefix_>- Integer between 64 and 128<br>n <_IPv6 Netmask_>- Number in a format<br>XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:<br>XXXX<br>This parameter is applicable only for a:<br>n Virtual System<br>n Virtual Router<br>For interfaces on a Virtual System that connect to a<br>Virtual Router, you must use the possible maximum<br>for the IPv6 address family:<br>n Netmask<br>FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFF<br>F<br>n Prefix 128|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|propagate<br>{true |<br>false}|n true<br>n false|Controls how to propagate the IPv4 routes to adjacent<br>Virtual Devices:<br>n true- Propagate the IPv4 routes<br>n false- Do not propagate the IPv4 routes<br>(default)<br>Note- This parameter is applicable only for a<br>Virtual System with VLAN or physical interfaces.|
|propagate6<br>{true |<br>false}|n true<br>n false|Controls how to propagate the IPv6 routes to adjacent<br>Virtual Devices:<br>n true- Propagate the IPv6 routes<br>n false- Do not propagate the IPv6 routes<br>(default)<br>Note- This parameter is applicable only for a<br>Virtual System with VLAN or physical interfaces.|
|topology<br>{external<br>||n external<br>n interna<br>l|Specifies the Topology configuration of the interface:<br>n external- External interface.|
|internal_<br>undefined<br>|<br>internal_<br>this_<br>network |<br>internal_<br>specific }|_<br>undefine<br>d<br>n interna<br>l_this_<br>network<br>n interna<br>l_<br>specific|n internal_undefined- Internal interface with<br>undefined topology. This is the default for a<br>Virtual System in Bridge Mode.<br>n internal_this_network- Internal interface.<br>This is the default for a Virtual System and<br>Virtual Router. Virtual System in Bridge Mode<br>does not support this topology.<br>n internal_specific [specific_group<br><_Name of Network Group Object_>]-<br>Internal interface with topology defined by the<br>specified Network Group object.<br>This parameter is applicable only for a:<br>n Virtual System<br>n Virtual System in Bridge Mode<br>n Virtual Router|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|specific_<br>group<br><_Network_<br>_Group_<br>_Object_<br>_Name_>|Name of Network<br>Group Object|If you specified the "topology internal_<br>specific" parameter, then specify the name of the<br>Network Group object that contains the applicable<br>Network objects.<br>Note- This parameter is applicable only if you<br>disable the automatic topology calculation with<br>the "set vd ... calc_topo_auto false"<br>command (see"Modifying Settings of a Virtual<br>Device" on page 1791).|
|mtu <_MTU_>|Integer|Specifies the MTU value for this interface.<br>Default is 1500 bytes.<br>This parameter is applicable only for a:<br>n Virtual System<br>n Virtual Router|


##### Example - Add VLAN interface eth4.100 with IPv4 1.1.1.1/24 to the Virtual System 'VirtSystem1'

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o add interface vd VirtSystem1 name eth4.100 ip 1.1.1.1/24


#### Adding a Bridge Interface to a Virtual System

##### Description

Some Software Blades and features are not supported on a Virtual System in Bridge Mode, because it may not have an IP address.

For example: Threat Emulation, Identity Awareness, Identity Awareness Captive Portal, and UserCheck Portal are not supported.

This command adds a Bridge interface to an existing regular Virtual System object that always has an IP address.

As a result, the Virtual System can support these Software Blades and features for the traffic that passes over the configured bridge interface.


##### Notes:

- Names of bridge interfaces have a template "br _X_ ", where "X" is a digit.

- It is necessary to add subordinate interfaces in pairs to a bridge interface.

- To see the bridge interfaces you configured in the Virtual System object:

   1. Connect to the command line on the VSX Gateway (each VSX Cluster Member).

   2. Log in to the Expert mode.

   3. Go to the context of the Virtual System:

      - vsenv < _VSID_ >

   4. Examine the list of interfaces:

      - ifconfig

- You can delete bridge interfaces from a Virtual System either in SmartConsole, or with the "vsx_provisioning_tool" command (see "Removing an Interface from a Virtual Device" on page 1802).

##### Syntax

attach bridge vd < _Name of Virtual System Object_ > ifs1 < _Name of First Subordinate Interface_ > ifs2 < _Name of Second Subordinate Interface_ >


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of Virtual_<br>_System Object_>|Object<br>name|Specifies the name of the Virtual System<br>object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first<br>command in a transaction.|
|ifs1 <_Name of First_<br>_Subordinate_<br>_Interface_>|Interface<br>name|Specifies the name of the physical interface to<br>be the first subordinate interface of a bridge<br>interface.<br>Note- This physical interface must not<br>have an IP address|
|ifs2 <_Name of First_<br>_Second Interface_>|Interface<br>name|Specifies the name of the physical interface to<br>be the second subordinate interface of a bridge<br>interface.<br>Note- This physical interface must not<br>have an IP address|


##### Example 1 - Adding a Bridge interface with subordinate interfaces "eth2" and "eth3" in the Virtual System "VS1"

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o attach bridge vd VS1 ifs1 eth2 ifs2 eth3

##### Example 2 - Adding a Multi Bridge interface in the Virtual System "VS1"

In this example, we add pairs of VLAN interfaces to the Virtual System "VS1" to add a Multi Bridge interface (for more information, see the <u>R81VSXAdministration Guide</u> > section "Virtual System in Bridge Mode"):

> - VLANs eth2.403 and eth3.403 as the first bridge interface

> - VLANs eth2.504 and eth3.504 as the second bridge interface

The prerequisite is to configure both physical interfaces "eth2" and "eth3" as VLAN Trunks (see "Configuring a Physical Interface as VLAN Trunk" on page 1808).

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o attach bridge vd VS1 ifs1 eth2.403 ifs2 eth3.403, attach bridge ifs1 eth2.504 ifs2 eth3.504


#### Adding a VPN Tunnel Interface to a Virtual Device

##### Description

Virtual Tunnel Interface (VTI) is a virtual interface that is used for establishing a Route-Based VPN tunnel.

This command adds a VTI to an existing Virtual System object.

The VPN tunnel and its properties are defined by the VPN community that contains the two Security Gateways.

You must define the VPN community and its member Security Gateways before you can create a VTI.

To learn more about Route Based VPN, see the <u>R81Site to Site VPNAdministration Guide</u> > Chapter Route Based VPN.

##### Syntax

add interface vd < _Name of Virtual System Object_ > vpn_tunnel numbered peer < _Name of VPN Peer Object_ > local < _Tunnel Local IP_ > remote < _Tunnel Remote IP_ > [tunnel_id < _Tunnel ID_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of Virtual_<br>_System Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual<br>System object (as configured in<br>SmartConsole).<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first<br>command in a transaction.|
|vpn_tunnel numbered|n true<br>n false|Specifies the type of the VPN tunnel as<br>numbered.<br>Uses a specified, static IPv4 addresses<br>for local and remote connections.|
|peer <_Name of VPN Peer_<br>_Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the remote peer<br>object as defined in the VPN community<br>in SmartConsole.|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|local <_Tunnel Local_<br>_IP_> remote <_Tunnel_<br>_Remote IP_>|IPv4<br>configuration|Specifies the IPv4 addresses in dotted<br>decimal format for the VPN tunnel<br>endpoints:<br>n local <_Tunnel Local IP_>-<br>IPv4 address of the VPN tunnel on<br>this Virtual System<br>n remote <_Tunnel Remote IP_><br>- IPv4 address of the VPN tunnel<br>on the remote VPN peer<br>Applies to the Numbered VTI only.|
|tunnel_id <_Tunnel ID_>|Integer|Specifies the unique Tunnel ID (integer<br>from 1 to 32768).<br>Note- If the specified ID is already<br>used by another VPN tunnel on this<br>VSX Gateway or VSX Cluster<br>Member, this parameter is ignored<br>and the next available ID is used<br>instead.|


##### Example - Numbered VTI

vsx_provisioning_tool -o add interface vd vs1 vpn_tunnel numbered peer AWS_Peer local 169.254.46.238 remote 169.254.46.237 tunnel_id 10


#### Removing an Interface from a Virtual Device

##### Description

This command removes an interface from an existing Virtual Device object:

- Virtual System

- Virtual System in Bridge Mode

- Virtual Switch

- Virtual Router


##### Important:

- If the interface you remove leads to a Virtual Router, all routes through that interface are removed automatically.

- You must remove all subordinate interfaces of a bridge interface in the same transaction. This also removes the bridge interface.


Note - If there are routes that have a next-hop IP address, which would become inaccessible without this interface, the transaction fails.

##### Syntax

remove interface vd < _Name of Virtual Device Object_ > {name _<Name of Interface>_ | leads_to < _Name of VSW or VR Object_ >}


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of_<br>_Virtual Device_<br>_Object_>|Object<br>name|Specifies the name of the Virtual Device object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first command<br>in a transaction.|
|name <_<Name of_<br>_Interface>_>|Interface<br>name|Specifies the name of the physical or VLAN<br>interface.<br>Note- You must use the "name" or "leads_<br>to" parameter, but not both.|
|leads_to <_Name of_<br>_VSW or VR Object_>|Object<br>name|Specifies the name of the Virtual Switch or Virtual<br>Router object, to which this interface connects.<br>This parameter is applicable only for a Virtual<br>System.<br>Note- You must use the "name" or "leads_<br>to" parameter, but not both.|


##### Example 1 - Removing a VLAN interface from a Virtual System "VS1"

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o remove interface vd VS1 name eth4.100

##### Example 2 - Removing all subordinate interfaces "eth2" and "eth3" of a bridge interface in the Virtual System "VS1"

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o remove interface vd VS1 name eth2, remove interface vd VS1 name eth3


#### Modifying Settings of an Interface

##### Description

This command changes the settings of an interface that belongs to an existing Virtual Device object:

- Virtual System

- Virtual System in Bridge Mode

- Virtual Switch

- Virtual Router


Note - You cannot change or remove the IP address or netmask of an existing interface with this command. You can remove the interface and add a new interface with a different IP address, but not all the previous interface settings are kept.

##### Syntax

set interface vd < _Name of Virtual Device Object_ > {name < _Name of Interface_ > [new_name < _Name of New Interface_ >] | leads_to < _Name of VSW or VR Object_ > [new_leads_to < _Name of New VSW or VR Object_ >]} [propagate {true | false}] [propagate6 {true | false}] [topology {external | internal_undefined | internal_this_network | internal_ specific [specific_group < _Network Group Object Name_ >]}] [mtu < _MTU_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of Virtual_<br>_Device Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual<br>Device object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the<br>first command in a transaction.|
|name <_Name of_<br>_Interface_>|Interface name|Specifies the name of the physical<br>or VLAN interface.|
|||Note- You must use the "name"<br>or "leads_to" parameter, but<br>not both.|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|new_name <_Name of New_<br>_Interface_>|Interface name|You can change the name, but not<br>the type of interface.<br>Note- You can change a VLAN<br>or physical interface only to a<br>VLAN or physical interface.|
|leads_to <_Name of VSW_<br>_or VR Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual<br>Switch or Virtual Router object, to<br>which this interface connects.<br>This parameter is applicable only for<br>a Virtual System.<br>Note- You must use the "name"<br>or "leads_to" parameter, but<br>not both.|
|new_leads_to <_Name of_<br>_New VSW or VR Object_>|Object name|You can where the interface leads:<br>n You can change an interface<br>that leads to a Virtual Switch<br>only to lead to a different<br>Virtual Switch.<br>n You can change an interface<br>that leads to a Virtual Router<br>only to lead to a different<br>Virtual Router.|
|propagate {true |<br>false}|n true<br>n false|Controls how to propagate the IPv4<br>routes to adjacent Virtual Devices:<br>n true- Propagate the IPv4<br>routes<br>n false- Do not propagate the<br>IPv4 routes (default)<br>Note- This parameter is<br>applicable only for a Virtual<br>System with VLAN or physical<br>interfaces.|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|propagate6 {true |<br>false}|n true<br>n false|Controls how to propagate the IPv6<br>routes to adjacent Virtual Devices:<br>n true- Propagate the IPv6<br>routes<br>n false- Do not propagate the<br>IPv6 routes (default)<br>Note- This parameter is<br>applicable only for a Virtual<br>System with VLAN or physical<br>interfaces.|
|topology {external |<br>internal_undefined |<br>internal_this_network<br>| internal_specific}|n external<br>n internal_<br>undefined<br>n internal_<br>this_<br>network<br>n internal_<br>specific|Specifies the Topology configuration<br>of the interface:<br>n external- External<br>interface.<br>n internal_undefined-<br>Internal interface with<br>undefined topology. This is the<br>default for Virtual System in<br>Bridge Mode.<br>n internal_this_network-<br>Internal interface. This is the<br>default for Virtual System and<br>Virtual Router. Virtual System<br>in Bridge Mode does not<br>support this topology.<br>n internal_specific<br>[specific_group<br><_Network Group Object_<br>_Name_>]- Internal interface<br>with topology defined by the<br>specified Network Group<br>object.<br>This parameter is applicable only for<br>a:<br>n Virtual System<br>n Virtual System in Bridge Mode<br>n Virtual Router|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|specific_group<br><_Network Group Object_<br>_Name_>|Name of Network<br>Group Object|If you specified the "topology<br>internal_specific" parameter,<br>then specify the name of the<br>Network Group object that contains<br>the applicable Network objects.<br>Note- This parameter is<br>applicable only if you disable<br>the automatic topology<br>calculation with the "set vd<br>... calc_topo_auto<br>false" command (see<br>"Modifying Settings of a Virtual<br>Device" on page 1791).|
|mtu <_MTU_>|Integer|Specifies the MTU value for this<br>interface.<br>Default is 1500 bytes.<br>This parameter is applicable only<br>for:|
|||n Virtual System<br>n Virtual Router|


##### Example - On the Virtual System "VS1", change the VLAN interface eth4.10 to the physical interface eth5

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o set interface vd VS1 name eth4.100 new_name eth5 propagate true topology internal_specific specific_group NYGWs


#### Configuring a Physical Interface as VLAN Trunk

##### Description

This command configures a physical interface as VLAN Trunk.

This is required to configure VLAN interfaces the physical interface.


Important - Make sure the physical interface you configure as VLAN Trunk does not have an IP address.

##### Syntax

set physical_interface vd < _Name of VSX Gateway or VSX Cluster Object_ > name < _Name of Interface_ > vlan_trunk {true | false}

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of VSX Gateway or_<br>_VSX Cluster Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the VSX<br>Gateway or VSX Cluster object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the<br>first command in a transaction.|
|name <_Name of Interface_>|Interface name|Specifies the name of the physical<br>interface.|
|vlan_trunk {true | false}|n true<br>n false|Controls whether this physical<br>interface is a VLAN Trunk:|
|||n true- VLAN Trunk interface<br>n false- Regular physical<br>interface (default)|


##### Example - On the VSX Gateway "VSX1" configure the physical interface eth2 as VLAN Trunk

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o set physical_interface vd VSX1 name eth2 vlan_trunk true


#### Adding a Route

##### Description

This command adds an IPv4 or IPv6 route to an existing Virtual System or Virtual Router object.


Note - This command detects IPv4 and IPv6 automatically.

##### Syntax

add route vd < _Name of VS or VR Object_ > destination {< _IP Address_ > [/< _IP Prefix_ >] | default | default6} [{netmask < _IP Netmask_ > | prefix < _IP Prefix_ >}] {next_hop < _Next Hop IP Address_ > | leads_to < _Name of VS or VR Object_ >} [propagate {true | false}]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of_<br>_VS or VR_<br>_Object_>|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual System or Virtual<br>Router object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first command in a<br>transaction.|
|destination<br>{<_IP_<br>_Address_><br>[/<_IP_<br>_Prefix_>] |<br>default |<br>default6}|See the<br>Notes<br>column on<br>the right|Specifies the route destination settings:<br>n <_IP Address_>- IPv4 or IPv6 address<br>n <_IP Prefix_>-<br>l For IPv4 - Integer between 1 and 32<br>l For IPv6 - Integer between 64 and 128<br>n default- Use the default IPv4 route<br>n default6- Use the default IPv6 route|
|netmask <_IP_<br>_Netmask_>|Number|Specifies an IP Netmask:<br>n For IPv4 - Number in a format X.X.X.X<br>n For IPv6 - Number in a format<br>XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XX<br>XX|
|prefix <_IP_<br>_Prefix_>|Integer|Specifies the IP address prefix length:<br>n For IPv4 - Integer between 1 and 32<br>n For IPv6 - Integer between 64 and 128|


|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|next_hop<br><_Next Hop_<br>_IP Address_>|IP Address|Specifies the IP address of the next hop of the route.<br>Notes:<br>n This IP address must be on a subnet of an<br>existing interface.<br>n You must use the "next_hop" or "leads_<br>to" parameter, but not both.|
|leads_to<br><_Name of VS_<br>_or VR_|Object name|Specifies the name of the Virtual System or Virtual<br>Router object, which is the next hop for the configured<br>route.|
|_Object_>||Note- You must use the "next_hop" or "leads_<br>to" parameter, but not both.|
|propagate<br>{true |<br>false}|n true<br>n false|Controls how to propagate the IP routes to adjacent<br>Virtual Devices:<br>n true- Propagate the IP routes<br>n false- Do not propagate the IP routes (default)<br>Note- The "propagate" parameter is applicable<br>only if you specified the "next_hop" parameter.|


Example - Adding a route on the Virtual System "VS1" that uses the default IPv4 route as a destination and the Virtual Router "VR3" as a next hop

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o add route vd VS1 destination default leads_to VR3


#### Removing a Route

##### Description

This command removes an IPv4 or IPv6 route from an existing Virtual System or Virtual Router object.


Note - This command detects IPv4 and IPv6 automatically.

##### Syntax

remove route vd < _Name of VS or VR Object_ > destination {< _IP Address_ >[/< _IP Prefix_ >] | default | default6} [{netmask < _IP Netmask_ > | prefix < _IP Prefix_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of_<br>_VS or VR_<br>_Object_>|Object<br>name|Specifies the name of the Virtual System or Virtual Router<br>object.<br>Mandatory parameter, if this is the first command in a<br>transaction.|
|destination<br>{<_IP_<br>_Address_><br>[/<_IP_<br>_Prefix_>] |<br>default |<br>default6}|See the<br>Notes<br>column<br>on the<br>right|Specifies the route destination settings:<br>n <_IP Address_>- IPv4 or IPv6 address<br>n <_IP Prefix_>-<br>l For IPv4 - Integer between 1 and 32<br>l For IPv6 - Integer between 64 and 128<br>n default- Use the default IPv4 route<br>n default6- Use the default IPv6 route|
|netmask <_IP_<br>_Netmask_>|Number|Specifies an IP Netmask:<br>n For IPv4 - Number in a format X.X.X.X<br>n For IPv6 - Number in a format<br>XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX:XXXX|
|prefix <_IP_<br>_Prefix_>|Integer|Specifies the IP address prefix length:<br>n For IPv4 - Integer between 1 and 32<br>n For IPv6 - Integer between 64 and 128|


##### Example - Removing a route from the Virtual System "VS1" that uses the default IPv6 route as a destination

vsx_provisioning_tool -s localhost -u admin -p mypassword -o remove route vd VS1 destination default6


#### Showing Virtual Device Data

##### Description

This command shows the information about an existing Virtual Device object.

##### Syntax

show vd name < _Name of Virtual Device Object_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Value|Notes|
|---|---|---|
|vd <_Name of Virtual_|Name of the|Specifies the name of the Virtual|
|_Device Object_>|Virtual Device|Device object.<br>Mandatory parameter.|


##### Comments

- The command shows only non-automatic routes.

- The command does not show routes that are created automatically with route propagation.

- For a Virtual Router and Virtual Switch:

The command does not show the wrpj interfaces (created automatically) that connect to Virtual Systems.


### Script Examples


Note - Line numbers in the left column are written only to make it easier to read the script examples.

#### Example 1

Create a Virtual System connected to a Virtual Router.

Add a default route on the Virtual System that routes the traffic to the Virtual Router.

Add applicable routes on the Virtual Router to route the traffic to the Virtual System.

|Line|Command|
|---|---|
|1|transaction begin|
|2|add vd name VR1 vsx VSX1 type vr|
|3|add interface name eth3.100 ip 10.0.0.1/24|
|4|transaction end|
|5|transaction begin|
|6|add vd name VR2 vsx VSX2 type vr|
|7|add interface name eth3.200 ip 20.0.0.1/24|
|8|transaction end|
|9|transaction begin|
|10|add vd name VS1 vsx VSX1|
|11|add interface leads_to VR1 ip 192.168.1.1/32|
|12|add interface name eth4.20 ip 192.168.20.1/24 propagate<br>true|
|13|add route destination default leads_to VR1|
|14|add route destination 192.168.40.0/25 next_hop<br>192.168.20.254|
|15|transaction end|


#### Example 2

Create a Virtual System connected to a Virtual Switch, with manual topology.

|Line|Command|
|---|---|
|1|transaction begin|
|2|add vd name VSW1 vsx VSX1 type vsw vs_mtu 1400|
|3|add interface name eth3.100|
|4|transaction end|
|5|transaction begin|
|6|add vd name VS1 vsx VSX1 calc_topo_auto false|
|7|add interface leads_to VSW1 ip 10.0.0.1/24 ip6 2001::1/64<br>topology external|
|8|add interface name eth4.20 ip 192.168.20.1/25 ip6<br>2020::1/64 topology internal_this_network|
|9|add route destination default next_hop 10.0.0.254|
|10|add route destination default6 next_hop 2001::254|
|11|transaction end|


#### Example 3

Add CoreXL Firewall instances to the Virtual System made in the last example.

Turn on automatic calculation of topology.

Change the name of the internal interface, and decrease its MTU.

|Line|Command|
|---|---|
|1|transaction begin|
|2|set vd name VS1 instances 4 instances6 2 calc_topo_auto<br>true|
|3|set interface name eth4.20 new_name eth4.21 mtu 1400|
|4|transaction end|


# QoS Commands

For more information about QoS, see the <u>R81QoSAdministration Guide.</u>


## etmstart

##### Description

Starts the QoS Software Blade on the Security Gateway - starts the QoS daemon fgd50, and fetches the QoS policy from the Management Servers configured in the $FWDIR/conf/masters file on the Security Gateway.

For more information, see:

> - <u>R81QoSAdministration Guide</u>

> - <u>sk41585: How to control and debug FloodGate-1 (QoS)</u>

##### Syntax

etmstart

##### Example

[Expert@MyGW:0]# etmstart QoS: Starting fgd50

QoS: Fetching QoS Policy from masters Fetching QoS Software Blade Policy: Received Policy. Downloading...

eth0(inbound), eth0(outbound). Download OK. Done. QoS started [Expert@MyGW:0]#


## etmstop

##### Description

Stops the QoS Software Blade on the Security Gateway - kills the QoS daemon fgd50 and then unloads the QoS policy.

For more information, see:

> - <u>R81QoSAdministration Guide</u>

> - <u>sk41585: How to control and debug FloodGate-1 (QoS)</u>

##### Syntax

etmstop

##### Example

[Expert@CXL1_192.168.3.52:0]# etmstop Unloading QoS Policy: Target(s): CXL1_192.168.3.52 CXL1_192.168.3.52: QoS policy unloaded successfully. Done. QoS stopped

[Expert@CXL1_192.168.3.52:0]#


## fgate

This section describes:

The 'fgate' command on Management Server

##### Description

Installs and uninstalls the QoS policy on the managed Security Gateways. Shows the status of the QoS Software Blade on the managed Security Gateways.

For more information, see:

> - <u>R81QoSAdministration Guide</u>

> - <u>sk41585: How to control and debug FloodGate-1 (QoS)</u>

##### Syntax

fgate [-d] load < _Name of QoS Policy_ >.F < _GW1_ > < _GW2_ > ... < _GWN_ > stat -h < _GW1_ > < _GW2_ > ... < _GWN_ > unload < _GW1_ > < _GW2_ > ... < _GWN_ > ver

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then redirect<br>the output to a file, or use the script<br>command to save<br>the entire CLI session.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|load <_Name of QoS_<br>_Policy_>.F <_GW1_><br><_GW2_> ... <_GWN_>|Runs a verifier on the QoS policy <Name_of_QoS_Policy>.<br>If the QoS policy is valid, the Management Server compiles<br>and installs the QoS Policy on the specified Security<br>Gateways<_GW1_> <_GW2_> ... <_GWN_>.<br>Notes:<br>n The maximal supported length of the <Name of<br>QoS Policy> string is 32 characters.<br>n To specify a Security Gateway, enter the main IP<br>address of the name of its object as configured in<br>SmartConsole. You can specify several Security<br>Gateways or cluster members in the same<br>command.|
|stat -h|Shows the built-in usage for the "stat" parameter.|
|stat <_GW1_> <_GW2_><br>... <_GWN_>|Shows the status of the QoS Software Blade and policy on<br>the managed Security Gateways.<br>Note- To specify a Security Gateway, enter the main IP<br>address of the name of its object as configured in<br>SmartConsole. You can specify several Security<br>Gateways or cluster members in the same command.<br>Important- This command is outdated and exists only<br>for backward compatibility with very old versions. Use<br>the ""cpstat" on page 956" command.|
|unload <_GW1_> <_GW2_><br>... <_GWN_>|Uninstalls the QoS Policy from the specified Security<br>Gateways<_GW1_> <_GW2_> ... <_GWN_>.<br>Note- To specify a Security Gateway, enter the main IP<br>address of the name of its object as configured in<br>SmartConsole. You can specify several Security<br>Gateways or cluster members in the same command.|
|ver|Shows the QoS Software Blade version on the Management<br>Server.|


##### Examples

###### Example 1 - Installing the QoS policy on one Security Gateway specified by its IP address

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fgate load MyPolicy.F 192.168.3.52 QoS rules verified OK! Downloading QoS Policy: MyPolicy.F... Target(s): MyGW MyGW: QoS policy transferred to module: MyGW. MyGW: QoS policy installed succesfully. Done. [Expert@MGMT:0]#

###### Example 2 - Installing the QoS policy on two cluster members specified by their object names

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fgate load MyPolicy.F MyClusterMember1 MyClusterMember2 QoS rules verified OK! Downloading QoS Policy: MyPolicy.F... MyClusterMember1: QoS policy transferred to module: MyClusterMember1. MyClusterMember1: QoS policy installed succesfully. MyClusterMember2: QoS policy transferred to module: MyClusterMember2. MyClusterMember2: QoS policy installed succesfully. Done.

[Expert@MGMT:0]#

###### Example 3 - Viewing the QoS status on one Security Gateway specified by its object name

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fgate stat MyGW Module name: MyGW ======================= Product: QoS Software Blade Version: R81 Kernel Build: 456 Policy Name: MyPolicy Install time: Wed Dec 4 19:53:48 2019 Interfaces Num: 1 Interface table ---------------------------------------------------------------|Name|Dir|Limit (Bps)|Avg Rate (Bps)|Conns|Pend pkts|Pend bytes| ---------------------------------------------------------------|eth0|in | 1250000000| 0| 0| 0| 0| |eth0|out| 1250000000| 0| 0| 0| 0| ---------------------------------------------------------------[Expert@MGMT:0]#

###### Example 4 - Viewing the QoS Software Blade version

[Expert@MGMT:0]# fgate ver This is Check Point QoS Software Blade R81 - Build 123 [Expert@MGMT:0]#


The 'fgate' command on Security Gateway

##### Description

Installs and uninstalls the QoS policy on the managed Security Gateways. Shows the status of the QoS Software Blade on the managed Security Gateways. Controls the QoS debug.

For more information, see:

> - <u>R81QoSAdministration Guide</u>

> - <u>sk41585: How to control and debug FloodGate-1 (QoS)</u>

##### Syntax

fgate [-d] ctl -h < _QoS Module_ > {on | off} debug on off fetch -f < _Management Server_ > kill [-t < _Signal Number_ >] < _Name of QoS Process_ > load log on off stat stat [-h] ver [-k] unload


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter, then<br>redirect the output to a file, or use the script<br>command to save the entire CLI session.|
|ctl -h|Shows the expected syntax and the list of the available<br>QoS modules.|
|ctl <_QoS Module_> {on <br>off}||<br>Controls the specified QoS module:<br>n on- Enables the module (default)<br>n off- Disables the module<br>Note- In R81, the only available QoS module is<br>etmreg.|
|debug {on | off}|Controls the debug mode of the QoS user space<br>daemonfgd50(see sk41585<br>):<br>n on- Enables the debug<br>n off- Disables the debug (default)<br>This sends additional debugging information to the<br>fgd50daemon's log file$FGDIR/log/fgd.elg.|
|fetch -f|Fetches and installs the QoS Policy from all the<br>Management Servers configured in the<br>$FWDIR/conf/mastersfile.|
|fetch <_Management_<br>_Server_>|Fetches and installs the QoS Policy from the specified<br>Management Server.<br>Enter the main IP address or the name of the<br>Management Server object as configured in<br>SmartConsole.|


|Parameter||Description|
|---|---|---|
|kill [-t <br>_Number_>] <br>_Process_>|<_Signal_<br> <_Name of QoS_|Sends the specified signal to the specified QoS user<br>space process.<br>Notes:<br>n In R81, the only available QoS user space<br>process isfgd50.<br>n The QoSfgd50daemon, upon its startup,<br>writes the PIDs of the applicable QoS user<br>spaces processes to the<br>$FWDIR/tmp/<_Name of QoS_<br>_Process_>.pidfiles.<br>For example:$FWDIR/tmp/fgd50.pid<br>n If the file$FWDIR/tmp/<_Name of QoS_<br>_Process_>.pidexists, then this command<br>sends the specified Signal Number to the PID<br>in that file.<br>n If you do not specify the signal explicitly, the<br>command sends Signal 15 (SIGTERM).<br>n For the list of available signals and their<br>numbers, run thekill -lcommand. For<br>information about the signals, see the manual<br>pages for the kill<br>and signal<br>.<br>n To restart the QoSfgd50daemon manually,<br>run the"etmstop" on page 1819and then<br>"etmstart" on page 1818commands.|
|load||Installs the local QoS Policy on the Security Gateway.<br>If this command fails, run the"etmstop" on page 1819<br>and then"etmstart" on page 1818commands.|
|log {on ||off | stat}|Controls the state of QoS logging in the Security<br>Gateway kernel:<br>n on- Enables the QoS logging (default)<br>n off- Disables the QoS logging<br>n stat- Shows the current QoS logging status<br>You can disable the QoS logging to save resources<br>without reinstalling the QoS policy.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|stat [-h]|Shows the status of the QoS Software Blade and policy<br>on the Security Gateway.<br>The-hparameter shows the built-in usage for the<br>"stat" parameter.<br>Important- This command is outdated and exists<br>only for backward compatibility with very old<br>versions. Use the ""cpstat" on page 956" command.|
|unload|Uninstalls the QoS Policy from the Security Gateway.|
|ver [-k]|Shows the QoS Software Blade version.<br>If you specify the "-k" parameter, the output also shows<br>the kernel version.|


##### Examples

###### Example 1 - Fetching the QoS policy based on the $FWDIR/conf/masters file

[Expert@MyGW]# fgate fetch -f Fetching QoS Software Blade Policy: Received Policy. Downloading... eth0(inbound), eth0(outbound). Download OK. Done. [Expert@MyGW]#

###### Example 2 - Fetching the QoS policy from the Management Server specified by its IP address

[Expert@MyGW]# fgate fetch 192.168.3.240 Fetching QoS Software Blade Policy: Received Policy. Downloading... eth0(inbound), eth0(outbound). Download OK. Done. [Expert@MyGW]#

###### Example 3 - Viewing the QoS status

[Expert@MyGW]# fgate stat

Product: QoS Software Blade Version: R81 Kernel Build: 456 Policy Name: MyPolicy Install time: Wed Dec 4 19:53:48 2019 Interfaces Num: 1 Interface table ---------------------------------------------------------------|Name|Dir|Limit (Bps)|Avg Rate (Bps)|Conns|Pend pkts|Pend bytes| ---------------------------------------------------------------|eth0|in | 1250000000| 0| 0| 0| 0| |eth0|out| 1250000000| 0| 0| 0| 0| ---------------------------------------------------------------[Expert@MyGW]#

###### Example 4 - Viewing the QoS Software Blade version

[Expert@MyGW:0]# fgate ver

This is Check Point QoS Software Blade R81 - Build 123 [Expert@MyGW:0]# [Expert@MyGW:0]# fgate ver -k This is Check Point QoS Software Blade R81 - Build 123 kernel: R81 - Build 456 [Expert@MyGW:0]#


# IPS Commands

For more information about IPS, see the <u>R81ThreatPrevention Administration Guide.</u>

IPS commands let you configure and show the IPS on the Security Gateway without installing a new policy.

Important - Changes in the IPS configuration made with these commands are not persistent. If you install a policy or restart the Security Gateway, the changes are deleted.


## ips

##### Description

Shows various information about the IPS Software Blade.

Controls the IPS Software Blade.

##### Syntax

ips bypass < _options_ > debug < _options_ > off on refreshcap stat stats < _options_ >


Important:

- In a Cluster, you must configure all the Cluster Members in the same way.

- On Scalable Platforms (Maestro and Chassis), you must run the applicable commands in the Expert mode on the applicable Security Group.

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in usage.|
|bypass <_options_>|Controls the IPS Bypass mode.<br>See"ips bypass" on page 1831.|
|debug <_options_>|Collects the IPS debug.<br>See"ips debug" on page 1833.|
|off|Disables the IPS Software Blade on-the-fly.<br>See"ips off" on page 1834.|
|on|Enables the IPS Software Blade on-the-fly.<br>See"ips on" on page 1835.|
|refreshcap|Refreshes the IPS sample capture repository.<br>See"ips refreshcap" on page 1836.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|stat|Shows the IPS status.<br>See"ips stat" on page 1837.|
|stats <_options_>|Shows statistics for the IPS performance and Pattern Matcher.<br>See"ips stats" on page 1838.|


### ips bypass

##### Description

Controls the IPS Bypass mode:

- When CPU and/or Memory utilization reaches the configured higher threshold, IPS Software Blade disables itself.

- When CPU and/or Memory utilization goes down to the configured lower threshold, IPS Software Blade enables itself.

##### Syntax

ips bypass off on set < _options_ > stat

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No|Shows the applicable built-in usage.|
|Parameters||
|off|Disables the IPS Bypass mode.|
|on|Enables the IPS Bypass mode.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|set<br><_options_>|Configures the utilization thresholds (in per cent), at which to engage<br>(higher threshold) or disengage (lower threshold) the IPS Bypass mode.<br>The available options are:<br>n Configure the lower CPU threshold:|
||ips bypass set cpu low <0-100>|
||n Configure the higher CPU threshold:|
||ips bypass set cpu high <0-100>|
||n Configure the lower Memory threshold:|
||ips bypass set mem low <0-100>|
||n Configure the higher Memory threshold:<br>|
||ips bypass set mem high <0-100>|
||Example:|
||ips bypass set cpu low 80|
|stat|Shows the status of the IPS Bypass Under Load:<br>n IPS bypass mode<br>n CPU thresholds<br>n Memory thresholds|


### ips debug

##### Description

Collects the IPS debug information.


Note - For information about the kernel debug, see the <u>R81Quantum Security Gateway Guide</u> - Chapter Kernel Debug on Security Gateway.

##### Syntax

ips debug [-e < _Filter_ >] -o < _Output File_ >

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-e<br><_Filter_>|Specifies the INSPECT filter to capture packets.<br>For more information, see the explanation for the ""fw monitor" on<br>page 1077" command in sk30583:<br>What<br>is<br>FW<br>Monitor?|
|-o <_Output_<br>_File_>|Specifies the path and the name of the output debug file.|


##### Example

ips debug -o /var/log/IPS_debug.txt


### ips off

##### Description

##### Disables the IPS Software Blade on-the-fly.


Note - To enable, run the ""ips on" on page 1835" command.

##### Syntax

##### ips off

##### Example 1

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips off IPS is disabled

Please note that for the configuration to apply for connections from existing templates, you have to run this command with -n flag which deletes existing templates. Without '-n', it will fully take effect in a few minutes. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips off -n IPS is disabled Deleting templates Clearing table cphwd_tmpl [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### ips on

##### Description

Enables the IPS Software Blade on-the-fly, if it was disabled with the ""ips off" on page 1834" command.

##### Syntax

ips on [-n]

##### Example 1

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips on IPS is enabled

Please note that for the configuration to apply for connections from existing templates, you have to run this command with -n flag which deletes existing templates. Without '-n', it will fully take effect in a few minutes. [Expert@MyGW:0]#

##### Example 2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips on -n IPS is enabled Deleting templates Clearing table cphwd_tmpl [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### ips refreshcap

##### Description

After you install a new policy, the IPS Software Blade captures the first packet for each IPS protection and saves it in the packet capture repository.

This command refreshes the packet capture repository.

The IPS designates the next packet of each IPS protection as the first packet.

The new first packet replaces the previous one in the packet capture repository.

##### Syntax

ips refreshcap

##### Example

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips refreshcap

Refreshed IPS sample capture

- A single new packet capture will be issued upon the next detection of each attack. You can see

- the packet capture attached to the log or in the Packet Capture Repository. [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### ips stat

##### Description

Shows this information:

- IPS Status (Enabled or Disabled)

- IPS Update Version

- Global Detect (On or Off)

- Bypass Under Load (On or Off)

##### Syntax

ips stat

##### Example

[Expert@MyGW:0]# ips stat Active Profiles: My_IPS_Profile IPS Status: Enabled IPS Update Version: 635158746 Global Detect: Off Bypass Under Load: Off [Expert@MyGW:0]#


### ips stats

##### Description

This tool generates a report that includes both IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics.

The report can help administrators and protection writers analyze, which IPS protections or IPS components cause performance issues.

The output files are located in the $FWDIR/ips/statistics_results/ directory.

On a Standalone, the tool creates a directory for each specified IP address.

The output files are:

|File|Description|
|---|---|
|ips.dbg|Contains the raw report, which contains all the<br>information.|
|ips_stat_output_<br>file.csv|Contains the report with the IPS statistics.|
|pm_output_file.csv|Contains the statistics for the Pattern Matcher.|
|tier1_output_file.csv|Contains the statistics for the Pattern Matcher first tier.|
|tier2_output_file.csv|Contains the statistics for the Pattern Matcher second<br>tier.|


##### Syntax

|ips stats|-h|
|---|---|
|ips stats||
|ips stats|<_Seconds_>|
|ips stats|-g <_Seconds_>|
|ips stats|<_IP Address of Gateway_>|
|ips stats|<_IP Address of Gateway_> <_Seconds_>|
|ips stats|<_IP Address of Gateway_> -m|


Important - To generate a report on a VSX Gateway, you must use the Manual Mode.


##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|ips stats -h|Shows the applicable built-in usage.|
|ips stats|Available only in Standalone configurations.<br>Collects the IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics on the<br>Standalone computer during 20 seconds.|
|ips stats<br><_Seconds_>|Available only in Standalone configurations.<br>Collects the IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics on the<br>Standalone computer during the specified number of seconds.|
|ips stats -g<br><_Seconds_>|Manual Mode on the current Security Gateway.<br>Important- You must use this command on a VSX<br>Gateway.<br>Collects the IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics during the<br>specified number of seconds.<br>The output file is/ips_tar.tgz(in the root partition)<br>For analysis, you must copy this file to the root partition on the<br>Management Server.|
|ips stats <_IP_<br>_Address of_<br>_Gateway_>|Collects the IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics for the Security<br>Gateway with the main specified IP address during 20 seconds.|
|ips stats <_IP_<br>_Address of_<br>_Gateway_> <_Seconds_>|Collects the IPS and Pattern Matcher statistics for the Security<br>Gateway with the main specified IP address during the specified<br>number of seconds.|
|ips stats <_IP_<br>_Address of_<br>_Gateway_> -m|Available only on the Management Server.<br>Runs an analysis on the output file/ips_tar.tgzthat you<br>collected from the Security Gateway with the main specified IP<br>address.|


##### Related SK article

<u>sk43733: How to measure CPU time consumed by IPS protections.</u>

##### Example 1 - Collect the statistics on the Security Gateway with IP address 192.168.20.14 during 40 seconds

ips stats 192.168.20.14 40


Example 2- Collect the statistics on the current Security Gateway during 30 seconds

ips stats -g 30

Example - Analyze the statistics you collected from the Security Gateway with IP address 192.168.20.14

ips stats 192.168.20.14 -m


# Monitoring Commands

For more information, see the <u>R81Logging andMonitoring Administration Guide.</u>

This section contains commands for the Monitoring Software Blade (former SmartView Monitor) on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.


## rtm

##### Description

Controls the Monitoring Software Blade (former SmartView Monitor) on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.

Shows the information about the Monitoring Software Blade.

##### Syntax

rtm debug < _options_ > drv < _options_ > monitor < _options_ > rtmd stat < _options_ > ver < _options_ >

Note - "RTM" stands for Real Time Monitoring.

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in usage.|
|"rtm debug" on<br>page 1843|Collects the SmartView Monitor debug information.|
|"rtm drv" on page 1844|Starts, stops, or shows the status of the SmartView Monitor<br>kernel driver.|
|"rtm rtmd" on page 1845|Starts the SmartView Monitor daemon manually.|
|"rtm monitor" on<br>page 1846|Starts the monitoring process for an interface or a virtual link.|
|"rtm stat" on page 1852|Shows information about the SmartView Monitor.|
|"rtm ver" on page 1855|Shows the SmartView Monitor version.|


### rtm debug

##### Description

Collects the SmartView Monitor debug information in the $FWDIR/log/rtmd.elg file on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.

##### Syntax

rtm debug {on | off} [OPSEC_DEBUG_LEVEL | TDERROR_< _AppName_ >_ < _Topic_ >=< _ErrLevel_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|on|Start debug mode|
|off|Stop debug mode|
|OPSEC_DEBUG_LEVEL|Turn on OPSEC debug printouts|
|TDERROR_RTM_ALL|Turn on SmartView Monitor debug printouts|


##### Example

rtm debug on TDERROR_RTM_ALL=5


### rtm drv

##### Description

Starts, stops, or shows the status of the SmartView Monitor kernel driver on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.


Important - Do not run this command manually. Run the "rtmstart" on page 1856 and "rtmstop" on page 1857 commands.

##### Syntax

rtm drv off on stat

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|on|Starts the SmartView Monitor kernel driver|
|off|Stops the SmartView Monitor kernel driver|
|stat|Shows the SmartView Monitor kernel driver status|


### rtm rtmd

##### Description

Starts the SmartView Monitor daemon manually on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.

This also occurs manually when you run the "rtmstart" on page 1856 command.

##### Syntax

rtm [-d] rtmd

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-d|Runs the command in debug mode.<br>Use only if you troubleshoot the command itself.<br>Best Practice- If you use this parameter,<br>then redirect the output to a file, or use the<br>script<br>command to save the entire CLI<br>session.|


### rtm monitor

##### Description

Starts the monitoring process for an interface or a Virtual Link on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member.

If options and grouping are not used, this command monitors all traffic, on all interfaces, in both directions.

##### Syntax

rtm monitor vl < _Virtual_Link_Name_ > [-t {wire | application}] [-h < _Module_ >]

rtm monitor < _Key_1_ > [< _Key_2_ > [< _Key_3_ >] [< _Key_4_ >]] < _Value_Column_1_ > [< _Value_Column_2_ > [< _Value_Column_3_ >] [< _Value_Column_4_ >] [< _Value_ Column_5_ >] [< _Value_Column_6_ >]] [< _Filter_ >] [< _Options_ >]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|No Parameters|Shows the built-in usage and examples.|
|<_Virtual_Link_Name_>|Specifies the name of the monitored Virtual Link.|
|-t {wire |<br>application}|Specifies how to show the data:<br>n wire- Shows the data on the wire after compression, or<br>encryption.<br>n application- Shows the data as the application sees<br>it (not compressed and not encrypted).|
|-h <_Module_>|Specifies the Security Gateway by its IP address, or<br>resolvable hostname.|
|<_Key_1_> [... [<_Key__<br>_4_>]]|Specifies up to four keys in this format:<br>-k <_Key_Type_> [<_Key_Atrr_>] [<_Entity_1_> ...<br><_Entity_N_>]|


|Parameter<br>Description|
|---|
|The<_Key_Type_>can be one of these:<br>n connId- Monitors according to a connection ID.<br>n dst- Monitors according to a network object<br>(destination only).<br>n fgrule- Monitors according to a QoS Policy rule.<br>n fwrule- Monitors according to an Access Control<br>Policy rule.<br>n interface- Monitors according to an interface.<br>Use comma "," to specify the direction for the<br>interfacefilter:<br>,{in|out|both}<br>Default isboth.<br>n ip- Monitors according to a network object (source and<br>destination).<br>n orientation- Monitors according to connection's<br>direction.<br>n pktRange- Monitors according to a range of packet<br>sizes.<br>n src- Monitors according to a network object (source<br>only).<br>n svc- Monitors according to a service (for example,<br>http).<br>n tunnel- Monitors according to a VPN tunnel.<br>n tunnelType- Monitors according to a VPN tunnel type:<br>l 0- reserved<br>l 1- regular<br>l 2- permanent<br>n url [<_URL_Mode_>]- Monitors according to a URL.<br>The<_URL_Mode_>can be one of these:<br>l url_mod=full(default)<br>l url_mod=host<br>l url_mod=host_path<br>l url_mod=path<br>l url_mod=scheme<br>l url_mod=scheme_host<br>n wdAttack- Monitors according to web defense attacks.|
|<_Value_Column_1_><br>[... [<_Value__<br>Specifies up to six column values in this format:<br>-v <_Value Type_> [<_Accumulate Mode_>] [<_Sort_|
|_Column_6_>]]<br>_Mode_>] [<_Direction Filter_>] [<_Encryption_<br>_Filter_>]|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
||n The<_Value Type_>can be one of these:<br>l ab- Shows application bytes<br>l conn- Shows connections<br>l pkt- Shows packets<br>l session- Shows sessions<br>l wb- Shows wire-bytes|
||n The<_Accumulate Mode_>can be one of these:<br>l If<_Value Type_>=ab:<br>o acc=lineUtil<br>o acc=rate(default)<br>o acc=sum<br>l If<_Value Type_>=conn:<br>o acc=concurrent(default)<br>o acc=new<br>l If<_Value Type_>=pkt:<br>o acc=rate(default)<br>o acc=sum<br>l If<_Value Type_>=session:<br>o acc=new<br>l If<_Value Type_>=wb:<br>o acc=lineUtil<br>o acc=rate(default)<br>o acc=sum|
||n The<_Sort Mode_>can be one of these:<br>l sort=top(default for all views)<br>l sort=bottom<br>l sort=none(default for specific views)|
||n The<_Direction Filter_>can be one of these:<br>l dir=in<br>l dir=out<br>l dir=both(default)|
||n The<_Encryption Filter_>can be one of these:<br>l enc=yes<br>l enc=no<br>l enc=both(default)|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_Filter_>|Specifies the filter that can be one of these:<br>n For the atom filter:<br>-f <_Filter_Type_> [not] [<_Entity_1_> ...<br><_Entity_N_>]<br>n For the hierarchy filter:<br>-f {and | or} [...]|
||The<_Filter_Type_>can be one of these:<br>n connId- Monitors according to a connection ID.<br>n dst- Monitors according to a network object<br>(destination only).<br>n fgrule- Monitors according to a QoS Policy rule.<br>n fwrule- Monitors according to an Access Control<br>Policy rule.<br>n interface- Monitors according to an interface.<br>Use comma ","to specify the direction for the<br>interfacefilter:<br>,{in|out|both}<br>Default isboth.<br>n ip- Monitors according to a network object (source and<br>destination).<br>n orientation- Monitors according to connection's<br>direction.<br>n src- Monitors according to a network object (source<br>only).<br>n svc- Monitors according to a service (for example,<br>http).<br>n tunnel- Monitors according to a VPN tunnel.<br>n tunnelType- Monitors according to a VPN tunnel type:<br>l 0- reserved<br>l 1- regular<br>l 2- permanent<br>n url [<_URL_Mode_>]- Monitors according to a URL.<br>The<_URL_Mode_>can be one of these:<br>l url_mod=full(default)<br>l url_mod=host<br>l url_mod=host_path<br>l url_mod=path<br>l url_mod=scheme|
||l url_mod=scheme_host|
||n wdAttack- Monitors according to web defense attacks.|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|<_Options_>|Specifies these options:|
||n -e <_Export File Name_><br>Specifies the path and the name of the file, in which the<br>command saves its output.<br>n -h <_Module_><br>Specifies the Security Gateway by its IP address, or<br>resolvable hostname.<br>Default islocalhost.<br>n -i <_Interval in Seconds_><br>The command runs in the loop and shows the output<br>every specified number of seconds.<br>Default is 2 sec.|
||n -m {raw | resolve | both}<br>Specifies how to resolve the names.<br>Default isboth.|
||n -s {top | bottom | none} [index=<1...6>]<br>[updates=<1...200>]|
||Specifies how to sort the output.<br>If you specifynone, the defaults are:<br>index=1andupdates=50.|


##### Notes

> - Use the tilde character "~~" to specify a subrule (rule~~subrule).

To monitor for the QoS Policy, use: rule~~fgrule

> - The specified entities correspond to the specified grouping option.

For example, if the monitoring process works according to a service (svc), add all the monitored services, separated by a space.

##### Examples

Example 1

This command shows top services (based on bytes per seconds) on external interfaces in the inbound direction:

rtm monitor -f interface external,in -k svc -v wb


###### Example 2

This command shows top Access Control rules (based on average concurrent connections):

rtm monitor -k fwrule -v conn acc=concurrent

###### Example 3

This command shows Individual HTTP connections (bytes per second):

rtm monitor -f svc http -k svc -k connId -v wb

###### Example 4

This command shows bottom inbound IP addresses versus outbound IP addresses (based on packets per interval):

rtm monitor -k ip -v pkt dir=in acc=sum -v pkt dir=out acc=sum - v pkt acc=sum sort=bottom -i 10

###### Example 5

This command shows top tunnels (based on average concurrent connections):

rtm monitor -f tunnelType not 0 -k tunnel -k tunnelType -v conn -m resolve

###### Example 6

This command shows packet size distribution (based on packets per interval):

rtm monitor -k pktRange 0-99 100-499 500-999 1000-1999 ">2000" - v pkt acc=sum -i 1

###### Example 7

This command shows top URLs (based on sessions per seconds) - host part only:

rtm monitor -k url url_mod=host -v session


### rtm stat

##### Description

Show this information on the Security Gateway / each Cluster Member:

- The status of the Monitoring Software Blade

- The status of the SmartView Monitor daemon

- The status of the SmartView Monitor driver

- Number of opened Virtual Links

- Number of opened Views

- Some performance counters

##### Syntax

rtm stat -h rtm stat [vl | view] [perf [{on | off | reset}] [-i < _Interval_ >] [- r < _View_ID_ >] [-v[v][v]]

##### Parameters

|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-h|Shows the built-in usage.|
|vl|Shows current Virtual Links|
|view|Shows current Views|
|perf [{off | on |<br>reset}]|Controls whether to show performance information:<br>n off- Disables the feature<br>n on- Enables the feature<br>n reset- Resets the counters|
||The output shows these performance counters:|
||n New Connections<br>n Packets|
||n Inf Reclassify|
||n View Reclassify|
||n End Connections|
||n Packets / connections ratio|


|Parameter|Description|
|---|---|
|-i <_Interval_>|The command runs in the loop and shows the output every<br>specified number of seconds.|
|-r <_View_ID_>|Specifies the View ID to show.|
|-v[v][v]|Verbose output:|
||n -v- Verbose output|
||n -vv- More verbose output|
||n -vvv- Most verbose output|


##### Examples

Example 1

[Expert@MyGW:0]# rtm stat ------------------------------------------------------SmartView Monitor Status: Sun Mar 20 18:25:51 2022 ------------------------------------------------------Product is Enabled Daemon is ON ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance 0 ------------------------------------------------------Driver is ON Open Virtual-Links: 0 Open Views: 0 ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance 1 ------------------------------------------------------Driver is ON Open Virtual-Links: 0 Open Views: 0 ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance ... ------------------------------------------------------... _(truncated for brevity)_ ... [Expert@MyGW:0]#


###### Example 2

[Expert@MyGW:0]# rtm stat view -vvv ------------------------------------------------------SmartView Monitor Status: Sun Mar 20 18:25:51 2022 ------------------------------------------------------Product is Enabled Daemon is ON ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance 0 ------------------------------------------------------Driver is ON Open Virtual-Links: 0 Open Views: 0 ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance 1 ------------------------------------------------------Driver is ON Open Virtual-Links: 0 Open Views: 0 ------------------------------------------------------Status for kernel instance ... ------------------------------------------------------... _(truncated for brevity)_ ... -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------VIEW 1: svc | wb(rate) interval: 2 Seconds 60016,60016 | 5148 11008a,11008a | 229 Aggregate | 5377 Number of Entries(2) Keys(-k svc acc=replace ) Values(-v wb acc=rate ) Sort(-s top ) Filter(-) Daemon id:5 kernel id:0 timeUntilUpdate: 1 [Sec] -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[Expert@MyGW:0]#
